Malformed stdin symptom: empty, oversize, non-UTF8, duplicate-key, non-finite constant, or wrong-shape JSON prints bad_shape: <detail> to stderr with exit 1 and no proposal output.

No threads or retries here; bounded subprocess call takes timeout_s (default 10s) and cwd at verified checkout. Nonzero exit becomes bad_shape external planner exited nonzero; no partial proposal is returned.
Stdin capped at 1048576 bytes; larger input fails before parsing. Output uses canonical_json with sorted keys, compact separators, no floats, rejecting non-canonical values and surrogate code points.
Defaults: tick window 5, proposal id holdings-proposal-1, max_ms 5000. Overrides require tick_window positive int, max_ms 1-3600000, max_retries 0-10, proposal_id 1-128 clean chars.

Depends on executor.AdmittedExecutor.check_target for target admission, tools._check_action/_check_expectation/_check_proposal for shape, observe.validate_observation for frame truth, wender_bridge for command resolution and lock verification.
String hazard: NUL or lone surrogates fail bad_shape; floats and non-finite JSON constants rejected. Strict type() checks mean booleans never pass as ints for tick_window, coordinates, or budgets.
tools.py implements closed mvctl verbs over an injected bounded ToolClient: each verb builds one mv_tool_call/v0.2, sends it, validates the mv_tool_result/v0.2 reply, and never opens sockets itself.

observe(surface_id) sends op observe, validates observation shape plus surface correlation, optionally runs perception_adapter.perceive(frame) then revalidates, and returns a deep copy. Refusals and errors raise typed exceptions.
list_surfaces(cursor,limit) sends op list for exactly one page, validates each surface and next_cursor, and returns the page copy. Pagination stays with the caller; one call never drains more pages.

propose(proposal) locally validates action_proposal/v0.2 then sends op propose; on admitted returns the verdict copy after proposal_id correlation. Admission is not completion; refusals raise ToolRefusal with no retry.

wait_verify(proposal_id,expectation) shape-checks expectation locally (never transmitted), then polls op wait_verify until verified, timeout, refused, or error. Pending repeats only the wait within one monotonic budget; action is never resubmitted.

record_start(mode ram|disk) and record_stop(mode ram|disk) send record_request/v0.2 frames and validate record_event/v0.2 outcomes; record_stop drains frame_captured/dropped (ram) or exported (disk) until stopped.

Every call mints a random 16-byte hex request_id, sends {schema,request_id,op,args}, then requires reply schema mv_tool_result/v0.2 with matching request_id and op; mismatch fails as uncorrelated request_id/op.

Wait states: verified returns _VerifiedReceipt carrying validated receipt plus focus_verified/input_mono_ns/frame_sha256; timeout raises VerificationFailed; pending sleeps min(retry_after_ms,remaining) and loops; budget exhaustion raises TimeoutError.

Closed-shape invariant: proposals, frames, receipts, record frames use exact or closed key sets; unknown proposal/record versions with the right family prefix fail distinctly from fully invalid shapes.

Type invariant: type(value) is int is exact so booleans never count as integers; numbers must be finite; boolean constants require identity. Click/scroll/wait bounds and tick windows are range-checked.

Action contract: click needs int x,y plus button in {left,middle,right}; key needs 1-4096 names; type needs 1-65536 chars; scroll needs int dx,dy; wait ms 1-3600000; lane_submit needs verb/payload{nonce,seq,command,args}.

Expectation contract: changed_region bbox ints with w,h 1-16384; element_state role/name/state strings; state_sha256_change before hex digest plus non-inverted min/max_tick; text_present non-empty text.

Receipt contract: schema action_receipt/v0.2, verified True, empty error string, method in {pixel,element,state_sha256}; native_evidence when present must correlate surface_id, input_mono_ns, and focus_verified True.

Local shape/version/correlation failure raises ToolValidationError and nothing was admitted; message is like invalid proposal or uncorrelated surface_id. Transport failures including TimeoutError propagate unchanged.

Core refused status requires reason in {STALE_FRAME,SURFACE_NOT_AGENT_CONTROLLED,LOCKED_BY_OTHER,BUDGET_EXCEEDED,OUT_OF_BOUNDS,POLICY}; raises ToolRefusal(reason,None) because the frozen refused branch carries no core_seq.

Core error status requires code in {PROTOCOL,UNAVAILABLE,NOT_FOUND,VERIFICATION_FAILED}; VERIFICATION_FAILED raises VerificationFailed with payload copy, others raise ToolOperationalError(code,detail,result).

Tester-visible symptom: call raises ToolValidationError uncorrelated proposal_id/surface_id/request_id, or ToolRefusal with codes above, or VerificationFailed holding the receipt body; no retry happens automatically.

Recording symptom: ram request with disk fields fails ram recording forbids disk destination; disk request missing destination fails closed before transport; malformed stream event aborts with ToolValidationError; overlong stream fails record event stream exceeded cap.

wait_verify uses one monotonic deadline: remaining_ms recomputed from deadline minus clock reading each loop, custom clocks need callable sleep or no sleep; hostile retry_after_ms is clamped to remaining budget so it cannot stall past deadline.

record_stop consumes at most 256 stream events per call, each with its own fresh request_id, against a wall budget up to 60000 ms; leftover budget under 1 ms raises TimeoutError record_stop budget exhausted.
Caps: safe ints to 9007199254740991, ring/file bytes to 1073741824, fps to 120, vision summary to 4096 chars, list limit to 256, wait timeout to 60000 ms; out-of-range values fail locally.

Enumerations: record modes {ram,disk,screenshot}; verification {pixel,element,state_sha256}; surface kinds/states/visibility/control fixed sets; ram paths must match /dev/shm with 1-8 segments; disk paths must be absolute.
Depends on observe.validate_observation for observation v0.2 correlation with surface_id and generation; frame ramws_path and sha256 patterns enforced here before delegating deeper checks.

Identifier hazard: ids must match [A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:-]* and fit 128 chars; cursor, surface, proposal, recording, capability ids all share this gate, so empty or slash-containing ids fail before transport.

verify.py is the bounded agent workflow: observe, plan once via Wender or local planner, submit once, await the core receipt. Success is exclusively the core verified receipt; typed exceptions are terminal with no retries.

vision.py is the strict perception boundary: it validates a supervised transport (exit_code,stdout) reply as ve.cu_describe/v1 evidence and projects integer-only observation geometry without inventing element state.

run_loop(client,surface_id,proposal_id,timeout_ms,...) enforces timeout 1-60000 ms, computes one monotonic deadline, observes, selects planner branch, builds proposal, proposes, then wait_verify with remaining budget. Any nonpositive remainder raises TimeoutError.

build_proposal(frame,...) validates the frame via tools._check_frame, assembles action_proposal/v0.2 with based_on_frame sha256/generation and budget, validates via tools._check_proposal, and returns it.

describe(frame,transport) validates frame, calls transport(frame copy), requires (int,str) pair with rc 0, parses and frame-binds it. describe_observation wraps changed_regions as integer bboxes into observation/v0.2 with empty summary.

Planner selection: provider wender, or MV_WENDER_PLANNER_CMD set, or (provider None and planner None or configured wender root) uses WenderSubprocessAdapter with locked checkout and project_element_table; else calls local planner(observation) requiring an (action,expectation) pair.

Description flow: JSON parsed with duplicate-key rejection, schema ve.cu_describe/v1 and 64-hex digest checked, changed_regions/crops/marks capped at 16/8/24 with descending scores converted to integer score_ppm, companions and crop paths validated.

Loop states: observe must return matching surface_id else uncorrelated surface_id; propose once; wait_verify receipt must correlate proposal_id and after_frame surface_id, optionally fully receipt-checked; ends with final remaining() budget check before returning receipt.

Frame-binding invariant: returned frame_sha256/width/height must equal input frame sha256/width/height else frame binding mismatch. RAM paths must be absolute canonical /dev/shm/vqa-cu spellings with no .. or unresolved symlinks.
Shape invariant: rows use exact closed key sets; duplicate JSON keys rejected; boxes require integer x,y,w,h with w,h at least 1 and x+w/y+h inside frame, else rectangle outside frame.

Marks contract: id must equal 1-based index, kind in {button,tab,field,row,icon,text,unknown}; marks and marks_png must appear together, as must crop_dir and crop_pngs; crop_pngs length must equal crops length; OCR quartet must be complete when any present.

Every vision validation failure raises VisionBridgeError (a ValueError) with messages like invalid schema or digest, description cap exceeded, noncanonical RAM path, or invalid OCR fields; nonzero transport rc becomes description refused.

Loop failures: invalid timeout raises ValueError; bad provider or missing local planner or malformed local plan raises ObservationError bad_shape/unavailable; receipt correlation failures raise uncorrelated surface_id/proposal_id via tools._fail.
Perception symptom: caller sees ValueError description refused when helper exits nonzero or returns wrong tuple, or frame binding mismatch when helper describes a different frame than requested.

Workflow symptom: caller gets TimeoutError loop deadline exceeded or wait_verify budget exhausted when the 1-60 s budget lapses; no action is replayed, and the verified receipt is the only success signal.

No threads or retries: run_loop threads one deadline through observe, bridge plan_step, propose, and wait_verify via remaining(); vision never guesses paths or launches unmanaged children, delegating execution to the injected transport.
Caps: stdout over 1 MiB rejected; integers bounded by 9007199254740991; OCR strings capped at 64 UTF-8 bytes; mark_cap_reached flag set when 24 marks present, recording truncation without error.

Lazy imports avoid cycles: wender_bridge inside run_loop for command/backend/root checks, perception.deps_lock for pinned checkout, perception.vcore.project_element_table for planner input. tools.observe/propose/wait_verify perform transport.

Path and numeric hazards: spelling checked before resolution so traversal hides nothing; resolved path must equal input; scores must be finite 0-1 and strictly descending, else invalid score or scores not descending.

Run Wender planner as isolated pipe-only subprocess. Sends {observation,element_table,goal} UTF-8 JSON to stdin of (sys.executable,-m,wender.plan.cli) and reads {action,expectation,state,target_node}. Admits only custody-checked clicks; never dispatches or grants admission.
Hold optional muse_cli/muse_spark/baseten model backend hook with runtime-only credential buffer. Credentials stay in bytearray/memoryview, never logged, serialized, or placed in subprocess env.

plan_step(observation,element_table,goal) is main entry. Validates observation frame_ref, element_table schema vqa.element-table/v1 and frame match, goal string, then spawns planner, validates response, custody checks target, returns action,expectation,state,target.

resolve_planner_command(command,configured_env,use_env) resolves planner argv. Explicit command wins, else MV_WENDER_PLANNER_CMD JSON argv via verify.get_configured_planner_cmd, else DEFAULT_WENDER_PLANNER_CMD.
invoke(request) calls configured transport(request,provider,endpoint,credential). Rejects non-canonical JSON, requires dict request/response, requires in-memory credential for baseten kind.

Request JSON is canonical sort_keys,separators,ensure_ascii False,allow_nan False, UTF-8 encoded, fed to child stdin. Stdout must be unique-key UTF-8 JSON with keys action,expectation,state,target_node. Stderr is drained but discarded; only stdout parsed.
Child env is minimal: only PATH and LANG inherited plus PYTHONPATH=wender_root and PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1. No parent credentials inherited. cwd is resolved wender_root.

State must be wender.state/v1 with keys schema,source,prune,ax_sha256,ax_stable_sha256,viewport,nodes,actionable,counts. Digests are 64-hex, node ids 16-hex unique, parents earlier in list, actionable list must equal actionable-flagged nodes in order.

Response must contain exactly action,expectation,state,target_node. Action must pass _check_action/_check_expectation and be type click. Click x,y must lie inside target box, target actionable true and listed in state actionable, else SurfaceError alignment.

counts.nodes equals node count, counts.actionable equals actionable length, counts.raw >= nodes. Viewport w,h ints >=0 or None. Boxes None or [x,y,w,h] ints with w,h>=1. Source kind in cdp/atspi/godot/vision.
battery_state_sha256 cleared to None at start of every plan_step and set only after state validation, action/expectation checks, AdmittedExecutor.check_target and box containment all succeed.
Adapter has no planner session state; each plan_step is one attempt: clear digest -> validate inputs -> spawn -> validate response -> custody check -> publish digest. Failure leaves digest None.
timeout must be int/float type, finite, >0 and <=86400.0. Default 10s in adapter init. Enforced across pipe I/O and process wait via monotonic deadline.

Single-threaded selector loop over nonblocking stdin/stdout/stderr. Writes request in 4KB chunks, reads up to 64KB per read. Deadline checked before select and wait; TimeoutExpired kills process via finally kill+wait.
Byte ceilings: stdout 1048576, stderr 65536. Exceeding raises ObservationError bad_shape planner output exceeds maximum size. Stderr bytes dropped on success; only stdout returned.

On TimeoutExpired raises ObservationError timeout Wender planner timed out. On OSError raises unavailable Wender planner launch failed. Nonzero exit raises subprocess_failed Wender planner exited unsuccessfully.
Any shape violation raises ObservationError bad_shape via _require, e.g. state keys invalid, node id invalid, counts disagree, element bbox invalid, only custody-bound clicks supported.
String/Path env credential, empty or NUL-containing buffer, unknown provider, or unsupported model_backend dict keys raise bad_shape. Missing required credential raises unavailable.

User sees no click happening and planner step fails. Causes: bad wender_root, lock mismatch, frame/element mismatch, planner timeout or crash, non-click plan, or click outside custody-checked target box.

Credential must be bytes/bytearray, zeroed on clear_credential. redact/to_metadata and repr/str expose only <redacted>/None. invoke passes readonly memoryview to transport; no disk, env, log, or repr leak allowed.
Own deterministic admission state machine for surfaces, leases, pending proposals, budget, nonces/sequences. Pure reduce/apply; persistence only after journal fsync by Authority.

Durable serializer around CoreState plus journal. Success follows dependency publication and journal fsync, never merely a state plan. Exposes retain witnesses, flush_sync, admit, apply_with_witnesses.

decode(raw,peer,session,epoch,received_ns) is closed entry for proposals. Decodes envelope, maps OutOfBounds, rejects unless from==peer, session matches, to Core, body ActionProposal. Stores raw for replay re-decode.

admit(request,witnesses) applies Propose with witnesses and returns action_verdict/v0.2 admitted/refused with proposal_id, reason_code, core_seq. apply/apply_with_witnesses journal every Input before swapping state.

apply clones state, runs reduce(input) to Outcome{core_seq,reason,dispatch,cancelled,cancellation_reason,control_ready}, then commits. core_seq increments once per input via checked_add; overflow returns Overflow.

Surface lifecycle: Created inserts fresh id with no frame; Updated mutates display/live/agent_controlled with refresh fence; Lost sets live false; Destroyed sets live false and adds to destroyed tombstone set. Lost/Destroyed are terminal.

Losing liveness or agent control cancels all pending for that surface. Dispatched/unknown move to draining map; undispatched removed with lease cleanup. Returns cancelled ids with SurfaceNotAgentControlled reason.

Admission requires live agent_controlled surface, owner equals proposer, epoch matches nonzero, frame present and generation/sha match proposal, no refresh fence, lease/display conflict free, budget and deadline valid, Agent component.

Destroyed ids stay in destroyed set; Lifecycle/Frame/TakeControl/ReleaseControl on destroyed returns Policy. Metadata Updated cannot resurrect non-live; live only ORs true, agent_controlled only ANDs. Human-owned creation pins human_roles immutably.

Input is tagged journaled ABI: SurfaceRequest, SurfaceNotice, Lifecycle, Refuse, Connect, Surface, Frame, Propose, Dispatch, DispatchFailed, Receipt, TakeControl, ReleaseControl, Drain, HumanInput. Unknown fields denied.

Frame needs 64 lowercase-hex sha256, generation/width/height nonzero. Surface needs non-empty display, owner Endpoint, agent_controlled/live flags, optional frame and refresh_after fence, allowed_verbs list.
proposal() extracts ActionProposal from envelope body; non-proposal returns InvalidInput. Propose path re-decodes raw and requires envelope equality, catching deserialization-built request tampering.

Scroll dx/dy outside i32 returns OutOfBounds before reservation and at dispatch. Click outside frame, wait/scroll unsupported types, bad bbox, min_tick>max_tick, bad lane verb/nonce/seq, over-budget ms all map to OutOfBounds/Policy/BudgetExceeded as coded.

Duplicate proposal_id, msg_id, nonce, or seq<=stored returns Policy without budget charge. HumanInput on human_roles surface, destroyed, epoch 0, or existing pending/draining returns Policy. Unknown proposal Dispatch/Receipt/Drain returns Policy.

SurfaceRequest op must be create/destroy/list/frame_subscribe/frame_unsubscribe with catalog-valid create policy; targeting destroyed or non-live id returns Policy. Zero budget returns BudgetExceeded, else decrements budget.

Callers serialize Authority access. Each proposal dispatched at most once below retry ceiling; Dispatch sets dispatched true and dispatch flag. Failed recheck removes pending so retry needs new frame-bound admission.

Connect increments epoch and marks all pending unknown, forcing re-admission. DispatchFailed/Receipt/Drain require epoch match; unknown or undispatched receipts are Policy and never refund admitted-attempt budget.

Budget counts admitted attempts via remaining_budget, default 10000. Propose and HumanInput decrement on success; unknown dispatched work never refunded; DispatchFailed releases unqueued work without refund.

Deadline is received_ns plus budget.max_ms*1e6 with overflow check. Expired (now>=deadline) or now<received_ns yields BudgetExceeded. Lane key is JSON of (from,surface_id) for wait-lane nonce/sequence dedup.
Depends on journal canonical_bytes, Journal create/recover/append, Witness retain/verified/frame, wire decode_envelope/payload, catalog CreateRequest for create policy validation.

Start metaviewer-core daemon: read JSON Config from MV_CORE_CONFIG file, pin component_version to CARGO_PKG_VERSION, validate uid, bind XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/metaviewer/core.sock, open state dir server, serve with shared Mutex.
Offline journal replay tool. Scans journal with witness root, optionally with anchor file, prints sha256 of state snapshot unless --verify-only. Maps journal errors to exit codes 2/3/4.
Decode one catalog entry line into validated CatalogEntry. Runs preflight bounds checks then serde shape check then TryFrom policy. Input excludes framing LF but budget reserves it.
Bind a validated CatalogEntry to a LaunchTarget and derive launch_spec binary+args plus inner_argv, and build surface_request/v0.2 create payload for admission.
main builds current-thread tokio runtime, blocks on run, prints metaviewer-core: error to stderr and exits 2 on any failure. No args; all config via env files.
main calls run, prints error to stderr, exits 3 on Duplicate, 4 on Witness, 2 otherwise. Args are --journal, --witness-root, optional --anchor, --verify-only; any other shape is Invalid.

new(entry,target) gates kind-target pairs: Browser->Browser, Program notepad/metaviewer-nested, Vm notepad-vm, Game absolute app_dir slots 1-4 with 1280x900x1280x900, Desktop valid class slot>0. Else InvalidTarget.

preflight scans raw bytes without allocation: depth max 32, string values max 65536 decoded length, max 256 unique keys per object with duplicate detection, array commas max 4096. Oversize beyond MAX_ENVELOPE_BYTES rejected first.

launch_spec maps Browser/Program/Vm to srf-identity-surface start --kind --identity --windows 1 [--program], Game to srf-holdings-capsule start --slots --app, Desktop to srf-capsula-desktop iniciar --clase --slot --json. Nested entry adds fixed inner_argv.

Wire row needs schema plus entry_id,kind,profile_id,label,image,window/display sizes,display_only,network,seccomp_identity,nested_depth,limits{memory_bytes,cpu_milli}. Unknown fields denied; serde checks shape after preflight.
Program kind always emits CreateNested desktop_capsule with geometry w/h and profile_id,nested_depth; other kinds emit Case0 Browser/DesktopCapsule/GameCapsule/Vm with geometry and profile_id.
Refuses foreign registration before sockets/session: config.core.hello.component_version must equal compiled CARGO_PKG_VERSION, else error core component version pin mismatch.
Requires MV_CORE_CONFIG path to JSON config file and XDG_RUNTIME_DIR for socket dir. Uses serve::effective_uid, config.validate(uid), serve::bind, serve::state_dir for state.
Missing --journal/--witness-root, duplicated flags, unknown arg, or scan failure returns JournalError Invalid/Corrupt etc. verify-only suppresses snapshot hash print but still validates.

Oversized maps to Oversized, depth>32 DepthExceeded, long string StringLimitExceeded, duplicate key DuplicateField, >256 keys KeyLimitExceeded, >=4096 array items ArrayLimitExceeded, bad syntax Malformed.
User sees daemon exit 2 with metaviewer-core: message on stderr and no socket. Causes: missing env, unreadable config, version pin mismatch, uid validation failure, bind failure.
Operator sees catalog registration rejected as InvalidTarget when pairing wrong binary/program, non-absolute game path, out-of-range slots, or mismatched nested geometry.
Hard caps prevent allocation blowup: envelope bytes, 32 nesting, 64KB strings, 256 keys/object, 4096 array elements. Checked before typed allocation.
Decode/launch depend on crate::wire MAX_ENVELOPE_BYTES/DecodeError and wire payload SurfaceRequest types. Binaries depend on metaviewer_core serve/journal modules and tokio runtime.
Pure frozen catalog authority with no processes or filesystem. Stores entries by entry_id, (kind,profile) index, and surface states. Terminal surface ids stay reserved forever.
new(entries) builds registry, rejecting DuplicateEntry on repeated entry_id and DuplicateProfile on repeated (kind,profile_id). Projections returns cloned entries; state queries Live/Destroyed/Lost.
create(request) validates then emits LaunchSpec and marks surface Live. destroy/mark_lost move Live to Destroyed/Lost via finish; non-Live finish returns SurfaceNotLive.

from_surface_request converts admitted Case0 DTO with explicit nested_depth 0 only; from_nested_surface_request converts CreateNested DTO with i64 depth. Both check geometry range, identity, kind mapping.
validate_create checks valid surface id, unused id, Kind::parse, depth<=1, profile lookup UnregisteredProfile, stored depth equality, exact window geometry match. Returns Registration on success.

Entry requires schema catalog_entry/v0.2, valid ids/text, memory 1..1073741824, cpu 1..20000, sizes 1..16384 with window<=display, depth<=1. Nested/metaviewer-nested rows must match exact pinned image, geometry 1280x720x1280x900, display_only, None network, seccomp.

Kind parses browser/program/vm/game_capsule/desktop_capsule only, else UnknownKind. Network is none/proxy. CatalogError maps to POLICY SurfaceEvent via surface_event with code POLICY and debug detail.

Nested create requires DesktopCapsule kind else NestedPolicy, depth 0-1 else NestedDepth, geometry 1..16384, valid identity, and depth1 must be exactly 1280x720 else NestedPolicy. Kind fixed to program.

valid_id 1-128 chars, alnum start, alnum/._:- rest. valid_identity 2-48 lowercase alnum start, lowercase/digit/- rest. valid_text <=256 non-blank after trim. Browser/Program/Vm profiles must also satisfy valid_identity.
Surface states Live->Destroyed or Live->Lost only. Once terminal, id remains in map so validate_create returns SurfaceIdUsed and finish returns SurfaceNotLive; no reuse or resurrection.
Bad id returns InvalidSurfaceId, reused id SurfaceIdUsed, unknown kind UnknownKind, depth>1 NestedDepth, depth mismatch NestedDepth, unknown profile UnregisteredProfile, size mismatch Geometry.
Schema/id/label/image/limits failures return InvalidEntry, bad profile InvalidProfile, oversized depth NestedDepth, nested mismatch NestedPolicy, bad geometry Geometry.

User sees surface create silently replaced by POLICY surface event naming the CatalogError debug. Causes: duplicate entry/profile at startup, unregistered profile, wrong geometry, reused surface id, destroyed surface retry.
No runtime resource allocation; limits field only validated. Registry is in-memory BTreeMaps; create reserves surface id entry without spawning anything—launch is caller's job from LaunchSpec.
Depends on decode::decode_entry/CatalogEntryWire/Limits and launch::Registration/LaunchSpec/LaunchTarget submodules, plus wire payload SurfaceRequest and DecodeError for admission bridging.
Exact geometry match required: requested w/h must equal frozen window size, not merely fit display. Stale catalog entries cause Geometry refusals even when display could fit the request.
core/src/control/mod.rs exists only for frame publication via publish_frame. Operator control transitions, cancellation notices and daemon forwarding belong to serve, not here.
core/src/control/tests.rs proves genesis-frame behavior: generation 0 is refused as stale without committing, generation 1 is admitted and committed, with journal recovery checked.
core/src/journal/anchor.rs only reads an externally protected metaviewer.checkpoint/v1 head and verifies a journal against it. It never creates, refreshes, or falls back from a required anchor.

Entry is publish_frame(authority: &mut Authority, surface_id: &str, frame: Frame, witnesses: Vec<Witness>). Callers supply a mutable Authority plus surface id, frame, and retained witnesses; returns Result<Outcome, JournalError>.

Data flows surface lookup -> refusal branch -> authority.apply(Input::Refuse) or authority.apply_with_witnesses(Input::Frame, witnesses). On frame-store error it attempts authority.apply(Input::Refuse { reason: Refusal::Policy }) and returns that result.

Publication requires a strictly newer generation across a control refresh fence: generation 0 always refused; otherwise frame.generation must exceed previous frame.generation when a previous frame exists.
Frame validity requires width != 0, height != 0, sha256 length 64 of lowercase hex digits, and at least one witness with w.sha256 == frame.sha256. Any violation maps to Refusal::Policy.
Unknown surface_id (surfaces.get returns None) yields Refusal::Policy via authority.apply(Input::Refuse). No frame is stored; Outcome.reason carries the refusal.
Known but !surface.live yields Refusal::SurfaceNotAgentControlled via Input::Refuse. Distinguishes a non-agent-controlled surface from generic policy refusal.
Stale generation (0, or <= previous.generation) yields Refusal::StaleFrame via Input::Refuse. A resumed surface therefore needs a newer frame to advance.
Bad dimensions, non-64 or non-lowercase-hex sha256, or no matching witness yields Refusal::Policy via Input::Refuse. Same path covers all content-identity failures.

If apply_with_witnesses for Input::Frame fails, publish_frame attempts a durable Input::Refuse Policy entry and returns its outcome. Storage failure or poisoning propagates as Err rather than fake success.

User sees the picture never update after publishing: an old or zero generation, zero size, bad hash, or missing witness silently becomes a journalled refusal instead of a new frame. Logs/Outcome show StaleFrame, SurfaceNotAgentControlled, or Policy.

Refusal is journalled but commits no frame: expected state is before.clone() with core_seq += 1 only; on success the surface frame is additionally set to Some(frame). Recovered Authority state must equal expected.

Entries are verify_with_anchor(root, anchor_path) for the conventional root/journal.jsonl and scan_with_anchor(path, root, anchor_path) for an explicit journal plus archive root. Both return Result<Replay, JournalError>.

Flow: read_file(anchor_path, MAX_LINE) -> canonicalize anchor and root -> reject archive-local anchor -> parse Checkpoint -> scan(path, root) -> compare json(expected) vs json(replay.checkpoint). Mismatch returns Corrupt.

Anchor must live outside the session archive with storage permissions the archive writer cannot rewrite. Path separation is checked (anchor.starts_with(archive) rejected) but cannot prove independent administration; that is a caller precondition.
Anchor pins the exact head: json(expected) must equal json(replay.checkpoint). Legitimate later appends need a new trusted anchor. Unanchored scan proves local consistency only.

Missing, unreadable, overlong, symlink-containing, noncanonical, unparseable, or archive-local anchor maps to JournalError::Corrupt. Scan failure or checkpoint JSON mismatch also returns Corrupt with no Replay.

Depends on admission Authority, Frame, Input, Outcome, journal Witness and JournalError, and Refusal. Reuses authority.apply and authority.apply_with_witnesses; no direct storage access in this module.

Control transitions must use serve authenticated routing; this module must not gain a transition function (compile_fail example uses control::transition). Refusals are journal entries, so retrying a stale frame without bumping generation never advances.
Tests isolate parallel runs with static NEXT AtomicU64 temp-dir suffixes and TempRoot Drop removing the dir. publish_frame itself takes &mut Authority, so callers serialize admission updates.
TempRoot deletes its temp dir on drop; test Authority dirs use mode 0o700. Anchor reads are bounded by MAX_LINE via read_file, limiting memory from an oversized anchor file.

Test session uses CoreState::session(frame-genesis), Input::Connect, and a live agent-controlled surface with frame None, then journal path sessions/frame-genesis/journal.jsonl for Authority::recover verification.

Private archive v1 journal gives durable replayable session history: canonical event sidecars retain inputs/outcomes and boundary bytes, checkpoint.json binds count/tail/archive/genesis, recovery rolls back torn/unsealed tails and cleans sidecars/orphans, witnesses verify digests before disk/cache.

Journal::create(state_dir,state) is fresh-session entry: validates session_id via safe_component and core_seq 0, builds state_dir/sessions/<id>/{events,artifacts} with 0700, writes genesis.json and journal.jsonl header, stages first checkpoint.json, syncs dirs to ancestors.

Journal::recover(path,root) is restart entry: takes exclusive WriterFile lock, scans journal, on scan error rolls back uncommitted tail, cleans uncommitted artifacts, replays from genesis, promotes checkpoint.next only after full-closure replay, evicts surface caches.

Live entries are retain_witness sync-now, retain_verified_pixels/retain_verified_witness/retain_frame_witness grouped, verify_surface_frame[_with_geometry], flush_sync/close/shutdown; close/shutdown flush group-commit, close channel, join worker.

Write flow: caller bytes -> sha256_hex check -> artifacts/<sha256> via publish/publish_unsynced -> dirty_files+unsynced_witnesses -> journal.jsonl append via WriterFile -> checkpoint.next/json; frame path stages batches through SyncCmd::Flush.

Read flow: read_file checks symlink, size, ino/dev, exact length; parse enforces canonical_bytes sorted keys and deny_unknown_fields; scan replays Genesis/Event lines, recomputes archive_next chain and tail; verify_witness rereads artifacts and rehashes.

Journal states: poisoned latch, unsynced_frames/first_unsynced_at, dirty_files/staged_dirty_len, pending_checkpoint/staged_checkpoint_count, completed counts, sync_failed; poisoned or sync_failed forces Poisoned and clears surface caches on next op.

SyncWorker states in WorkerState: queue, staged StagedBatch with deadline, in_flight, closed, finished, sticky_err, completed counts; loop pops Flush, waits for deadline/closed, executes batch, records sticky_err; Barrier returns sticky result to flush_sync.

Canonical identity: json uses canonical_bytes with sorted keys and rejects non-u64/i64 numbers; parse rejects duplicate keys/alternate spellings by comparing bytes; hex requires 64 lowercase hex; Witness byte_len in 1..=MAX_BYTES.

Confinement: confined rejects ParentDir and any symlink prefix; private_directory_for_uid requires dir uid==current_uid and mode 0700; artifact/frame files require uid match and mode &077==0; current_uid reads /proc/self/status Uid and caches.

Checkpoint schema metaviewer.checkpoint/v1 with count/tail/archive/genesis; closure snapshots live values; matching_checkpoint accepts json/next only if all four equal replay; Header metaviewer.journal/v1, Genesis metaviewer.archive/v1.

Witness is sha256+byte_len; VerifiedPixels guarantees bytes hash to sha256 except fast-path memcmp hit; Event holds SessionRecord+Envelope+Input+Outcome+state+witnesses; event_kind maps Refused/Admitted/Executed/SurfaceChanged; audit_envelope wraps record.

Any inline/background fsync failure sets sync_failed/poisoned; next commit/retain/flush returns Poisoned, clears caches, aborts batches, joins worker; worker sticky_err persists and join logs journal background sync failed.

Torn/unsealed tail: scan error Empty/Blank/Utf8Bom/MissingLf/Oversize/Corrupt triggers rollback removing torn sidecar/journal bytes, deleting orphans, syncing events/artifacts/journal/checkpoint.next in order, truncating journal, syncing dirs.

Digest/ownership path: read_verified_inner returns frame digest mismatch on length/trailing/hash mismatch; verify maps to Witness; retain rejects empty/>64MiB/non-hex/mismatch; is_verified_artifact checks dev/ino/uid/mode/mtime/ctime.

User sees commit or flush_sync fail with Poisoned after disk error, recent frames missing after restart from torn-tail rollback, startup refusal UPGRADE-REQUIRED with expected/found versions, logs journal close failed, background sync failed, join timed out.

Tester sees fail-closed Corrupt(empty), Corrupt(blank), Corrupt(utf8_bom), Corrupt(missing_lf) for torn line without LF, Corrupt(oversize) over 64 MiB, frame digest mismatch on tampered pixels, Locked when another writer holds flock.

Frame group-commit: unsynced frames wait FRAME_SYNC_WINDOW 50ms or FRAME_SYNC_MAX_BATCH 8; stage clones handles and stages deadline batch; dispatch queues Flush up to MAX_PENDING_SYNC_BATCHES 4 then coalesces by rel path.

Close/Drop: flush_sync drains via direct execute or Barrier with 5s join_timeout_for; join sets closed, waits for finished, on timeout poisons and keeps worker for later join; Drop flushes then joins with abort.

Bounded memory: MAX_UNCOMMITTED_ARTIFACTS 32 evicts oldest uncommitted, MAX_DIRTY_FILES 32 syncs/evicts oldest, MAX_VERIFIED_WITNESS_CACHE 256 LRU, surface/retained caps 64MiB each, MAX_BYTES 64MiB, MAX_RECORDS 100000.

Durability order: witness file sync, artifacts dir sync, events dir sync, journal.jsonl sync, checkpoint.next sync, rename to checkpoint.json, root sync; execute_sync_batch validates existing checkpoint count/schema if rename races.

No config file: layout from state_dir/sessions/<session_id>; safe_component limits 128 chars alnum/._-; core_version from CARGO_PKG_VERSION; uid/mode enforced on state/sessions/root/events/artifacts; archive budget 64 MiB.

Depends on admission Authority/CoreState/Input/Outcome for retain and replay, Envelope/Endpoint/Component/Clock/Command for audit_envelope, MAX_FRAME_BYTES for MAX_LINE, internal sha256/StreamingSha256, unix DirBuilderExt/MetadataExt for modes and dev/ino.

Hazards: symlink/ParentDir escape blocked by confined plus ino/dev recheck; fork-inherited flock needs explicit WriterFile unlock; torn sidecar/journal/next on crash; stale checkpoint.next replaced only under lock after replay; disk bytes never cached without SHA-256.

This file implements the durable session journal: ordered SessionRecord lines in journal.jsonl linked by prev_sha256 and tail, per-sequence event sidecars in events/, content-addressed witnesses in artifacts/, plus genesis and checkpoint files for replay and crash recovery.

Journal.append is the sole write entry: caller supplies Input, Outcome, CoreState and witnesses. It reconciles worker progress, rejects poisoned handles, validates sequence linkage and state transition, verifies witnesses, then follows frame or non-frame durability path before updating in-memory state.

Non-frame appends publish the event sidecar unsynced, append the journal line, fsync dirty witness and event files, fsync artifact and event directories, fsync journal.jsonl, then write and fsync checkpoint.next before atomic rename to checkpoint.json and root directory sync.

Frame appends publish the event sidecar unsynced, append the journal line, stage checkpoint via checkpoint_unsynced without immediate promotion, track dirty files with pending checkpoint, and either dispatch or stage a background sync batch based on batch size and time window.

Append and replay require strict linkage: expected sequence is count plus one, outcome and state sequence must match it, reduced state from apply must equal supplied outcome and snapshot, record uses msg_id event linkage and prev_sha256 equal to tail, else Invalid is returned.

Witnesses are content verified by digest and byte length via verify_witness and verified cache, recorded in committed set, tracked in dirty files if unsynced; required witness derived from input and outcome must be present or append fails with Witness.

Once a durable mutation starts the handle is poisoned until success; any sync failure latches poisoned and sync_failed. Later append, retain, and flush_sync return Poisoned, witness sync failure blocks retry, and only recovery can clear it.

Size and count policies bound growth: journal bytes plus line ending, archive bytes including snapshot, file length, and record count are checked against MAX_BYTES, MAX_RECORDS and MAX_LINE; overflow returns Policy, oversize line returns Oversize, and next sequence overflow is rejected.

Line readers enforce exact framing: UTF BOM is rejected as Utf8Bom, missing trailing newline as MissingLf, empty or whitespace-only line as Blank, overlong read as Oversize, corrupt parse as Corrupt or Duplicate, leaving torn tail detectable on next scan.

Visible failure is a rejected write or a scan error naming Poisoned, Invalid, Witness, Io, MissingLf, Unsealed, Corrupt, Duplicate, or UpgradeRequired; after a torn append the journal holds an extra sidecar and truncated line, and recover rolls back to the last committed prefix so later appends resume cleanly.

verify_prefix_and_classify_tail replays genesis through checkpoint count checking header, genesis binding, hash chain, envelope, witness, state apply, kind, snapshot and archive, then walks beyond prefix to distinguish torn bytes from structurally valid uncommitted tail while enforcing frame ordering.

try_rollback_uncommitted_tail never rolls back UpgradeRequired, Invalid, Locked or Poisoned scan errors; otherwise it loads checkpoint.json and checkpoint.next candidates, verifies each prefix, highest count first, and returns the original scan error if none verifies.

Crash-safe rollback forces committed witnesses, genesis, and committed events durable, ensures checkpoint.json durably holds the chosen checkpoint, removes uncommitted events and orphan artifacts and syncs those directories, truncates journal to prefix offset and syncs it, then removes stale checkpoint.next and syncs root.

Non-frame path synchronizes with the background worker through a Barrier command over a rendezvous channel with a join timeout; success continues, worker error propagates, timeout marks aborted and returns Io, keeping the worker thread alive across normal flushes.

Drop and close flush pending group commits, promote checkpoint.next, and join the worker so the session directory is quiescent on return; without join a detached worker still mutates the directory after drop, which the negative control demonstrates.

Append tracks dirty open files, unsynced witnesses, unsynced frame count, first unsynced time, staged lengths and completed sync batches; reconcile_worker_progress keeps in-flight batches tracked until durable and does not clear them when completed count has not advanced.

Steady-state recover with checkpoint.json matching the journal performs no historical fsync; when checkpoint.next holds the proven checkpoint while checkpoint.json is stale, recover forces witnesses, genesis, events, journal and directories durable before promoting next and syncing root.

Session directories require private mode and owner match; foreign owner is refused even with private mode. A retained duplicate file description keeps the lock held as Locked across recover; closing the old descriptor must not release the new writer lock.

default_state_dir resolves the conductor state destination without creating it: non-empty absolute XDG_STATE_HOME joined with metaviewer if set, otherwise non-empty absolute HOME joined with local state suffix; empty or relative values return Invalid.

scan and verify_chain are read-only validators: they confine the path, enforce private archive, check header schema and core version, bind genesis by header hash and session, replay each record with sidecar and witness checks, reject extra event files as Unsealed, and require a matching checkpoint.

On-disk dependencies are journal.jsonl lines, events sequence files, artifacts addressed by digest, genesis.json, checkpoint.json and checkpoint.next, plus artifact, event and root directories whose fsync ordering guarantees crash consistency; missing or non-file entries fail the operation.

Torn event sidecar alone, torn journal line, and truncated genuine checkpoint.next each still recover the committed prefix and reclaim sidecars and orphan artifacts; sidecar cleanup precedes journal truncation, each recovery step is idempotent, and stale next-sequence files do not collide with later appends.
Regression suite proving unchanged-frame fast path skips SHA-256 only when committed surface witness, generation, geometry, epoch and permissions all match.
Tests enter via Journal::create, CoreState::apply, retain_verified_pixels, verify_surface_frame and VerifiedPixels::read_verified_for_surface with shm files and digests.
Control flows Input::Frame into CoreState then Journal::append with frame witnesses; verification reads shm bytes and returns VerifiedPixels carrying sha256, hash_skipped, hash_ns and timing fields.
Witness cache states: unprimed, committed, evicted, poisoned. Commit on retain/append; evict on lifecycle or epoch change; poison clears bytes and forces JournalError::Poisoned.
Fast path requires same session root, same surface_id, same epoch, advancing generation, same width/height, same length and digest, mode 0o600, unpoisoned journal.
VerifiedPixels reports hash_skipped true with hash_ns 0 and skipped_hash_ns>0 on hit; false with hash_ns>0 on full streaming SHA-256. shm_read_ns plus skipped_hash_ns stays within elapsed nanos.
Stale generation, geometry change, wrong epoch, other surface, other root, bad mode 0o644, or poison all fall back to full hash or return Invalid/Poisoned without appending records.
Single-byte flip at start, middle, or end with spoofed digest fails read_verified_for_surface with InvalidData and verify/retain with Witness; journal count and journal.jsonl lines unchanged.
Length attacks truncated or extended by one byte fail under both advertised and actual lengths with InvalidData/Witness; advertised true digest of changed bytes forces full hash and succeeds.
Corrupted artifacts/<sha> on disk makes Journal::recover during scan refuse with Witness and never bless unhashed bytes; fail_next_witness_sync plus retain_witness Io sets poisoned and clears cache.
User sees unchanged frames still verified slowly or refused: every repeat frame costs a full hash after lifecycle, epoch, geometry, permission, or poison change instead of instant hit.
Tampered pixels are rejected rather than recorded: spoofed or truncated shm yields InvalidData/Witness errors and no new journal record, so the frame never commits.
Lifecycle Update, TakeControl, ReleaseControl handling, Lost, Destroyed, and Connect/epoch change each evict affected surface witnesses; Connect clears all entries and bytes to zero.
Per-surface witness cache capped by MAX_SURFACE_WITNESS_BYTES 64 MiB: 22 surfaces of 1280x900 RGB24 retain newest 19 and evict oldest 00-02; bytes never exceed cap.
Fast versus full journal runs must be bit-identical: journal.jsonl, checkpoint.json, replayed state, boundaries, count, tail, archive and genesis match across static and changed generations.
Bench for 1280x900 verify runs only when MV_RUN_HASH_BENCH is set or test filter contains bench_1280x900_frame_verify; prints p50/p95 total, hash and memcmp timings without assertions.
Suite depends on CoreState admission inputs, Journal witness retention, temp session roots, 0o700 dirs, 0o600 shm files, and recovery_fix fixtures included from tests/journal_recovery_fix.rs.
Approved pure-Rust SHA-256 provides streaming digests with lowercase-hex output used as frame and witness identifiers.
Crate root reserves authority namespaces and owner lanes for admission, journal, supervisor, verify, control, record and catalog modules.
Callers create StreamingSha256::new or default, feed bytes via update, and consume with finalize_hex; sha256_hex is the one-shot helper.
Bytes accumulate in 64-byte buf with total_len counter; full blocks compress immediately and remainder buffers; finalize appends 0x80, zero pad, big-endian bit length, then hex-encodes state.
Digest format is fixed 64-char lowercase hex via 0123456789abcdef table; initial state uses standard SHA-256 IVs and 64 round constants.
Chunked updates must equal one-shot hash for lengths spanning padding edges 55,56,57,63,64,65,119,120,128,4097,131073 and chunk sizes 1,7,63,64,65,512,8192.
Hasher states: empty, partial-block buffered, block-aligned; update fills partial block first, streams whole 64-byte chunks, then buffers tail; finalize consumes and pads exactly once.
total_len counts all updated bytes; buf_len stays below 64; finalize emits one or two blocks depending on whether buf_len exceeds 56 after 0x80.
Test-only oracle is sha2 crate RefSha256 digest; production path uses local rotr, s0/s1, ep0/ep1, rnd and sched macros plus compress_block with no unsafe code.
No error return: misuse such as double finalize is prevented by consuming self; wrong digests surface downstream as witness mismatches, not here.
If this code miscomputes, every frame hash mismatches its pinned witness and captures or journal appends are refused as invalid events.
StreamingSha256 holds no locks or globals; each instance is single-threaded mutable state safe to use per stream.
Memory footprint is constant: 8-word state plus 64-byte buffer regardless of input length; compression is inline over borrowed blocks.
Crate forbids unsafe_code; sha2 dependency and STAGE_TIMINGS hash_ns accounting plus hash_calls_3mb counter compile only under cfg(test).
Timing instrumentation mutates journal STAGE_TIMINGS thread-local on every update/finalize in tests, so benchmarks include that overhead and must not be read as production cost.
Lib re-exports replay, transport and wire at top level and exposes serve; admission/journal map to W1-CORE-ADMIT and later owners documented in header comment.
RAM host capture policy bounds live pixel retention and recording rows; serve owner journals prepared transitions before installing state.
Inputs arrive via frame/frame_verified with FrameRef plus bytes and now_ms, drop_frame on loss, and prepare for recordStart, recordStop, screenshot and list.
frame checks empty, over-RING and sha256_hex mismatch then delegates to frame_verified; verified frames update latest map and fan out append_frame per active recording with journal events.
Rows move recording to sealed on recordStop or screenshot; sealed captures use export path independent of sampling limits and pixels stay resident until reclaimed.
At most 64 rows, 8 concurrent recordings, 8 MiB per ring, 64 MiB total retained bytes, max_fps ceiling 60 default 3 fps with 1000/fps ms decimation.
Refusal codes are exact: SURFACE_UNKNOWN, CAPTURE_UNAVAILABLE, ALREADY_RECORDING, NOT_RECORDING, LIMIT, BUDGET_EXCEEDED for fps 61, POLICY otherwise; replies carry ok, code and request_id.
Oversize, empty, or sha-mismatched bytes return Error::Event and never enter RAM; projected total over MEMORY returns Error::Overflow with state unchanged.
recordStart with unknown surface, no latest, duplicate active recording, over row or recording cap, or over MEMORY preflight returns ok false without allocating IDs or events.
Coordinator refusal Case5 maps BUDGETEXCEEDED to BUDGET_EXCEEDED else POLICY; recordStop on missing or non-recording id returns NOT_RECORDING.
User sees recording that stops early or never starts: over-rate frames vanish as decimated with dropped_frames count, oversize frames are refused, and ninth recording shows LIMIT.
Stopped recording shows frame count, duration_ms and concatenated-bytes sha256; decimated runs report fewer frames plus dropped_frames, e.g. 3 kept and 3 dropped.
Decimation keys on per-id max_fps and last_frame_ms: frames within now-last < 1000/fps are dropped and counted; kept frames update last_frame_ms and ring counts.
project_append predicts FIFO eviction without cloning: evicts oldest ring frames until len fits RING, subtracts evicted bytes before adding; append_frame then pops oldest and pushes back.
retained_bytes sums latest plus all ring bytes with checked_add to Overflow; frame_verified preflights latest replacement plus per-id projections before mutating latest or journal.
recordStop seals row, stamps duration_ms from created_ms, concatenates ring bytes in order and returns sealed true with sha256; list returns rows; screenshot reply has no ram_path or pixels.
Host IDs are capture-<serial> with checked serial increment and valid_id check for _host_id; wire coordinator IDs stay host-generated with renderer correlation in boundary witness.
Depends on Coordinator settings memory/ring/max_fps, RecordRequest/Event serde schemas, sha256_hex witness, and JournalSink Events wrapper for observe/handle output.
latest replacement and ring eviction interact: exact 64 MiB fill succeeds but one extra byte overflows; callers must treat Overflow as unchanged state, not partial commit.
Build a deterministic ustar archive of RGB24 PNG frames for one sealed capture, with zero timestamps and owners and private entries, bounded to 16 MiB, 4096 frames, 4096 pixels per axis.
Host.export_plan(id) validates id, sealed flag, pixel store presence and frame count, then encodes every retained frame with png() before any disk access.
png() prepends filter byte 0 per row, wraps rows in zlib stored blocks with Adler32, then emits PNG signature plus IHDR bit depth 8 color type 2, IDAT, IEND chunks with CRC32 via chunk().
Receipt is {id, bytes, sha256} where sha256 is over final tar bytes including two trailing zero blocks; archive name is {id}-{digest}.tar; export retains RAM authority.

Unknown or malformed id returns CAPTURE_UNKNOWN; unsealed returns NOT_SEALED; missing or empty pixels or width*height*3 mismatch returns CAPTURE_UNAVAILABLE; over 4096 frames, bad dimensions, or tar over limit returns LIMIT.

publish_transaction(destination, transaction) pins destination to a directory FD, refuses read-only mode bits, writes exclusive 0600 temp .mv-export-{name}-{tx} via /proc/self/fd, then hard-links final name.

Publication starts with temporary set and published unset; after hard link both set; after temp removal only published set; commit() clears published so Drop keeps file, otherwise Drop unlinks both and syncs directory.

No clobber: hard_link fails with DESTINATION_EXISTS if final name exists; re-pinned directory dev/ino must match; published path symlink_metadata must be a regular file with same dev/ino as held open temp.

Pin failure, read-only mode, temp create/write/sync failure, grant replacement, inode substitution, temp unlink or directory sync failure return DESTINATION_UNAVAILABLE; existing final returns DESTINATION_EXISTS.
recover(destination, receipt, transaction) reconciles only journal-pinned final name {id}-{digest}.tar; removes matching temp name, then validates or removes final without following replaced links.

Receipt id must pass valid_id and sha256 must be 64 lowercase hex; archive must be regular file under size limit, O_NOFOLLOW open, same dev/ino, bounded read matches receipt bytes and digest, mode 0600, else removed and false returned.

pin_directory walks only absolute paths with RootDir and Normal components, rejecting dot segments, NUL, CR, LF, non-UTF8 and overlong paths, opening each level O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW from / through /proc/self/fd.
Descriptor-relative publication plus verify-then-link closes symlink-swap races; libc_flags uses O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK with arch-specific constants for aarch64 versus x86/x86_64.

User sees export refused with DESTINATION_EXISTS when file already present, or DESTINATION_UNAVAILABLE when destination missing, read-only, replaced, or a symlink alias; aborted journal leaves no file because Drop cleans up.
File synced after write, directory synced after link and after Drop cleanup; temp always created create_new 0600 and permissions reasserted even for privileged host.
recover uses symlink_metadata and O_NOFOLLOW open and bounded take(EXPORT_LIMIT+1) read, so a swapped symlink target is removed by name without reading or deleting the victim file.
Provide a one red-pixel screenshot capture host by loading frame_ref.valid.json, forcing 1x1 dimensions and matching digest, then ingesting one frame and preparing a screenshot capture.
Two export_plan calls on same id are byte-identical; receipt sha256 and bytes match archive; first header name is frames/00000000.png with modes 0000600 and PNG magic at offset 512.
One-pixel red PNG bytes must equal an independent hex reference covering zlib stored block, PNG CRC32s and Adler32, catching wrong filter, dimensions or checksums.
Published file content equals plan bytes, mode is 0600, directory holds exactly one entry; after commit a second publish fails DESTINATION_EXISTS without changing file or entry count.
Publishing to a missing path returns DESTINATION_UNAVAILABLE; dropping an uncommitted publication leaves zero directory entries, modelling an aborted journal before commit.
Pre-existing symlink final name causes DESTINATION_EXISTS and the link target bytes stay untouched; alias paths, child paths and dot-dot paths are refused with DESTINATION_UNAVAILABLE.
A 0500 destination is refused even though the test process could write; entry count stays zero, proving explicit read-only mode check rather than relying on OS denial.
Unknown, dot-dot and rooted ids give CAPTURE_UNKNOWN; clearing sealed gives NOT_SEALED; truncated pixel bytes give CAPTURE_UNAVAILABLE, all before any publication.
4097 retained frames refuse LIMIT; three 2048x1024 RGB frames refuse LIMIT by archive bytes, proving RAM-side size validation precedes disk work.
recordStart id refuses NOT_SEALED, second frame accepted, recordStop seals; export then contains frames/00000000.png and frames/00000001.png in order with differing PNG payloads.
Exporting retains RAM authority: pixel store length stays 2 after export, so export is a copy rather than a move.
recover on symlink archive and temp names with transaction 5 returns false, removes both names, leaves victim file bytes keep, proving unlink-by-name without target following.
A tester sees no leftover temp or partial tar after a crash before commit, and no clobber of an existing export; symlink attacks do not delete outside files.
In-memory JournalSink clones every SessionRecord for guard tests; sealed_disk, coordinator, request, start, frame and export helpers build minimal valid RAM and disk recording scenarios.
coordinator() uses memory 32, ring 16, max_fps 30, one surface s, and fixed disk grant cap plus /exports/a.tar; all budget tests run against these small overlapping reservations.
Three sequential screenshot, frame, seal, release cycles each reach Phase::Sealed then vanish from recording(); release is what reclaims the 16-byte named reservation.
ram_start with ring u64::MAX returns POLICY recording bounds are invalid without overflow, creates no recording, journals a Refused record; checked_add paths stay safe.
Starting on unknown surface with two actives held returns POLICY surface is not admitted, creates nothing, journals Refused; pressure does not bypass admission.
Third 16-byte start over 32-byte memory fails BUDGETEXCEEDED; ram_stop alone does not free budget; detail names held a=16 b=16; only release(a) lets c start.
Uppercase frame digest fails observe with Error::Event, coordinator clone unchanged, journal length unchanged; digest alphabet is strictly lowercase hex.
ram_path /dev/shm/ and /dev/shm/subdir/ are rejected as directory paths even under /dev/shm, atomically with no state or journal change.
/tmp/x.png rejected as non-shm path; /dev/shm/x.png accepted, byte_count becomes 8, journal grows by one, proving the starts_with /dev/shm guard and atomic reject.
Exported receipt with byte_count 0 on sealed disk recording fails Error::Event with clone and journal unchanged; zero-byte exports never mark Exported.
Exported receipt with uppercase digest fails Error::Event atomically; export digest alphabet matches frame rule.
Valid exported event moves sealed disk r to Phase::Exported with byte_count 8 retained; reservation r=16 still blocks new starts until release(r), then start succeeds.
Two unreleased screenshots block third with BUDGETEXCEEDED naming shot1=16 shot2=16; releasing shot1 admits shot3, proving sealed screenshots hold reservations.
Six 6MiB latest frames total 36MiB; four recordStarts reach 60MiB under 64MiB cap; fifth start and screenshot both refuse LIMIT with empty events and unchanged host.
Latest replacement subtracts old latest plus evicted ring frame to land exactly 64MiB; oversize latest or unknown surface returns Overflow with host unchanged.
Single-surface 3MiB latest plus two ring frames total 3xLEN; recordStop reports frames 2 and sha over concatenated ring bytes, proving FIFO eviction of oldest ring frame.
Recording authority is an explicit offline seam: caller supplies admitted surfaces and a durable JournalSink; sink failure commits neither recording state nor chain cursor.
New requires ring nonzero and within 1GiB and memory, max_fps 1..120, surface ids valid, and disk grant with valid capability id plus absolute path; else Error::Configuration.
valid_id needs nonempty up to 128 chars, first char alphanumeric, rest alphanumeric or . _ : -; used for request, surface, recording and capability ids.
absolute needs rooted path up to 4096 chars, no NUL/CR/LF, only RootDir and Normal components, no dot or dot-dot segments.

Unadmitted surface, inactive stop, bad fps/ring, over-limit fps/ring, over-memory reservation, reused or released identity, or unauthorized disk grant each journal a refused event and leave next state uncommitted on sink error.
Every unreleased capture reserves ring bytes against memory_bytes with checked_add; refusal detail lists held id=bytes pairs truncated at 3500 chars plus count of additional reservations.

Recording starts in Phase::Recording; ram_stop or disk_stop moves matching mode and surface entry to Sealed and emits stopped with frame and byte counts; screenshots use supplied capture id as wire id.
release removes only sealed or exported ids, records a session-lifetime tombstone, emits no wire event and leaves journal chain unchanged; unknown, released or active ids error without mutation.
observe accepts frame_captured metadata and exported receipts from the authenticated recorder, deriving ring evictions locally; pixels never cross the journal boundary.

Frame needs active recording, matching surface, byte_count 1..ring, absolute /dev/shm/ non-directory path, 64 lowercase-hex sha, valid request id; overflow and mismatch return Error::Event atomically.

Oversize ring pushes evict oldest frames first, emitting dropped with ram_ring_oldest policy before the frame event; screenshot frames auto-seal and emit stopped; counts include post-eviction retained frames.

Export receipt needs sealed disk recording, matching surface, byte_count 1..EXPORT_BYTE_LIMIT 16MiB, lowercase hex sha, valid request id and exact configured capability and path; success moves to Exported.

commit builds SessionRecord with incremented core_seq and hash-chained prev_sha256 over canonical bytes, appends whole entry to sink first, and only then swaps self to next; sink error leaves self unchanged.
JournalSink.append must durably append the entire record plus events or return Error; entries carry metadata only, never raw pixels.

User sees recording stop reporting retained frame and byte counts after eviction, or an export that only succeeds after disk stop with the exact authorized destination; wrong destination never changes state.
release only reclaims coordinator metadata; the adapter owns RAM files and must reclaim its copies separately, and observed paths grant no filesystem deletion authority.
Record unit tests use a failing-capable in-memory sink storing records and events; helpers build settings, coordinator, ram_start requests, and /dev/shm frame events for refusal and lifecycle checks.
disk_start with null or mismatched capability or path journals POLICY refusal, leaves recordings empty, records Refused kind with unchanged prev chain 0-repeat-64.
ram_start then 10-byte frame plus 9-byte frame emits dropped_frames 1; 17-byte frame errors atomically; ram_stop seals with frame 1 byte 9; second stop and id reuse are refused.
Journal chain links by sha: second record prev_sha256 equals sha over canonical bytes of first record, verified with canonical_bytes and sha256_hex.
Export before disk_stop errors; after stop first export succeeds; second identical export errors; retargeted destination_path with resealed phase still errors.
Screenshot frame with /dev/shm/../disk path errors atomically; valid 8-byte frame seals with stopped event; second frame on sealed screenshot errors.

Zero, oversize, zero-fps, high-fps, over-ring, over-max-fps and unknown-surface starts each journal POLICY without creating recordings; sink failure returns Journal with state unchanged; bad limits fail Configuration.
ReplayTable holds bounded session plus sender-instance replay evidence as entry triples and per-key last sequence; new rejects zero capacity with MissingOrZero.

Empty or over-128-char session, instance or nonce gives InvalidIdentity; seq 0 gives ZeroSequence; seen triple gives DuplicateNonce; seq below previous+1 gives NonIncreasingSequence with overflow mapped to Exhausted.
Capacity checked after identity and order checks: at-capacity inserts fail CapacityExceeded without mutating entries or sequences; successful insert stores triple and latest seq.
contains tests exact session, endpoint, nonce triple; snapshot clones entries set and sequences map for callers to persist or compare.
Caller sees duplicate or replayed message rejected by nonce, out-of-order message rejected by sequence, and reconnect allowed once without losing duplicate protection.
Prove stale frame generations over both direct frame and frame_ready event wirings are journalled as STALE_FRAME refusals without tearing down the connection or bumping epoch.
Prove frames for unknown surfaces are journalled as STALE_FRAME refusals without creating surface state, tearing down, or bumping epoch, for both wire forms.
Tests run async serve bodies on a current-thread Tokio runtime; start_server binds a temp unix socket, opens Server state, and spawns serve with the test uid.
Peer connects, exchanges hello, then sends envelope/v0.2 bodies with per-peer seq and nonce prefix; receive uses read_frame deadline plus a short watchdog that names the peer and seq on failure.
SharedFrame creates a 100x60 RGB file under /dev/shm with mode 0600 filled with f bytes; value() loads frame_ref.valid.json, sets matching dimensions and digest, ramws_path and generation.
After created surface and accepted generation 32, stale inputs 20, 32, 31 or unknown-surface 33 each return decision refused with STALE_FRAME, matching proposal id and core_seq before+1.
After each refusal a flush_sync plus journal scan shows replayed core_seq, snapshot and epoch equal live state; unknown-surface creates no surface key; demo surface frame stays generation 32.
A later valid generation 33 is fanned out to ui with generation 33 and no preceding refused-frame fanout; epoch unchanged; final flush plus scan snapshot matches live authority.

Temp creates a unique directory from process id and atomic NEXT and removes it on drop; SharedFrame removes its shm file on drop; close_server aborts task and waits for connection tasks to release server.
close_server aborts the serve task, drops peers, then waits up to 2s until Arc strong count returns to one, proving connection tasks released the server before state teardown.
Sender sees a refused verdict with STALE_FRAME instead of disconnect; other peers see no bogus frame; next good generation still arrives normally.
Test nonces derive from instance plus seq and timestamps are zero, so these helpers must not be mistaken for production replay or clock handling.
Provide a small JSON canonicalizer for serve state: parse, sort object keys, normalize strings and integers, re-emit a byte-stable form for hashing and comparison.
canonicalise_and_verify_state first requires 64 lowercase-hex claimed digest, then canonicalises, hashes with sha256_hex, and returns canonical bytes only on exact digest match.
Input must be nonempty UTF-8 up to 1MiB, exactly one JSON value with no trailing bytes, root must be an object; output must also fit 1MiB or Oversize is returned.
Empty gives Empty, overlong gives Oversize, bad UTF-8 gives InvalidUtf8, bad tokens or trailing bytes give Syntax, non-object root gives RootNotObject, depth over 64 gives DepthExceeded.
Objects sort entries by key after parsing and reject duplicate keys; arrays preserve order; whitespace around values is insignificant.
Strings reject unescaped controls and bad escapes, validate \u hex, pair high and low surrogates into one code point, and reject lone surrogates or truncated escapes.

Numbers reject leading zeros, fractions as FloatForbidden, exponents as ExponentForbidden, and out-of-range values as IntegerOutOfRange; only integers within plus/minus 9007199254740991 survive, with -0 normalized to 0.

Emitter writes null, booleans, integers, sorted objects and ordered arrays; strings escape quote, backslash, short controls symbolically and other controls as lowercase \u00xx, leaving other Unicode verbatim.

Vectors pin byte-for-byte parity with the JS implementation for sorted keys, verbatim Unicode, control escapes, raw angle and ampersand handling, safe-int bounds, and a holdings state fixture with expected sha values.
1.5, 1.0, 1e5, 1E-2, plus/minus 9007199254740992 are refused; 63 nested arrays pass while 64 fail DepthExceeded; 1MiB+1 spaces fail Oversize.
Parser is a single-pass byte cursor with skip_ws and peek; output preallocates input length; hashing uses sha2 Sha256 over canonical bytes.
Digest helper depends on sha2 crate; hex digest uses lowercase formatting required by is_hex64 checks elsewhere.
is_hex64 requires length 64 with only 0-9 and a-f; uppercase or wrong length fails verification as DigestMismatch before parsing.

Caller sees Empty, Oversize with size, InvalidUtf8, Syntax message, RootNotObject, DepthExceeded, DuplicateKey, FloatForbidden, ExponentForbidden, IntegerOutOfRange, or DigestMismatch instead of canonical bytes.
Canonical bytes can differ in length from input because of key sorting, escape normalization and Unicode verbatim output; callers must use returned bytes and digest, not the raw input.

capture.rs is the host capture API: screenshot, RAM recordStart/recordStop, export of sealed captures, and list, plus per-frame ingest, durable journaling, lazy export recovery, and record_request/v0.2 wire mapping. RAM recordings expire on restart; metadata and receipts remain replayable.

capture_request(peer,method,request) is the host binding seam. Only registered UI principals pass; others get invalid capture requires registered UI. Dispatches screenshot, recordStart, recordStop, export, list to capture_transition or capture_export_to after strict shape checks.

capture_wire(now_ns,env,request,boundary) maps record_request/v0.2 ops ram_start, ram_stop, screenshot, and disk_start onto capture methods. Unknown ops, bad max_fps 1..120, or wrong ring_bytes fall through to unsupported_at refusal path.

capture_frame_at(now_ns,frame,pixels) is the per-frame ingest path. It first runs lazy export recovery, ignores frames with no active recording, and otherwise forwards verified frames or journals a dropped marker on oversize failure without disabling rendering.

capture_transition collects live surfaces, calls capture.prepare, journals {method,request,reply,transitions} via capture_journal retain plus apply_with_witnesses, swaps in next state, and returns reply plus events for publication.

capture_export_to journals export-started durably before publication, then publishes the archive transactionally and journals export completion. On success it commits publication; completion witnesses carry digest and byte count, never a pathname.

After frames or wire transitions, capture_publish_states sends capture.state to all connected UI peers for affected recording rows, and capture_metadata wraps CAPTURE_REPLY detail as bounded JSON inside surface_event/v0.2 error events.

Recording lifecycle is start active recording, accumulate frames and dropped markers, then stop to sealed recording with frames, duration, sha256, dropped_frames. Duplicate recordStart returns ALREADY_RECORDING; unknown ids and surfaces are refused.

Export states are started durable, published file, completed or recovered. Restart scans events 1..core_seq for export-started without matching export, re-runs recover on host_destination plus receipt, and journals export with recovered true exactly once via exports_recovered flag.

RAM captures expire on process restart while snapshots and journaled metadata replay identically. Oversize or unavailable frames never disable authority rendering; active recordings journal a dropped marker and keep recording.

Export transaction id is monotonic and equals pre-export core_seq plus one. Failed export-started still advances core_seq; recovery and next export continue increasing, so tx1 < tx_fail < tx_crash < tx2 holds.

Non-list requests must have exact key sets in order, schema capture_request/v1, printable request_id length 1..64, valid surface or recording id, mode ai for recordStart, and destination null or recording:configured for export, else invalid capture shape.

ram_start requires ring_bytes exactly 8388608 and max_fps 1..120; disk_start never starts a disk recorder, it only exports an already sealed capture. Core independently checks MV_RECORDING_DESTINATION against destination_path and recording:configured capability.

Journal maps reply ok false with BUDGET_EXCEEDED to Refusal::BudgetExceeded and other failures to Refusal::Policy, else Input::SurfaceNotice. Every transition and export start or completion is retained as a witness under events and artifacts.

If destination missing or request destination is not recording:configured, plan yields DESTINATION_UNSET and only completion is journaled. Unknown capture yields CAPTURE_UNKNOWN; missing path yields DESTINATION_UNAVAILABLE with two seq steps; existing archive yields DESTINATION_EXISTS.

If disk_start fps exceeds MAX_FPS for a non-sealed id, authority applies Refuse BudgetExceeded and refuse_at answers the wire. Wrong ring_bytes, bad fps, or unknown surface op returns unsupported POLICY verdict instead of reaching capture logic.

When frame_verified fails during active recording, code calls drop_frame for the surface and journals {capture_frame:dropped} with record_event dropped, dropped_frames 1, policy ram_ring_oldest. With no active recording an oversize frame journals nothing.

If the artifact journal directory is replaced by a file, capture_export_to errors before publication and no archive appears. On recovery, matching digest completes with ok true; altered bytes are removed and completion is ok false code CAPTURE_UNAVAILABLE. Temp .mv-export files are reclaimed.

What the user sees: UI shows capture error or stale capture.state rows, or export reply says ok false with DESTINATION_UNSET, CAPTURE_UNKNOWN, DESTINATION_UNAVAILABLE, DESTINATION_EXISTS, or CAPTURE_UNAVAILABLE. Cause is refusal, grant mismatch, or interrupted export awaiting lazy recovery at next capture call.

Tests run sealed-list and host-capture suites concurrently in threads in the same process using unique 0700 temp roots, asserting no collision and Temp cleanup on panic unwind without affecting siblings.

Limits enforced: ring_bytes must equal 8 MiB, wire max_fps 1..120 with sealed-aware MAX_FPS gate, request_id 1..64 printable ASCII, surface and recording ids validated by valid_id. Violations are refused or unsupported without state change except sequence advance.

Recovery scans all events 1..core_seq and reads named artifacts; exports_recovered makes it once per Server::open. Temp .mv-export-<name>-<tx> files are deleted on recovery whether the archive validates or not.

Export grant comes from host env MV_RECORDING_DESTINATION plus opaque recording:configured token inherited from operator setting. Start witnesses keep host_destination locally; no pathname enters UI replies, only receipt id, sha256, and bytes.

Depends on authority retain_witness and apply_with_witnesses for events and artifacts under root, capture prepare/frame_verified/drop_frame/export_plan/publish_transaction state machine, and record::capture::export::recover for crash completion.

layout.rs owns slot placement: a slot is the surface ID or its kit DOM ID cuk-ai-slot-<surface_id>, including its attached terminal. Layout never creates, stops, or rebinds terminal sessions; move and tab target a group plus index, not another capsule ID.

slot_surface(slot) resolves a slot token to its surface identity. Exact surface IDs and destroyed tombstones win unchanged; otherwise the cuk-ai-slot- prefix is stripped. This prevents a real ID that starts with the prefix from rebinding.

placement_change(sid,value) computes the next Placement from current state plus an op without mutating stored state. Accepted ops are hide, show, move, tab, float, fold, unfold, subject to hidden guards; anything else returns LAYOUT_ILLEGAL_TRANSITION.

layout_refusal(env,boundary,code) handles a refused layout intent: it records unsupported, then sends a surface_event/v0.2 error to the sender with surface_id from params slot_id, code, and detail equal to request_id.

States are visible versus hidden plus optional position. hide only applies when visible, show only when hidden, move/tab/float only when visible and store the intent as position, fold/unfold only when visible with no position change; all other combos are illegal.

Human and shared authority is WRITE for placement while agent authority is READ. Accepted intents are published unchanged by core and replayed from committed witnesses, so the stored position value equals the requested intent value.

Refusal flow converts env.body to a value, calls unsupported with the witness boundary, then emits SurfaceEvent error carrying slot_id, refusal code, and request_id detail back to env.from. No placement state is changed.

Illegal transitions include show when already visible, hide when already hidden, any move/tab/float/fold/unfold while hidden, and unknown op strings. Result is Err LAYOUT_ILLEGAL_TRANSITION and the caller follows the layout refusal path.

What the user sees: a move, hide, show, or fold action does nothing and a surface error appears for that slot with LAYOUT_ILLEGAL_TRANSITION. Cause here is acting on a hidden slot or repeating the current visibility state.
Depends on ToolState has_surface and is_destroyed_surface for identity resolution, placements map for current Placement, and parent Server send plus unsupported for witness-backed refusal reporting.

Prefix stripping is order-sensitive: checking exact and destroyed identities first avoids hijacking a real surface whose name begins with cuk-ai-slot-. A destroyed exact ID retires as a tombstone instead of rebinding to another surface.

Server is the single serialization point for authority transitions and publication. It owns Authority journal, ReplayTable, peer Connection queues, observers and subscribe state, human_inputs pendings, ToolState, capture host and frame timings.

Config.validate requires core plus exactly one agent and one daemon registration, rejects duplicate or unsupported endpoints, and builds HandshakePolicy per peer. Server.open rejects unsafe session_id characters and recovered session mismatch before using state_dir.

Depends on admission Authority, CoreState, Frame, Surface and Input, journal Witness and VerifiedPixels, wire payload FrameRef, Hello, SurfaceEvent and SurfaceState, transport read/write_frame, record capture Host, plus layout, timings and tools modules for policy and retention.

Entry via bind then serve accept loop spawning connection tasks. connection_with_liveness verifies peer credential, enforces handshake deadline, replays hello through a socket pair for HandshakePolicy checks, rejects already-connected endpoints, journals daemon Connect, and replies Hello.

Outbound flow tags core envelopes with serial, msg_id, ts_ns and nonce, self-validates with decode_envelope, then try_send on bounded peer queue. fanout_at sends to Ui peers and observers, filtered per surface by subscriptions versus unsubscribed entries.

Frame witnesses are admitted only from regular non-symlink /dev/shm files bounded to 64 MiB with matching owner, zero group/other mode bits, expected length and lowercase hex sha256. Anchored open pins each directory with O_NOFOLLOW|O_DIRECTORY via /proc/self/fd and triple-checks dev and ino before and after read.
