User sees radios disabled until ready and verified, a density readout, a wall fps line like 30 requested with actual or placeholder, and a typed refusal row with fixed copy on save or apply failure. Malformed stored text silently uses defaults.

Recording fps field strictly parses trimmed integer strings, clamps to 1..60, and schedules persistence. Empty or non-integer input silently reverts the field to the current value with no save and no visible error.
Actual wall fps comes from a sliding-window meter over frame_ref.ts_ns notices on framesPort. Each notice pushes the timestamp, updates the readout, and re-arms a single decay timer one window out.

At most one fps decay timeout is ever pending. The decay callback re-reads the meter and re-arms for the remaining window when a sample is still inside, so a stale rate never lingers. Teardown never throws.
Frames subscription holds a single stop function; resubscribe and unmount call it defensively. Missing or throwing subscribeFrames leaves the panel running with a placeholder actual readout.

Settings objects must carry string scheme/density and numeric wallFps/recordingFps. Equality compares all four fields; non-objects are never equal. Guards prevent persisting partial or unchanged payloads.

Hidden live sessions field accepts non-negative whole numbers; blank or invalid input shows Enter a non-negative whole number. The previous limit is still active. Valid input updates the injected hiddenSessionSettings.

Live theme goes through capsule-ui-kit setKitScheme inside applyLive, which returns false instead of throwing. Density application and wall cadence belong to parent and host; panel only saves the request.

settingsHost.js adapts the injected preload host to the HostSettingsPort. It prefers host loadSettings/saveSettings when present and falls back to kit Storage only when the matching method is absent. Fixture schemes stay in memory.

Entry is createSettingsHostImpl(host, storage, fixtureScheme): partial host plus Storage plus optional fixture scheme. Returns loadSettings/saveSettings pair. Static decodeStoredSettings rides on the factory for the boot parser.

Fallback is per-method: absent loadSettings reads kit scheme and density preferences and synthesizes wall and recording defaults; absent saveSettings validates then writes scheme only. A host rejection never triggers fallback.

Fallback load normalizes legacy light/dark to mv-light/mv-dark, validates density, and encodes a full four-key object. Fallback save decodes the JSON, then writes only the scheme key, failing when storage is null or the write fails.

Invalid save payload throws the decoded coded error; null storage or failed write throws ERR_SETTINGS_SAVE_FAILED. Fixture host records text in memory with load/save call logging and always resolves true on save.

Both directions run through the closed four-key definition, so saves validate every field and loads fall back per field. Fallback persists exactly one storage key per the host feature-detection contract.
User with no preload sees scheme and density restored from local preferences and wall/recording at defaults. A failed local write surfaces as Settings could not be saved on the host downstream.
Depends on capsule-ui-kit SettingsModel readStoredSetting, writeStoredSetting, SETTINGS_STORAGE_KEYS and on local settingsModel decode, encode, density helpers. No direct localStorage access.

Fallback saves only the scheme key, so density, wall and recording choices made while the host is absent are lost on reload. Mixed host with only one method splits persistence across host and Storage.
Fixture mode is selected by a non-null fixtureScheme string and builds a closed four-key payload with MV_DENSITY and default fps values. It isolates tests from both host and Storage.

settingsModel.js owns the closed four-key settings definition scheme, density, wallFps, recordingFps with defaults, decode, encode, host store, debounce runner, wall fps meter, refusal mapping, and DOM id and anchor builders. Pure JavaScript, zero imports.

decodeMvSettings accepts an object or JSON text in canonical keys only. Missing keys take defaults. Unknown keys, unknown scheme, density or fps, malformed text, and float or exponent fps lexemes like 30.0 or 3e1 refuse with coded errors.

decodeStoredSettings refuses the whole payload on unknown keys and float fps lexemes so store and boot fall back to full defaults. Invalid values of known keys fall back per value, so a valid scheme survives an invalid density and vice versa.

parseSettingsText captures raw fps number lexemes via the JSON.parse reviver context source, counting only top-level holder entries. Nested objects cannot poison the reading and string values cannot fool it. Missing source refuses strictly.

Closed sets are schemes mv-light/mv-dark, densities compact/comfortable, wall presets 3/30/60, recording integers 1..60. Defaults are mv-light, compact, wall 30, recording 3. Encoded saves carry exactly four keys in canonical order.

encodeMvSettings strict-encodes only valid settings to canonical JSON and throws the coded decode error otherwise. Host store save then requires an exact true acknowledgement or raises ERR_SETTINGS_SAVE_FAILED.

createHostSettingsStore validates the host eagerly, requiring both loadSettings and saveSettings. Load of null resolves defaults; non-string storage throws malformed; unknown-key or float-lexeme storage throws so callers use full defaults.

Stored-text failures malformed, unknown key, scheme, density, wall or recording fps fall back silently to defaults. Transport and host failures stay loud as typed refusals. Host text never reaches the screen.

Refusals map to fixed literals: host unavailable, stored settings unreadable with defaults in use, scheme could not be applied, could not be saved. Unknown codes collapse to save-failed. Raw error text is never shown.

User sees Stored settings are unreadable; defaults are in use when stored text is bad, Settings host is unavailable when wiring fails, and save or apply lines on write failure. Bad stored values silently keep valid fields.

createDebouncedRunner runs the first call synchronously, collapses within-window calls to one trailing last-value call, and exposes cancel, pending and pendingValue. Cancel drops the trailing call on unmount or host replacement.

Wall fps meter admits only non-negative safe-integer frame_ref.ts_ns values, records arrival clocks, prunes outside MV_WALL_FPS_WINDOW_MS 2000, and reads arrivals per second or null when empty. msUntilEmpty schedules decay past the inclusive edge.
Readout formats as N requested, X.X actual with one decimal, or placeholder -- when the window is empty. Unknown requested values normalize to the default preset, never an error.
Save burst window is 150 ms: first change writes immediately plus at most one trailing write. Fps window is 2000 ms. Both bound host writes and memory; encoded payloads are fixed-shape and tiny.
Stable DOM ids and semantic anchors cover the panel, scheme, density, wall fps, recording fps, actual readout, and refusal rows plus per-option radios, for agent_lane/v1 selection and testing.

Normalizers return the value when known else a fallback, defaulting to primary scheme, compact density, wall 30, recording 3. Recording fallback itself validates so an invalid fallback cannot leak through.
createMemorySettingsHost is the in-memory host double for tests: it records load and save calls, holds text in memory, and resolves true on save. No Storage or network is involved.

A fps number that parses as an integer but was written with a fraction or exponent refuses the whole load. Editors that serialize 30 as 30.0 therefore reset all settings to defaults rather than keeping the scheme.

RoleSurface.vue hosts one capsule tile and owns its native role view: it mounts, resizes, hides/shows and revokes the view through globalThis.metaviewerRoles, driven by tile geometry, modal state and control mode.

Operator entries are the tile menu (Switch mode, Mark as logged in, Watch read-only, Move desktop, Stop, Take control), the Reopen button after error, and the reconnect button after resource release; all funnel into lifecycle(), confirmLogin(), sync() or revoke().

Geometry entries are mount status fetch, 100 ms sync timer, window pointermove/resize listeners, capture-phase scroll listeners on window/document/ancestors/shell-wall, and a MutationObserver on body data-mv-modal; each calls sync().

sync() reads root.getBoundingClientRect(), collects scroll ancestors and wall viewport, computes baseClip via clipRoleBounds(), subtracts floating occluders, then calls api.mount/resize/visibility/raise with the surviving rectangle.

floatingPresentation() enumerates .dv-resize-container floats with nonzero rect and visible style, walks up to 64 ancestors for max zIndex, maps a dv-render-overlay-float portal to its container at portalZ-1, and returns front flag plus occluder rects above own tile.

View states: closed, connecting, ready, error, reconnecting. Flags: mounted, shown, busy/resync, ended/notifiedEnd, alive, resourceReleased, error, progress. wanted() is role human, or agent plus watching plus control agent; not-wanted revokes.

Temporary clipping, docking and window visibility must not revoke the authenticated session: when not visible but mounted, sync() calls api.visibility(id,false) and retains the connection instead of revoke(); only wanted()==false or errors revoke.

Host contract is globalThis.metaviewerRoles: status(surfaceId) returns role/view.state/view.code/view.recording, plus mount/resize/visibility/raise/close/confirmLogin/switchMode/stop and onFocus. Missing api leaves role agent with no mount and header teleported only when api and role exist.

clipRoleBounds() intersects tile rect with window viewport (innerWidth/Height or override) and every scroll/wall clip, then ceil/floor quantizes; visible requires width>=1 and height>=1, else bounds zeroed. Non-finite inputs yield null rect and skipped clips.

If status.ok===false throw XPRA_REFUSED; if view.state error throw view.code; if visibility/resize/mount reply !ok throw reply.code. Catch sets error.message or XPRA_REFUSED and awaits revoke(), which closes host view and resets mounted/signature/viewState.

User sees Connecting... before mount or when connecting, Reconnecting... when reconnecting after a prior connect, Human capsule or Read-only watch when live, Recording paused (size limit) badge, or error text with a Reopen button that clears error and retries sync().

lifecycle() blocks while busy, sets progress Switching to... or Stopping capsule..., awaits revoke(), emits lifecycle with completion promise for the persistent parent, then awaits it; !ok throws code into error. Reveal emits before stopped because pane close can unmount this component and suppress later emits.

sync() is single-flight: busy sets resync flag for re-entry, finally clears busy and re-runs sync() once when resync and alive and no end/error/progress. Signature JSON of bounds skips duplicate resize; mount vs resize chosen by mounted flag with attaching viewState connecting.

Geometrically hidden live views enter hiddenSessions pool via update(id,geometricallyShown,releaseHiddenSession,isGeometricallyShown); modal occlusion does not enter. Pool eviction calls releaseHiddenSession(), which sets resourceReleased and revokes; reconnect button clears flag and syncs.

bindScrollListeners() clears prior scrollCleanups, subscribes capture scroll on window/document/ancestors/wall and modal-attribute observer; onBeforeUnmount removes pointerdown/pointermove/resize listeners, clears interval, drains cleanups, and revokes unless transferring to another tile.

Painted requires nonempty getClientRects and computed style not hidden/collapse/none, so Dockview inactive tabs with nonempty rects stay session-retained but native-hidden. Modal active is body data-mv-modal attribute/dataset/props; visible requires geometricallyShown and clipped.visible and no modal.

collectClipRects() walks at most 64 parents to body/html, skips root-tag nodes without getBoundingClientRect, breaks at resize-container/overlay-float when floating, takes shell-wall or wall-workspace rect as wallViewport, else pushes ancestors with scroll/clip/auto overflow; falls back to getElementById shell-wall.

subtractRoleOccluders() returns hidden with zero width when occluders exceed 64, when split pieces exceed 256 or vanish, or when surviving area differs from bounding box (native views paint one rectangle only, so L/T/R/B splits must exactly tile).

Depends on injected overlayCoordinator (menuOpen synced via overlays.set with sync flush), hiddenSessionPool, and tileLayoutActions for resize/move/desktops/transfers/focus. Menu popover uses showPopover with source button and hides on :popover-open mismatch or outside pointerdown.

Malformed trees or cycles cannot spin: ancestor walks stop at 64 entries or seen-set repeat. Desktop move failure sets Desktop move is unavailable. Overlapping floats above the tile silently shrink the native bounds to hidden rather than misaligning paint.

SurfaceCanvas.vue is one wall tile: it hosts the live canvas element plus a read-only frame/generation/digest witness strip. The frame prop is an opaque scheduler handle; pixel bytes never enter Vue reactivity and drawing happens only inside a scheduler turn.

Router onRegistered pins delivery identity (surfaceGeneration/epoch) into registeredIdentity; later attaches use that verbatim, never projection generation/epoch props. A new delivery identity drops retained witness and FPS state; re-attach reclaims the scheduler canvas binding.

resolvedState normalizes state, forces lost, maps display active to live and display stale to stale, and degrades live-without-handle to connecting. Lost with retained handle shows frozen frame plus Lost badge; witness strip renders only for live/stale.

Scheduler contract: attachCanvas({surfaceId,surfaceGeneration,epoch,canvas}) returns ok/token, detachCanvas, getInstrumentation, evictSurface, subscribePresentation. bindToken symbol scopes unbind so wall and multislot tiles sharing surfaceId do not remove each other.

Evict runs only when router reports no stream and entry has no canvas and shouldEvictSchedulerEntry agrees; legacy path without router is a no-op. Unmount unbinds with keepStream true, checks now and again after 1200 ms past the 500 ms router grace; rebound streams skip both.

User sees Connecting to surface when live is claimed without a handle, Waiting for surface for empty, Lost plus No frames were presented without a frame, or Lost plus Showing the last frame with frozen bitmap when a witness exists.

Human input enters only when inputEnabled plus available inputPort plus canvas focus plus not lost. Key/click/scroll map through frameMap and queue on the port with streamId; Escape blurs and emits canvas-escape and is never forwarded.

pointerdown and click always preventDefault so a tile press never scrolls the page in any mode; non-focusable canvas still takes no focus and queues nothing. Contextmenu/auxclick are prevented only when canvasFocusable; letterbox and zero-delta wheels keep page scroll.

Latest gated pointerdown arms activePress {pointerId,button,inFrame}; cancel or gate close clears it. pointerup queues one click only for matching id/button started inside frame; other buttons ignored; no pointer-move forwarding.

Every gate closure (blur, inputEnabled off, READ switch, lost, stream/surface change, unmount) calls port.closeGate and drops queued input so it never dispatches later or replays; ports predating closeGate are skipped silently. Blur also clears activePress and echo dot.

Client-to-frame mapping uses paint-owned canvas.width/height with letterbox removal, never projection frameWidth/Height props; mapper failure fails closed with null. Canvas intrinsic size is owned by scheduler paint; no reactive width/height binding may clear a painted frame.

FPS counts only painted frames where presentCount/lastPresentedHandle advanced, over a 2000 ms window with footer refresh at most twice per second; capture_us arrives via paint hint, captureUs/frameRef props, or authority subscribeFrames, and never counts a frame by itself.

Footer shows FPS: count and CAP: ms, or em dash placeholder when the window is empty or capture is absent; a stall timer re-flushes to placeholder once the newest paint ages past the window. Text updates never cost frames.

Click echo is optional: failed pointerEcho import leaves capture working with no dot. Dot draws only at in-frame points through the same contain transform, hides on strictly newer inputTimestampMs or 1000 ms TTL or gate closure; echo faults never break input or paint.

Enabling input focuses canvas with preventScroll unless typing in another field; losing the gate blurs. Lost tiles never focus (no tabindex) and detach scheduler binding while keeping the frozen bitmap; mounting already lost releases the binding synchronously.

Gated-in tiles are WRITE-capable so the strip omits READ-ONLY; all other states render as before. Lost tiles render Lost badge with strip suppressed except panel badge; aria names and anchors derive from tileScheduler helpers.
fpsMeter.js is the pure painted-frame rate and capture-duration meter for a tile: sliding-window FPS plus latest frame_ref.capture_us formatting, with injected clock and no DOM access.
Window is 2000 ms, display refresh at most twice per second (500 ms), placeholder em dash when the window has no painted frames. All three are unit decisions exported for tests.

recordPaint stamps clock(), ingests capture_us from number or capture_us/captureUs/frame_ref.capture_us, pushes timestamp and prunes; recordReceived and recordCaptureUs update capture only so dropped frames never inflate FPS.

Snapshot prunes to half-open (now-windowMs,now] with 1e-6 tolerance, fps rounded count*1000/windowMs or null, capture shown only when window nonempty or nothing ever painted; stall returns both as placeholder. read() is live, readThrottled() cached.

normalizeCaptureMs accepts only non-negative safe integers, returning rounded ms or null; formatCaptureUs renders <n> ms or placeholder. extractCaptureUs returns null for non-objects or invalid values.

Invalid clock, windowMs or interval fall back to performance.now/Date.now, 2000 and 500 respectively. msUntilStall returns 0 with no paints else time until newest paint exits window; msUntilNextUpdate returns 0 when due.
Consumer sees fpsText/captureText as numbers or em dash; after a stall longer than the window both read placeholder, and capture alone arriving cannot revive FPS text without a paint.

frameTile.js bridges one brokered port to one canvas: it owns the admitted binding, budgets and presentation eligibility, keeping frame bytes in closure and ACKing only after scheduler release, fold drain or refusal.

onFrame rejects duplicate leaseId with REFUSED, submits to scheduler, records capture witness for admitted or FOLDED_DISPLAY_DISABLED folds, and resolves pending on onReleaseLease outcome; unadmitted non-fold deletes pending and returns REFUSED immediately.
registerSurface failure throws Error(reason). Port onRevoke destroys the scheduler surface. close() revokes with SHUTDOWN, destroys scheduler, and resolves all pending leases as SURFACE_DESTROYED.

Scheduler identity check stays intact: registered with binding plus state, presented via onPresent to presentHandle. The port verifies shape while submitFrame checks identity before folded refusal; valid folded captures still advance the reopen floor.
hiddenSessions.js caps retained native sessions for geometrically hidden live views so background tiles keep connections without unbounded cost; modal occlusion never enters.
Default limit 4; constructor and setLimit reject non-safe-integer or negative with HIDDEN_SESSION_LIMIT_INVALID. API: update(id,shown,release,isShown?), remove(id), size, limit, setLimit.

Entries keyed by id store shown/release/lastShown; clock bumps only when a tile transitions to shown. prune() sorts hidden entries (shown false and isShown() false) by lastShown and releases oldest beyond limit via release().

Over-limit eviction deletes oldest hidden entry then calls its release callback, which the caller wires to revoke and resource-release UI. Visible entries never evict; remove() drops without releasing.
Pool holds only callbacks and timestamps in a Map, no timers; memory bounded by visible plus at most limit hidden entries. Limit 0 means every hidden tile releases immediately on next update.
overlayCoordinator.js counts independent overlay owners so removing one menu never uncovers native views while another is open; body data-mv-modal=open mirrors owners.size>0.

observeOverlays scans role dialog/menu/listbox, details[open], data-state open, and popover; sets shared owner true when any has rects and visible style. MutationObserver plus pointerdown/keydown/beforetoggle/toggle/change/focusout keep it live; cleanup disconnects and clears owners.

Dockview floats (dialog plus dv-resize-container without aria-modal true) and sidebar nav menus (menu inside aside/nav/navigation) are excluded so modeless floats never hide their own native view and idle nav never occludes everything. Closed popovers are ignored.

API: set(owner,open) adds/removes owner object identity and syncs attribute; count; dispose() clears and syncs. Native popover/details toggles track per-element owners and prune disconnected nodes; SELECT open sets selectOwner until change/focusout/pointer-away/Escape/Enter/Tab.

Without body or MutationObserver returns a no-op cleanup. Missing getClientRects/visibility data simply fails the painted test so the overlay does not claim occlusion. Listener faults cannot occur inline; dispose path always clears all three owner classes.
pointerEcho.js draws a local click dot at the last human click so the operator sees input land before the capsule repaints; pure logic with no DOM, injected clock and timers for deterministic tests.
Dot lifetime 1000 ms without an answering frame and diameter 12 CSS px are unit decisions. At most one dot exists; last click wins and replaces any dot on screen.

echoPointFromClient delegates null-ness to mapClientToFrame so echo can never draw where a click is refused, then derives sub-pixel fx/fy via containFit scale/offsets. echoPlacement re-applies the same contain transform to canvas-box CSS px; null on bad sizes or out-of-frame points.

show() validates finite fx/fy, stamps now(), arms TTL timer (unref when available) and emits onChange show; observeFrame hides only on strictly newer inputTimestampMs; clear/dispose hide with cause; disposed refuses later shows.

frameInputTimestampMs recovers originating input time as timingScopes.presentationMs minus inputToPresentMs; null when instrumentation missing, figures non-finite, or sinceInput negative. Frames without timestamps never hide the dot.

Invalid show points return false with no state change. Broken setTimer still shows (frame or gate closure hides later); broken clearTimer or onChange listener never breaks input. Timer handle is nulled on fire before hide ttl.

Operator sees a dot at the click for up to one second; it vanishes early when the repainted frame answers the click, or immediately on blur/control loss/READ/surface change via clear(gate). Letterbox clicks never draw.
presentationServices.js installs renderer services through the entry/runtime seam: hidden session pool, overlay coordinator plus observer, and a persisted hidden-limit setting.

Limit reads preferences mv.hiddenLiveSessionLimit; absent uses default 4. Malformed stored value throws HIDDEN_SESSION_LIMIT_INVALID. Settings set() validates safe-integer >=0, persists string, and calls pool.setLimit.

Provides overlayCoordinator, hiddenSessionPool and hiddenSessionSettings via application.provide; onUnmount stops overlay observation and disposes coordinator so body attribute clears. No other teardown is owned here.

tileScheduler.js implements a fair newest-only wall-tile scheduler. Submission never draws; each surface holds one newest mailbox slot, a tick consumes it into a presented slot and fires metadata-only onPresent, and the wall draws via presentHandle reentrantly during that turn.

createTileScheduler(options) builds the registry; registerSurface(config) binds immutable identity principal plus epoch plus surfaceGeneration plus capture lease. Same-generation plus same-epoch re-register keeps canvas and pending paint; newer generation drains display and trims warm resources.

submitFrame(frame) is the only frame ingress. It validates binding, generation floors, lease liveness, packed RGB shape, aggregate byte cap and eligibility, then replaces the single mailbox slot newest-wins. It never draws and emits SUPERSEDED for the displaced slot.

runTick([targetSurfaceId]) executes one coordinated fair tick over a snapshot of surfaceOrder. It checks eligibility, lease expiry, staleness and frozen aggregate draws plus bytes plus present-ms, presents at most budget, and freezes the result record.

presentHandle({surfaceId,handle}) is the only draw path. It is valid only while insideTurn is true, only for the owning live surface, only for the current presented handle, and only with a canvas attached. Unknown, foreign, retired or mismatched handles refuse closed.

attachCanvas({surfaceId,canvas,[surfaceGeneration,epoch]}) binds one active canvas per surface, replacing prior attachment; generation or epoch mismatch refuses. detachCanvas(surfaceId,token) unbinds only when the symbol token matches, so stale unmounts are no-ops.

Frame bytes flow as owned tightly packed top-left RGB24 by reference from submitFrame mailbox to presented slot to canvas. convertRgb24ToRgba expands to opaque RGBA; little-endian aligned outputs use one Uint32 store per pixel, otherwise the reference byte loop, bit-identical.

drawRgb24ToCanvas resizes canvas to frame size, reuses entry.presentScratch only on exact byte length plus same dimensions plus full RGBA backing, else creates fresh ImageData and retains it. Short or over-long inputs always allocate fresh, preserving prefix semantics.

normalizeSurfaceState maps unknown input to empty, never fake-live; known states are live, connecting, lost, empty. canvasStateForRow maps backendLifecycle lost to frozen lost view, else attachment live to live and everything else to connecting; destroyed or detached rows never yield lost.

Fold, hide, and context-loss stop only the display branch: mailbox plus presented drain with explicit causes and warm resources trim, while capture lease stays active and capture witnesses advance. Unfold and restore raise minAdmissibleFrameGen above every witness floor and request newest generation; hidden backlog never replays.

updateSurfaceState accepts only presentation geometry and visibility patches. Patches containing folded or contextLost refuse with INVALID_BINDING so they cannot bypass drain accounting; hidden transitions drain display with HIDDEN. It returns eligibility plus box plus capture retention.

Destroyed ids stay tombstoned and revival refuses SURFACE_DESTROYED; evicted ids leave no tombstone and stay re-registerable. Eviction is only for fully retired canvas-less entries with streamRetired true and canvasAttached not true, else a live stream would strand with no entry.

Budget must be a frozen object with exactly maxDrawsPerTick, maxUploadBytesPerTick, maxPresentMsPerTick, maxWarmResourcesPerSurface, maxDrainSteps. Unknown, missing, or out-of-range limits refuse INVALID_BUDGET; constructor throws on invalid budget.

Eligibility requires panel open plus selected, unfolded, positive rounded size, viewport intersection, window permission, and live context. Any failure returns eligible false with frozen reason codes and box null; only fully eligible surfaces receive a frozen rounded content box.

DOM and QA anchors never carry raw host ids. Valid alnum-lead segments of at most 64 chars pass through byte-identical; anything else maps to a deterministic lead plus sanitized rest plus fnv1a32 suffix of at most 61 chars, keeping capsule slash grammar whitespace and slash free.

Surface size resolves from Width and Height variants or geometry, defaulting to 1280 by 900 with matching aspect token. computeTileContentBox packs one to many capsules into columns and rows, reserves the 23 px witness strip, and reports cell size plus strip visibility plus zero offsets.

Submit refusal always releases the candidate lease once as REFUSED, HIDDEN, CONTEXT_LOST, or SUPERSEDED for displaced mailboxes. Stale generation, binding mismatch, folded display, expired or missing lease, RGB shape mismatch, over-budget bytes, and hidden state each return their closed reason; folded advances the admissible floor.

Tick drops ineligible mailboxes with HIDDEN drain, and stale or expired candidates with REFUSED drain plus rejectedStaleFrames count. Over-budget candidates defer with budgetDeferrals and preserve priority via retry cursor. A present with no successful draw witness retires its handle, releases REFUSED, and retains canvas-less frames as pendingPaint.

Present outside a coordinated turn refuses INVALID_BINDING. Unknown handles refuse unknown-handle, foreign handles refuse SURFACE_MISMATCH, retired or non-current handles refuse STALE_FRAME_GENERATION. Missing canvas or failed 2d context refuses without advancing lastPresentedFrameGen.

Retained replays obey the same eligibility fence as submit and tick: ineligible attach still stands but skips drawing and both retained slots survive. Canvas-less pendingPaint paints on any eligible attach and becomes witness; lastPaint repaints only on a genuinely different element, never on same-element reattach.

User-visible words come from accessible names such as Live surface, Surface connecting, Surface lost, No surface, Capsule input, and Capsule lost: showing the last frame, plus the witness strip READ-ONLY ISOLATED EXECUTION and shortened digest head-ellipsis-tail. A failed tile shows black or frozen last frame with the Lost badge.

When hidden, folded, context-lost, over budget, or mailbox-empty, immediate present and tick return HIDDEN_SURFACE, FOLDED_DISPLAY_DISABLED, CONTEXT_LOST, BUDGET_EXHAUSTED, or EMPTY_MAILBOX with disqualifiers. The wall then shows no new pixels; instrumentation exposes eligible, box, pending and presented generations, and counters.

Ticks are reentrant-coordinated via insideTurn: onPresent or default presentHandle runs inside the same turn. Scan order starts at fairCursor over a snapshot so observer destroys cannot shift membership; nextCursor advances past each draw, with retryCursor preserving priority for temporarily deferred fittable frames.

Warm resources are bounded per surface; allocation requires resourceId plus non-negative byteLength plus native disposer, and eviction calls each disposer exactly once counting disposerFaults. Any eviction drops lastPaint and pendingPaint as the largest idle holdings. Drain releases mailbox plus presented exactly once under one cause.

Each display lease releases exactly once via onReleaseLease with principal, epoch, surface and frame generations, leaseId, cause, and clock timestamp. Retired handles stay in a one-per-surface map so later draws fail closed as stale; live map owns only currently drawable handles.

recordCaptureWitness requires strictly increasing captureGeneration per surface generation and counts captures; folded witnesses also raise the admissible floor. Admission without explicit cost uses the measured moving average clamped to tick budget and never below the 1 ms default; non-positive samples leave it untouched.

The module re-exports mapKeyboardEvent and mapClientToFrame from input keyMap and frameMap so SurfaceCanvas keeps a closed SFC dependency map. Input focus anchor tile-segment-input-focus and Lost badge anchor tile-segment-lost-badge derive from the same sanitized segment grammar.

Presentation observers, onPresent, onReleaseLease, canvas repaint, and disposer faults are swallowed and counted, never restoring retired ownership. Timing scopes record submission, parser consumption, and presentation stamps with verifiedDomainEffect left null; destroy clears registry and listeners but notifies first.
BrokerLaunchControls.vue provides the terminal opt-in checkbox and provider launch buttons. It drives an injected host broker through a cached facade, showing pending and outcome status rows.

SideTerminalOverlay.vue hosts the right-side terminal overlay above tiles with display:contents so tiles never reflow. It pairs launch controls with the kit SideTerminalPanel bound to an injected session port.

Control arrives via props broker, providers, idPrefix, anchorPrefix, visible, showMenu. broker maps through createSideTerminalBrokerFacade to facade; providers map through toKitMenuProviders to entries with empty fallback.

Overlay arrives via terminalBroker, terminalBinding {session,port}, hostProviders, open, deck, storage, topOffset, bottomOffset. rebind converts terminalBinding into facadeRef or an empty-state facade.

launch(entry) calls broker.open with command 80x24 and copied argv, empty for shell. Success sets outcome TERMINAL_OPENED; stale or disabled sessions are closed best-effort. Errors project TERMINAL_UNAVAILABLE or TERMINAL_LAUNCH_REFUSED.
Host provider data flows through toKitMenuProviders in both files. Malformed host data falls back to shell-only menu, so the menu never throws into the view.

providerAnchorSegment returns a grammar-valid anchor segment up to 61 chars. Valid ids pass through byte-identical; others map to lead plus sanitized rest plus fnv1a32 suffix. Raw id stays for host resolution.

States: enabled from facade state, busy from facade busy or launching, launching during open, outcome code. Overlay bindingState is TERMINAL_UNAVAILABLE, TERMINAL_ATTACHED, or TERMINAL_BINDING_REFUSED.
Enable checkbox is reset to enabled.value in finally so the view never shows an unacknowledged opt-in. Launch buttons stay disabled while busy or when opt-in is required but not enabled.
If setEnabled throws, outcome becomes TERMINAL_ENABLE_REFUSED with message Terminal access is unavailable. The checkbox is forced back to the authoritative enabled value.

If open throws containing TERMINAL_UNAVAILABLE, outcome is TERMINAL_UNAVAILABLE: terminal support is not bundled in this package. Otherwise outcome is TERMINAL_LAUNCH_REFUSED: This terminal launch is unavailable.
Null binding yields TERMINAL_UNAVAILABLE plus empty facade; constructor throw yields TERMINAL_BINDING_REFUSED plus empty facade. Kit panel then shows designed empty state, not exception text.
User sees greyed Enable and provider buttons while starting, a Starting session status line, then Terminal session opened, Terminal access is unavailable, or This terminal launch is unavailable.
An active flag set false on unmount guards async enable and launch continuations. Late completions skip outcome writes; launches that finish after disable or facade change close the new session.
rebind disposes the prior facade best-effort before replacing it, and unmount disposes again. Overlay open state is kit-owned with persisted width; wrapper contributes no layout box.
Depends on kit SideTerminalPanel and SidebarIcon, multislot toKitMenuProviders adapter, sideTerminalFacade factories, and host broker and SHELL_COMMAND and PROVIDER_COMMAND constants.

TerminalDeckView.vue is the full-wall terminal deck workspace beside Humans and Agents. It renders screen bar, Bootstrap and New terminal actions, launcher popover, equal-tile xterm grid, context menu, and busy-close confirm.

Control arrives via open, terminalBroker, terminalBinding session facade, terminalSessionPort, hostProviders, brokerCommands, clipboard, storage, closeGraceMs. Controller is built once from those props.

syncTerminals reconciles viewportElements against controller screens: destroys unretained terminals, creates MvDeckTerminal plus FitAddon per new session, replays buffered output, resizes, and focuses the focused slot.

Tile input flows from xterm onData through controller.writeSessionBytes as encoded bytes, with Ctrl+C mapped to 0x03. Fallback onTileKeyDown forwards single chars and Enter only when no xterm is mounted.

Deck state mirrors controller.state through revision bumps: screens with slots, activeScreenIndex, focusedSlotId, pendingCloseSlotId, launcherOpen, toast, errorCode and errorMessage, gridColumns, profiles.
Context menu state holds open,x,y,slotId,hasSelection,selectionText. Right-click sets it from readSlotSelection; pointer outside, Escape, screen change, or hide closes it.
All screens stay mounted but only the active screen is visible; inactive tiles use hidden, inert, and aria-hidden. Grid column count derives from deck state and is exposed as data-grid-cols.
Copy reads xterm selection first then window selection. Copy and paste go through controller copySelection and pasteClipboard for the menu slot; copy is disabled without selection.
Bootstrap paste prefers clipboardData text, else controller.pasteClipboard result. Pasted text lands in pastedBootstrapText and data-pasted-slot-id; shortcut paste is intercepted and handled here.
launchProfile, launchCustomCli, restartSlot, bootstrap failures are swallowed locally; the message projects via deckState.errorMessage with errorCode in data-error-code and role alert.
Closing a busy slot sets pendingCloseSlotId and shows a confirm dialog stating SIGINT then terminate. Confirm closes, cancel clears. Idle slots close without the dialog path.
User sees No terminals on Screen N with Open Shell hint, bootstrap toast, terminal/error alert text, exited or restored badges on tiles, and Close busy terminal confirm copy.
User sees a right-click Copy/Paste menu at cursor position; Copy is greyed without selected text. Clicking elsewhere or pressing Escape makes it vanish.
Global capture listeners forward keys to controller.handleKeyDown and close launcher or menu on outside pointerdown. Launcher, confirm, and menu jointly drive overlayOpen for the modal attribute.
overlayOpen reflects open plus launcher, pending close, or menu. It notifies injected overlayCoordinator or toggles body data-mv-modal; unmount always clears it.
destroySlotTerminal unregisters from controller, disposes onData and terminal, and drops map entries. Hide blurs terminals; unmount destroys all and disposes controller.
MvDeckTerminal extends xterm Terminal with documentOverride from createTerminalDocument. Fit is best-effort with 80x24 fallback; failed terminal construction registers a null terminal placeholder.
Props configure storage fallback to localStorage, closeGraceMs, broker command list, and clipboard. Custom CLI input is mirrored into controller state and Launch is disabled while blank.
Depends on @xterm/xterm plus FitAddon, terminalDeckModel controller and shortcuts, capsule nonce document, terminal.css, clipboard, broker, and session port facade.
TerminalView.vue mounts one xterm session view for an injected session and MessagePort. It binds input, output, resize, and status without spawning or killing host sessions.
providers.js is a pure renderer-importable provider menu normalizer. It validates host-owned entries and builds inert reference-only rows; executable resolution and spawning stay host-side.
Input is session id, nullable port, and host element ref. bindTerminal runs on mount and on session or port change; missing port, host, or session leaves an empty section.

Terminal output flows from port through createTerminalClient write into terminal.write; input flows from onData and onBinary into client.input. ResizeObserver posts {session,cols,rows} on host size change.

createProviderMenu takes normalized entries plus host capabilities and returns frozen reference-only rows with id,label,hint,command,disabled. Shell row is always first; provider rows need positive capability.
Provider ids must match closed grammar 1..128 chars and must not be shell or provider. Unknown keys, malformed fields, duplicates, and reserved ids throw instead of filtering.
Provider argv must be 1..33 strings, no NUL, each up to 4096 UTF-8 bytes, argv[0] non-empty and not dash-led. Returns a frozen copy; violations throw TypeError or RangeError.
Custom dialog splits argument text on whitespace runs only with no quoting or shell evaluation. Empty executable, dash-led head, NUL, oversize, or over 32 items returns null argv plus message.
Shell entry keeps empty argv and command shell; host spawns its own login shell. Menu rows never carry argv, exe, cwd, or env across the boundary.
Dispose runs before each rebind and on unmount, disconnecting observer and disposing input, binary, client, and terminal. Status shows Terminal attached after bind; stale callbacks are invalidated.
Non-object records throw expected an object; byte sizes use TextEncoder so the module stays renderer-importable. Capability rows with bad id, available, or reason throw TypeError.
User sees an empty terminal host box when no port is injected, or a Terminal attached status line above the terminal once bound. No host error strings are rendered.
User sees custom-dialog messages Enter an executable, The executable must not start with a dash, Arguments must be text, Too many arguments, or size and null-byte refusals.
Each bind creates Terminal plus FitAddon and a ResizeObserver; dispose tears all down. Terminal uses allowProposedApi false and convertEol false with 120px minimum host height.
Depends on @xterm/xterm, FitAddon, xterm.css, Vue lifecycle, and terminalClient for sequence and credit handling. No filesystem, PATH, IPC, or spawn here.
sideTerminalFacade.js adapts an injected authorized session port to the kit overlay shape. It offers attach, data, exit, ack, write, resize, close, and dispose with no launch capability.
Input is {session,port}. Session must match closed id grammar and port must expose postMessage, else TERMINAL_BINDING_REFUSED. Kit calls capabilities then attach.
Terminal bytes flow from createTerminalClient write into data listeners as {session,seq,bytes,byteLength} with cumulative totals. Ack releases contiguous credits via stored done callbacks.
Every ack, write, resize, and close must name the bound session while attached; mismatched id or detached facade throws TERMINAL_BINDING_REFUSED.

Empty facade answers capabilities developerMode false and attach with zero sessions, so the kit shows designed empty state. ack, write, resize throw typed unavailable; close and setEnabled paths refuse.
Broker facade separates launch authority from port IO. Absent setEnabled means already authorized; present method must acknowledge. canEnable and canOpen reflect host method presence.
Broker facade holds reactive enabled and busy. setEnabled and open set busy, await host, then clear it. open refuses unless enabled and idle; enabled starts true when no opt-in method exists.
Pump or exit events normalize to exited or failed with typed codes TERMINAL_SESSION_EXITED or FAILED and messages Session ended or Session ended unexpectedly. Unknown shapes fail closed to failed.
copyText accepts only lead-alnum plus 0..127 of alnum . _ : -. Off-grammar text throws ERR_CLIPBOARD_INVALID before any host round-trip; host text never reaches visible strings.

createSessionTransport validates the injected window.metaviewer.sideTerminal fixed API and binds attach, resize, close, listProviders, copyText. Absent methods mean unavailable capability, never exception.

Present-but-not-callable methods throw TypeError. Bad session shapes throw SESSION_INVALID; non-literal-true resize, close, copyText replies throw REFUSED or UNAVAILABLE; malformed listings throw PROVIDERS_UNAVAILABLE.
Port facade attaches once per session via transport.attach, binds terminalClient, flushes queued inputs, then emits data and exit per session. Failed attach drops the entry and emits one exit.
Per-session entries hold port, client, seq, bytes, pending credits, queue, and in-flight attach. Writes before attach queue; late ports after close are shut and emit no exit.
Ack with unknown seq or mismatched cumulative bytes throws TERMINAL_CREDIT_REFUSED. resize without host method throws SESSION_UNAVAILABLE; bad cols and rows throw RESIZE_REFUSED.
release removes the entry, disposes client best-effort, and closes port-like objects. close forwards to host only when supplied and swallows async failures; dispose clears all sessions and listeners.
User sees Session ended for clean exits or Session ended unexpectedly for failures, with tone info or error. Typed codes travel only in data attributes, never visible text.
Depends on Vue reactive and toRaw, terminalClient boundary, and kit useKitGeometry. Broker facades are cached per source in a WeakMap; lifecycle refs derive deterministic DOM ids from capsule id.
Close and dispose only detach this view; host session ownership and process lifetime stay host-side. Double attach throws ALREADY_ATTACHED; onStatus disposes then emits exit.
No runtime config; lifecycle helper naming is deterministic from capsule id for pending, notice, and dismiss ids and anchors. Host guarantees shell in capabilities but menu does not depend on it.
terminalClient.js binds one session MessagePort to xterm read and write callbacks. Parser completion is the output-credit boundary; disposal invalidates late callbacks.
Input is {session,port,write,onStatus}. Port starts listening immediately via addEventListener plus start. Returns frozen {input,dispose}.
Inbound {session,seq,bytes} frames with strict key shape go to write(bytes,done). Contiguous parser completions advance ackSeq and consumed, then post {session,ack,bytes}.
Frames must have exact keys bytes,seq,session with Uint8Array bytes, seq received+1, length up to 65536, and under 256 pending. Violations deactivate and report Terminal stream refused.
Input posts {session,seq,bytes} with incrementing inputSeq only while active and bytes up to 65536. Oversize input is dropped silently.
States are active versus deactivated. Any session mismatch, error, exitCode, malformed frame, overflow, or dispose flips to inactive; later frames and input completions are ignored.

Frames for another session deactivate with Terminal binding refused. Error or exitCode frames deactivate with the host error or Exited (code). Retryable TERMINAL_IO_REFUSED with exact keys rewinds inputSeq.
Malformed shape, non-Uint8Array, gap, oversize chunk, or 256 pending frames deactivate with Terminal stream refused. Duplicate or late parser done callbacks are ignored.
User sees terminal output stop and a status line Terminal binding refused, Terminal stream refused, host error text, or Exited (code). No further output or input flows after that.
Output acknowledgements are cumulative and only for contiguous completed parser writes, so out-of-order completions wait. Input sequence resets only on the exact retryable refusal shape.
Pending map holds at most 256 unacked frames; dispose deactivates, clears pending, and removes the message listener. Port stays outside Vue and host owns session lifetime.
Strict exact-key checks mean any extra host field fails the stream closed. Session mismatch kills the whole client rather than skipping one frame, so cross-talk ends the view.

Owns multi-screen terminal deck state: screens, slots, focus, pending close, launcher, toasts and errors, plus broker open/close, session attach/write/resize, persistence and keyboard shortcuts for TerminalDeckView.vue.
launchProfile(profileId) opens an admitted broker profile on the active screen or reuses reuseSlotId, defaulting to 80x24 cols/rows, and marks the slot running/busy with the new sessionId.
launchCustomCli(rawCommand) opens an admitted shell session then types the trimmed single-line command plus newline into the PTY, without widening broker spawn admission.
handleKeyDown(event) consumes deck shortcuts and Escape for launcher/pending-close, calling preventDefault/stopPropagation; unmatched keys return false so PTY input and Ctrl+C pass through.

openBrokerSession enables the broker then opens {command,args,cols,rows}; attachSession binds the session via sessionFacade or a direct MessagePort facade; writeSessionBytes sends PTY input bytes through the same path.

Slot status is running while sessionId is live, exited after broker exit or close, restored after reload with busy false and sessionId null. Exit events from closingSessions are ignored to avoid double-marking during close.
Busy running slots need confirmation: confirmClose callback or pendingCloseSlotId dialog; force bypasses it. Exited/restored slots close immediately. Confirm executes close, cancel clears pending id.

serializeDeckState persists schema, activeScreenIndex, sequences and per-slot id/title/kind/profileId/customCommand only; live handles and sessionIds are never stored. deserializeDeckState rejects wrong schema, empty or over-limit envelopes with null.
Screens are always numbered 1..N with label Screen N after add/remove/load. Deserialize clamps activeScreenIndex into range and derives nextScreenSeq/nextSlotSeq above observed numeric suffixes.
Tile grid maps count to columns: 0-1 to 1, 2-4 to 2, 5-9 to 3, else 4. Non-finite counts clamp to 0, so empty screens render one column.

Unknown broker/IPC errors normalize to {code,hint,message} with message CODE: hint. Explicit code/reason wins; otherwise message tokens, phrase matches, or TERMINAL_OPEN_REFUSED fallback. Custom remedy replaces the built-in hint.
Empty, NUL-, CR- or LF-containing custom commands set COMMAND_NOT_ALLOWED with Enter a single-line command and throw before any broker open, so no session is consumed.

Broker refusal or invalid/missing session id sets errorCode/errorMessage, closes the launcher, notifies, and rethrows. Callers launchProfile/launchCustomCli repeat the formatting and keep the launcher closed.

User pastes nothing and sees toast Paste failed: clipboard read failed or target slot is not running, so pasteClipboard returns pasted false. Failure also records TERMINAL_PASTE_FAILED errorCode/message.
Bootstrap copy shows toast Copied on success or Copy unavailable when neither clipboard.writeText nor operator entry copy succeeds; it returns {ok,text,toast} with the AGENT_ENTRY_PROMPT text.
Copy with no selection silently does nothing and returns copied false without touching the clipboard, because empty explicit text, terminal selection and getSelection fallback are all empty.

Close sends SIGINT byte 0x03, waits closeGraceMs, then closes broker and facade best-effort. closingSessions guards the session during the wait; the timer is tracked in pendingTimers for dispose cleanup.
dispose() unsubscribes transport onData/onExit, clears toast and pending close timers, disposes direct port facades and the owned port facade, and blocks further notify/persist side effects.
Defaults: close grace 150ms, toast 2000ms, at most 16 screens and 16 slots per screen. Non-negative finite overrides win; serialize truncates beyond the maxima.
Profiles always start with Shell, then hostProviders/providers listing/brokerCommands filtered by PROVIDER_ID_RE, availability flags and seen ids. Unavailable or provider-id providers are omitted.

Only exact Ctrl+Shift+T/W/C/V and Ctrl+PageUp/PageDown match, with Alt/Meta rejected; all other keys return null. Misreading this lets deck shortcuts swallow PTY input or leak Ctrl+C away from SIGINT.

Persistence uses localStorage key metaviewer.terminalDeck/v1 with envelope schema tag of the same value; storage read/write failures fall back to a fresh screen or are swallowed so quota never crashes the deck.
Declares the consumer prop boundary for the vendored AiMultiSlot kit SFC: capsule identity, layout flags, session selection, provider/command launch inputs and multislot registry attachment.
Declares the control-bar prop boundary: capsule identity plus input mode, copy state, surface/terminal visibility, folded and floating flags.
Declares the side-terminal panel prop boundary: optional session facade, provider list, storage handle, open flag and top/bottom offsets.
Re-exports the kit TerminalView and declares the local createStreamRegistry factory that wires Terminal/FitAddon classes and authorized PTY input callback to a multislot registry.
AiMultiSlotProps requires capsuleId string; sessions carry sessionId/title/kind/activity and providers carry id/label/hint/argv with optional command. epoch/generation order concurrent slot updates.
AiSlotControlBarProps requires only capsuleId; every display and mode field is optional so the bar renders before surface state arrives.
All SideTerminalPanel props are optional; storage is a minimal getItem/setItem pick or null, and open accepts boolean or null for not-yet-loaded panels.
Attachment and activity flow through attachmentState/activityState strings plus hasControlLease boolean; streamRegistry of MultislotRegistryLike binds live session streams outside Vue props.

createStreamRegistry is the entry for building the terminal stream registry consumed as AiMultiSlotProps.streamRegistry; onSendAuthorizedPtyInput carries sessionId, epoch, attachmentId, inputSeq and data.
Both types depend on ../multislot/multislotAttach.js MultislotRegistryLike for the registry shape; TerminalView.d.ts additionally depends on the vendored .kit capsule-ui-kit TerminalView types.
selectedSessionId must name one entry of sessions; surfaceHidden/terminalHidden/folded/floating are independent booleans so a capsule can be folded yet surface-visible.
Provider entries use argv arrays while commands is a separate string list and launching is a single boolean; treating launching per-provider or argv as shell text misroutes terminal launch input.
Owns multi-view multi-desktop wall state: loads persisted desktops, reconciles surface assignments from rows/modes, renders one WallWorkspace per desktop, and persists layout changes.
selectView switches the active human/agent view; selectDesktop switches the active desktop within it. selectView before load is deferred via requestedView.
addDesktop appends a desktop via electron layout helper and surfaces layout-error on limit failure; removeDesktop deletes the active-view desktop and drops its ready/adapter/revealed entries.
followSurface optionally reassigns a surface view then activates its home desktop; revealSurface delegates to the home wall or returns ok false when the surface has no home.

moveTile relocates a surface across desktops: hides native visibility, emits close intent, relocates assignment, prunes layouts, reveals on target, persists, optionally navigates. Read-only or unknown ids return ok false.
adapter(view,id) builds a per-desktop feed/storage/defaultProfile: projection rows filtered by desktopRows, snapshot rows rewritten, layout read/written per desktop layout JSON, then persisted.
Desktops stay hidden until loaded true; each WallWorkspace registers in walls on mount and becomes ready via wallReady, which applies its preset, reveals assigned surfaces once, and emits ready.
cleanLayouts prunes every desktop layout to surfaces assigned to that exact view/desktop, collapsing grid-preset orphans, before each atomic persist so stale references never accumulate.

persist() deep-clones state through cleanLayouts and writes atomically; concurrent calls coalesce via dirty/saving flags. After a write failure it latches readOnly and emits layout-error with LAYOUT_SAVE_REFUSED thereafter.
When storage write rejects, persist sets readOnly true, emits layout-error, rethrows, and later persists reject immediately with LAYOUT_SAVE_REFUSED while moveTile and setPreset refuse with ok false.
On load, schema mismatch or failed layout-profile decode/migrate throws LAYOUT_CONTRACT_INVALID, latches readOnly, and emits layout-error; the wall then runs on defaults without saving.

User sees an empty desktop even though surfaces are assigned: reveals only run for ready walls and skip already-seen ids, so a wall that never fires ready or a failed revealSurface leaves tiles unrevealed.
Global capture-phase keydown/keyup maps chords via desktopShortcut; matched or captured codes are preventDefaulted and stopImmediatePropagated, with keyup releasing the capturedKeys guard.

Projection listeners, key handlers, native shortcut listener and the prune timer are registered on mount and removed on unmount via alive flag and clearTimeout; adapters/walls/revealed maps are keyed by stable view-id keys.
Startup prune waits for a live non-stale snapshot with rows for 5000ms, polling every 250ms; only then are assignments missing from the projection deleted, so early native fill is never pruned.
Desktop component keys use a WeakMap plus usedKeys set with -next suffixing; keying by view-id alone would collide across state reloads and reuse the wrong wall adapter.
Depends on WallWorkspace.vue rendering, layout.js createWallLayout, kit layoutProfile decode/migrate, electron desktopLayout state helpers and desktopShortcuts chord mapping.
Renders the interim empty-wall placeholder: eyebrow, title, hint and an Add capsule button, as a one-file seam for the future kit EmptyWall swap without touching callers.
The Add capsule UiButton click is the only action; it emits add-capsule so the parent opens capsule creation. No other events or host calls exist.
Props are title and hint strings with defaults naming a clear workspace and capsule hint; emits is exactly add-capsule with no payload.
title and hint flow one-way into the h1 and hint paragraph; no storage, projection or intent builders are read, and no state is written back.
Stateless view with no lifecycle branches: it renders its section whenever mounted and disappears when the parent swaps in wall content.
Section keeps aria-labelledby pointing at empty-wall-title, the decorative mark stays aria-hidden, and the button keeps id empty-wall-add with data-semantic-anchor wall/add-capsule.
User sees A clear view of your work with Add a capsule to bring your surfaces together in one wall and an Add capsule button when the wall has no capsules.
No local failure path: missing kit UiButton import or wall.css would break render upstream; the component itself has no validation, logging or fallback text.
Depends only on capsule-ui-kit UiButton and local wall.css for the mv-wall-empty styles; explicitly no host calls, storage or surface inventory.
Callers must listen for add-capsule; rendering this view without that listener shows a working-looking button that does nothing.
Validates panel dependencies before render: exact capsule id, non-empty presentation instance, projection view with getSnapshot/subscribe, intent builders, and scheduler/registry objects.
Fold toggle emits one visibility intent with verb fold or unfold from current visibility; on live-axis tiles it first sets uiPhase to folding/unfolding for the pending-busy row.
Control requests resolve the verb via controlVerbForRow then emit one control intent; uiPhase moves to taking-control or releasing-control until authority state moves.
Close and dock-back emit presentation intents close and dock-back for the exact capsuleId; handlers stay silent when no authoritative row exists instead of inventing identity.

Projection snapshots flow from projectionView through bindView into snapshot ref; row selects the exact id/surfaceId match, lastRow keeps the last admitted row, and tile derives the seven-state decision.
Kit panel receives a mirrored view whose rows add folded boolean from visibility; snapshots without rows or with no changed rows pass through by reference without mutating inputs.
Display status prioritizes refusal code, then destroyed/lost lifecycles, then unknown lifecycles as Waiting, then stale transport, then live only with a live snapshot plus envelope and row.

Only live, folded, human-control and agent-acting tiles arm fold pending-busy; folding/unfolding phases render Folding/Unfolding until visibility, control, lifecycle, refusal or transport status moves.
A surface row is selected only when row.id and row.surfaceId both equal capsuleId; duplicate or mismatched rows never bind, and missing rows yield null rather than a fabricated row.
Frame host stays mounted except for destroyed rows; canvas drawing is further limited to active, standby and ceded lifecycles, while chrome and diagnostics keep rendering.
Semantic anchors are capsule/id/action for the 7 known panel actions; unknown actions throw PANEL_INVALID_ANCHOR. Popout is always unavailable with a denies-new-windows reason.
Control boxes round to integer CSS pixels; hidden or non-finite x/y/width/height inputs yield null so the registry never stores a fabricated box.

Missing or malformed capsuleId, presentationInstance, projectionView, intentBuilders, controlRegistry or non-null tileScheduler throws ERR_PANEL_INVALID_PROP with a naming message before any subscription.
User sees Folding or Unfolding in the status row after a fold gesture until authority moves; refused folds clear busy and keep authoritative state with the typed refusal row.

Connecting tiles show a placeholder with no frame claim; lost tiles show a typed status row unless a presented frozen frame keeps the canvas and frame identity. Freshness text is plain, never a live region.

Tile-scheduler presentation notices bump presentationRevision outside the projection feed, re-reading frozen-frame and freshness witnesses; schedulers without subscribePresentation keep the legacy badge path.
View subscription and presentation subscription are unbound on prop change and unmount, preventing stale capsule feeds and leaked scheduler listeners.

Depends on NetworkPanel, TileCaptureChrome, kit CapsulePanel, tileStates derivation helpers and wall.css; object capabilities travel by provide for tileScheduler, projection view, scheduler and registry.

Popout denial and prop errors are visible refusals with fixed text; collapsing refusal codes or treating quiet output as done would hide STALE_FRAME, LOCKED_BY_OTHER, BUDGET_EXCEEDED, OUT_OF_BOUNDS and POLICY.

Renders the per-tile capture chrome rail above each wall tile: record-for-AI toggle, screenshot button, capsule-id copy chip and recording badge. Lane owns layout and copy; kit owns record toggle and glyph.

Record intent enters via kit SaasRecordButton submit-intent into onRecordIntent, which calls captureState.toggleRecord(capsuleId). Intent never leaves the tile; disabled or missing store returns silently.
Screenshot enters via shot button click into onShotClick, which calls captureState.screenshot(capsuleId). Sets shotCapturing true until the returned promise settles, then clears it.
Copy enters via Copy ID button into onCopyId, which snapshots surfaceId and profileId and runs copyCapsuleReadyLine through copyFeedback. Disabled state returns without touching the clipboard.

Flow: props captureState plus capsuleId feed readSurfaceEntry into entry, then surfaceEntryPhase into phase. Phase drives busy, recordReason, badgeText, badgeVariant and is passed to SaasRecordButton.

Capsule chip flow: props surfaceId into capSurfaceId, combined with profileId and tileState into capsuleIdModel capId. Chip renders only when capId.visible; bare chrome without surfaceId keeps the three-control rail.

Screenshot is momentary: shotCapturing is lane-local shallowRef true only in flight. Store carries only settled lastShot. shotDisabled holds while unavailable or capturing; label flips Screenshot to Capturing to Captured.

Copy states ready, copying, copied, unavailable live in copyState and copyReason via createCapsuleCopyFeedback callback. New run replaces the timer; copied shows Copied, unavailable shows Copy unavailable.

Missing store, available false, or missing toggleRecord/screenshot actions make unavailable true via isCaptureUnavailable. Controls disable with shared unavailable reason instead of throwing; badge still renders.

captureState contract: bySurface entries carry phase, elapsedMs and lastShot; toggleRecord and screenshot are functions of surfaceId returning promise-like {ok} rows. clipboard prop is optional CapsuleClipboardLike with writeText.
If unavailable or phase is starting/stopping, recordDisabled true and button disables. Reason is Recording is unavailable or Recording is <phase>. Handler then ignores submit-intent.

If unavailable or a capture is pending, shotDisabled true with reason Recording is unavailable or Screenshot capture is pending. Handler ignores clicks; aria-busy and data-unavailable-reason expose it.
Copy disables when canCopy false, clipboard unreachable, or state copying. Reason is blockedReason or Copy unavailable. Status line shows Copied or Copy unavailable only after a run; otherwise empty.

User sees a small badge reading Idle, Starting, Recording MM:SS, Stopping or Sealed with matching data-variant. Title reads Phase <phase>. Frozen or wrong readout means entry.elapsedMs or phase stopped updating.

User sees screenshot button labelled Screenshot, Capturing while pending, or Captured after lastShot. Accessible name names the capsule and pending/captured state. Stuck Capturing means the screenshot promise never settled.

onShotClick sets the flag before calling screenshot and clears it in done attached as both fulfillment and rejection handlers. Non-promise returns clear it synchronously, so the button cannot stick busy.
Copy confirmation timer is owned by copyFeedback. onBeforeUnmount calls copyFeedback.dispose to clear the pending reset-to-ready timer when the tile unmounts.
displayOnly true removes the whole rail by v-if, for nested display-only mode. Default false renders the rail with role group and tileChromeGroupName label.

Depends on kit SaasRecordButton and SidebarIcon for controls, and on tileCapture.js for phase mapping, DOM ids, anchors and copy helpers. DOM ids and semantic anchors derive from capsuleId via tileRecordDomId and family.
Guards check disabled first, then null store and missing function. A store exposing only one of toggleRecord/screenshot still counts unavailable, so one control can mask the other being present.

Presentation-only wall composition over kit DockWorkspace: exactly one permanent panel per capsuleId. Never touches storage, layout bytes or backend verbs; reveal and presentation intents use only the Dockview api from the kit ready event.

Lifecycle starts at handleReady(payload with api, windows, host). Requires getPanel/addPanel plus state/show/hide/float/dock; otherwise returns ERR_INVALID_READY. Ready event is re-emitted via onReady.
revealSurface(capsuleId, placement) creates or reveals the panel- prefixed panel. Validates id, checks tab/split/floating, requires ready api, admits the row, then addPanel or show/float/setActive.

Local verbs close, hide, show, float, dock-back arrive via applyPresentationIntent or panel onPresentationIntent. Unknown verbs, unknown panels or not-ready refuse; close also emits panel-closed with capsuleId.
Exposed component methods revealSurface, applyLayoutEcho, setPreset, resizeTile, resizeFocused and applyPresentationIntent thinly delegate to the controller for host and panel callers.

Admission reads projectionView.getProjection rows by surfaceId, then demands row.id equals capsuleId and lifecycle active, standby or ceded. Lost with allowLostSurface passes for fixtures; lost/destroyed refuse as ERR_SURFACE_GONE.

WallSurfaceRouter resolves capsuleId from panel params via resolveRouterCapsuleId, renders missing-id alert on null, else renders SurfacePanel with projection, intents, schedulers, captureState and panel callbacks.

Tab flow: resolveDockTabCapsuleId reads params capsuleId then reversible panel- prefix; resolveDockTabTitle prefers panel title then capsuleId then Capsule fallback. describeDockTab freezes id wall-tab- plus anchor or null title-only.

Preset engine: setPreset stores preset and focusTile then refreshPreset; applyPreset closes destroyed rows, prunes orphans, skips when unready, signature-unchanged or maximized, else moves panels and rebuilds grid or floating groups.

presetRectangles computes exact cell geometry for single, side-by-side, grid, focus-strip and floating. Equal rectangles mean same-cell tabs. Maximized tiles return empty; duplicates or bad sizes throw LAYOUT_PRESET_INVALID.

Capsule ids are never invented: blank, trimmed-different or whitespace-bearing values refuse with ERR_INVALID_CAPSULE_ID. resolveRouterCapsuleId returns null for the same shapes, rendering the missing-id alert.

Panel ids are deterministic panel- plus capsuleId and tab ids wall-tab- plus capsuleId, never bare numeric indexes. Tab anchors are workspace/tab/<capsuleId>; retired or foreign panels render unanchored without invented identity.

All controller results are frozen WallAdmissionResult: ok true with value, or ok false with frozen code and message from wallError. Callers match on ok, never on thrown errors except internal preset path.

Reveal refuses ERR_INVALID_CAPSULE_ID, ERR_INVALID_PLACEMENT, ERR_NOT_READY before restore settles, row errors, or ERR_REVEAL_FAILED with the caught message. Existing panel path shows, floats or activates instead of duplicating.

Layout echo for committed move/tab validates slot_id, group_id grammar and index 0..255, then docks and moveTo with index. Float delegates to applyFloatEcho with x/y/width/height ranges; anything else refuses ERR_INVALID_PLACEMENT.

resizeTile wider/narrower/taller/shorter/fit refuses ERR_NOT_READY or LAYOUT_SIZE_INVALID, then setSizes via panelAllocation gap share or float outer rect, clamped to 240x200 minima and wall maxima. Failure returns LAYOUT_SIZE_FAILED.
User sees Panel unavailable: <id> plus retired-type reason when the kit routes an unknown component here. Never renders a live-looking tile; message stays honest about reset needed.
User picks a tile preset and nothing moves, or sees Tile layout is unavailable. Causes: unknown preset name, wall not ready, maximized tile veto, or kit moveTo missing during preset application.

A 150ms interval calls controller.refreshPreset continuously to reassert the preset after kit changes; cleared plus controller.dispose on unmount. Refresh failures reset preset and emit layout-error with LAYOUT_PRESET_FAILED.

Restored panels from an earlier run close only after 5000ms of absence from a live non-stale snapshot. Still-filling projections never drop live tiles; collapseEmptyGroups keeps the initial empty target until a real panel exists.
Identity slots cap at 256; without a panel list it never prunes on a guess. Retained panels plus slotted panels survive; others drop from panelIdentities and panelOrder.

Props carry workspaceComponent, scope, storage, ownerWindowId, projectionView, intents, registries, colorScheme light/dark, density, defaultProfile, captureState, displayOnly and clipboard. Viewport seeds 1280x720 before kit remeasure.

Depends on kit DockWorkspace for layout host, restore and persistence, and on SurfacePanel for tile content. Registers CapsulePanel router and SurfaceTab tab component; kit owns validated persistence and settled gates.

captureSlot remembers group, sibling reference, direction from geometry or order, and index before close so reveal can restore placement. Geometry fallback uses bounding rects; zero-size rects fall back to group and panel order.

Builds the single Copy ID for AI ready line a terminal AI receives: names the capsule and identity, the attach-env source line, and the mw_run command with site and workflow placeholders, or an id-only line when identity is unusable.

Copy entry is copyCapsuleReadyLine(ids, clipboard): builds the line, enforces byte bound, picks injected then ambient clipboard, awaits writeText. Never throws; every outcome is a projected copied/unavailable row.

Feedback entry is createCapsuleCopyFeedback(onState, options): run(copy) emits copying, awaits the copy callback, emits copied or unavailable, then schedules reset to ready. New run supersedes the prior timer.

Display flow: surfaceId plus profileId plus tile into capsuleIdModel. Unusable id yields invisible empty model; usable id yields short text, hover with full id and identity, copy name, and canCopy unless tile is lost or error.
Clipboard flow: injected clipboard wins when writeText is a function; else ambient navigator.clipboard. capsuleCopyAvailable reports reachability without writing, so the button can disable up front.

Copy states are closed: ready, copying, copied, unavailable. copying while pending, then copied or unavailable until delayMs 2000 returns to ready. Generation counter drops stale completions; dispose freezes further runs.
Surface ids must match 1..128 shell-safe characters. Non-grammar input yields null line and invisible chip, so nothing unusable is displayed or put in a command.
Identity must match lower-case 1..64 characters for mw_run. Absent or non-grammar identity yields an id-only line telling the operator to supply the name, never guessing one.
User-visible strings are fixed: Copy ID for AI, Copied, Copy unavailable. Status and disabled reasons reuse them so tile and multislot copy read identically.

Null line gives unavailable ERR_CAPSULE_ID_INVALID; over 4096 UTF-8 bytes gives ERR_CAPSULE_LINE_TOO_LARGE; no clipboard gives ERR_CLIPBOARD_UNAVAILABLE; write rejection gives ERR_CLIPBOARD_WRITE_REFUSED. Thrown copy callbacks map to write-refused.

User sees a short id: whole when 14 or fewer characters, else first 8 plus ellipsis plus last 5. Full id stays on hover and in the accessible name. Empty text means a non-string reached the formatter.
User sees the id chip only for usable ids; on lost or error tiles the id stays visible but Copy disables with Capsule is <tile>; nothing to manage. No command is offered for those tiles.
Overlapping copy clicks increment generation; only the latest completion emits and schedules reset. dispose sets disposed, clears the timer, and later runs return without emitting.
Line is capped at 4096 UTF-8 bytes via TextEncoder, inside the 16384 host clipboard bound. Oversize lines refuse before touching the clipboard rather than truncating a command.
Transient Copied confirmation clears after 2000ms, injectable via delayMs with setTimer and clearTimer doubles for tests.

Pure module with no imports, framework calls or host access. Renderer stays display-only: formats host-issued ids and writes one string to the injected clipboard; never builds paths or launches anything.

Ready line carries no host path, only the documented attach pointer name and operator-repo-relative mw_run invocation, so it is identical in dev and packaged runs. Site and workflow stay placeholders chosen from MemoryWeb data.

Creates and migrates the wall Dockview layout profile: seeded empty wall or one leaf per capsule surface arranged in a grid, with placements recorded. Foreign or demo panels migrate to the empty product wall.

Creation entry is createWallLayout(scope, surfaces): clones the kit default profile, sizes grid from the first surface, registers panel-<id> panels, arranges leaves, then decodes and migrates before returning the profile.

Restore entry is migrateWallLayout(raw, scope): null passes through; unparseable JSON returns raw for kit quarantine; failed decode or non-CapsulePanel/identity-mismatched panels return a fresh empty wall; otherwise raw survives.

Dimensions read Width/width/frameWidth then geometry w/width variants, same for height, rounded. Both valid keeps them; either invalid falls back to 1280x900 with aspect and aspectRatio string derived from the pair.

Tile box derives wall size, count, columns and rows, cell size, strip height, then fits the capsule aspect into the cell minus strip. Returns box plus surface, cell, strip and grid counts; stripVisible flags fit.

Grid rule: up to two leaves stay flat with equal widths; three or more split into two columns, five or more into three, filled row-major so reading order matches reveal order. Column branches stack vertically per Dockview depth alternation.

Empty wall always has a branch root with one empty wall-empty leaf; non-empty wall replaces it with arranged leaves. activeGroup follows the first surface; savedWallPlacements records groupId and index per panel.
Defaults are 1280x900 capsule size and 23px footer strip. Never hard-coded 16:9; strip reserves live-tile footer space and is omitted when showStrip is false.

Missing or whitespace-bearing surface id throws Invalid capsule identity; duplicate panel id throws Duplicate capsule identity; absent placements throw Layout placements absent; failed kit decode throws with its reason.

User sees letterboxed capsule content with footer strip visible when stripVisible true. Wrong aspect or clipped footer means surface Width/Height or geometry aliases were unreadable and defaults applied.
User sees an empty wall after upgrade or demo import instead of old tiles. That is the deliberate migration when foreign panel identities are detected, not a data loss of live capsules.
Layout creation is synchronous and pure: structuredClone of the kit default, then in-memory leaf assembly, then synchronous kit decode. No async restore or storage writes happen here.
Grid math uses floored leaf sizes from gridWidth and gridHeight so allocations sum without drift. Zero or invalid wall sizes fall back to capsule dimensions rather than dividing by zero.
Scope defaults to product metaviewer, profile default, workspace main-wall. Caller-supplied scope threads through creation and migration for kit profile decoding.
Depends only on kit createDefaultLayoutProfile and decodeAndMigrateLayoutProfile for profile shape and validation. No framework, host or storage access in this module.
Migration is destructive by design: one foreign or renamed panel discards the entire saved panel map for the empty wall. Stale demo identities therefore cannot resurrect as phantom live tiles.
Tile capture helper core: tile-scoped ids, anchors, accessible names, elapsed formatting and defensive capture-store reads driving the chrome rail on every wall tile.
Store read entry is readSurfaceEntry(captureState, surfaceId): accepts bySurface as Map or plain object, returns the entry record or null. Missing store, key or malformed entry never throws.
Availability entry is isCaptureUnavailable: true for missing store, explicit available false, or missing toggleRecord/screenshot. hasCaptureActions requires both functions to be callable.
Phase flow: entry.phase through normalizeTileCapturePhase into one of six phases, defaulting unknown to idle. Chrome badge, busy flag and record gating all consume this single normalization.

Id flow: host surface id through tileIdSegment into tile-<segment>-record-ai, screenshot and recording-badge DOM ids and identical semantic anchors. Canonical ids pass through; others hex-encode per UTF-16 unit.
Record phases are idle, starting, recording, stopping, sealed and error. starting and stopping count busy via tileCapturePhaseBusy; error renders as Idle with detail kept in lastCode, never shown.

Screenshot label machine: capturing true gives Capturing, else settled lastShot gives Captured, else Screenshot. Accessible names add the capsule label and pending/captured phrasing for the same states.
Only the six listed phases are known; any other phase value normalizes to idle. Badge, variant and busy checks therefore cannot branch on an unexpected string.
Chrome label prefers trimmed capsuleLabel, falls back to capsuleId, then capsule. Group name is always Tile capture controls for <label>, so the rail never has an empty accessible name.
Elapsed formats finite non-negative milliseconds as MM:SS zero-padded. Unreadable values render --:--, never a fabricated zero; only active recording shows the readout.
