s: ui/src/creative/CreativeCapsule.vue::{MAX_STORYBOARD_FRAMES, MAX_PROMPT_LENGTH, MAX_IMAGE_BYTES, MAX_DATA_URL_LENGTH, MAX_IMAGE_DIMENSION, MAX_SELF_PATH_LENGTH, DATA_PNG_PREFIX, PNG_MAGIC_B64, BASE64_PATTERN, SELF_PATH_PATTERN, SCHEME_PATTERN, FRAME_ID_PATTERN, SHA256_PATTERN, FRAME_KEYS_SORTED, refused, creativeError, validateCapsuleId, validateImageSource, validateStoryboardFrame, validateStoryboardFrame.clean, validateStoryboard, deriveCreativeStatus, buildStoryboardIntent, props, emit, idResult, board, admittedFrames, isAdmitted, anchorRoot, dispatchIntent, onSelectFrame, onRegenerate, onClosePanel}

t: Status is Live when frames are admitted, Waiting for storyboard when empty, and Refused plus code when id or board refuses. The template shows the board only when isAdmitted.
Validation is synchronous and atomic per render: computed props re-derive on each prop change with no locks, retries, or partial admission of a bad frame list.
Ceilings are 8 frames, 2000 prompt chars, 2 MiB decoded PNG, 2800000 URL chars, 8192 pixels per axis, and 512 chars for self paths; base64 length and padding are checked without decoding.
UI depends on capsule-ui-kit UiPage, UiToolbar, and UiButton. Validation and intent builders are dependency-free so node:test can load the same script block directly.
DOM identities embed encodeURIComponent of the capsule id plus frame ids with no shared per-frame ids; a hostile or odd id could still produce long but structurally namespaced anchors.

When host.demo returns {ok:false,code}, message becomes refusal(verb,code): PUBLIC[code] if known else REFUSED[verb]. Start: choose unused id and running identity; Stop: seal failed, restart with new id; Prompt: record/stop first; Check: folder must exist and pass index check.

Known public codes: DEMO_BUSY, DEMO_NOT_RECORDING, BUTTON_UNAVAILABLE naming MV_OPERATOR_REPO checkout. Unknown/result throw yields 'Demo operation unavailable.' Identity list failure yields 'The identity tool could not run: <reason>'.

Entry is props.open watcher plus props.host (default operatorHost). On open it clears rows/message, calls host.identity.list(), fills rows for the identity select, or shows identity-tool failure text.

invoke(verb) maps verb to host.demo args: start {identity,demo}, stop [], prompt {demo,site}, check {site}. Results flow back to recording/sealed/url/message; prompt and check produce Copied/Site check text, start produces viewer URL.
IDs match /^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$/; demo 1-40 chars, site 1-64 chars. demoOk/siteOk gate Start/Copy/Check buttons and hint text. Violations never reach host.demo.

Demo ids are single-use per dialog lifetime: successful start appends demoId to used; hint blocks reuse with 'already recorded: choose a new one'. sealed must equal current demoId to enable Copy prompt.

DemoDialog.vue is a record-then-automate dialog: pick an identity, record a viewer session as a named demo, then copy an AI prompt and verify the generated site. It drives host.demo start/stop/prompt/check and reports status in-message.

States: idle -> recording (start ok sets recording, clears sealed, sets url) -> sealed (stop ok sets recording false, sealed=demoId). busy true during any invoke; Confirm Close disabled while busy or recording.

invoke returns immediately if busy, so double-clicks never double-start. busy set true before await and cleared in finally; message cleared at entry. Close/back handlers no-op while recording or busy.
Unmount race: onUnmounted sets unmounted flag and stops an active recording via host.demo.stop(). After start resolves, if unmounted it immediately stops instead of leaving a dangling recording.
Stop clears viewer url and prior sealed before checking result, so a failed stop never shows a stale URL or sealed id. Start clears sealed/url on entry to recording. No timers or ports held.

Default host is operatorHost import. BUTTON_UNAVAILABLE tells user to check MV_OPERATOR_REPO points to operator checkout. No other env config; placeholders pplx-ask-1 and perplexity are examples only.
Depends on capsule-ui-kit UiButton/UiTextInput and .kit ConfirmDialog for layout, plus host.identity.list and host.demo start/stop/prompt/check. Emits only close; parent controls open.

Privacy warning is load-bearing: dialog text says use dummy data because frames can show field contents while typed text is stored as length only. Recording requires user to log in first before pressing Start.

ui/src/frames holds two main-world MessagePort consumers that paint remote surfaces onto tile canvases and ack every delivery so host readers never block. displayPortRouter handles unverified 20-30 fps DISPLAY ports (display_port/v1, display_frame/state, display_ack/v1) with RGB24->RGBA putImageData, 2s stale watchdog, stacked bindings, park on hide/unbind, 500ms display-request retry, and once-per-stage diagnostics. framePortRouter handles brokered verified ports (frame_delivery/v0.2, frame_ack/v0.2) with sha256 verification, pinned stream identity, serial newest-only validateAndPaint via tile scheduler register/submit/present, unbound newest-only hold with expiry and retained replay, generation-ordered retire/SUPERSEDED, and FOLD_DRAIN/HIDDEN/CONTEXT_LOST/SURFACE_DESTROYED mapping. Both validate closed-shape window notices same-origin with exactly one port, close spare ports, and never paint on mismatch. Offers install/getShared routers, bindSurface/unbind, setSurfaceVisible, getSurfaceStatus. Needs window-like target, tile getCanvas/onFrame/isVisible or scheduler, host reportDiag and ack reader.

User sees tile freeze then visible stale badge after 2s without frames, or blank tile when binding hidden/unbound. No exception surfaces; failures appear only as HIDDEN/REFUSED acks and capped display-diagnostic posts.

User sees tile stuck in Connecting when never PRESENTED (no scheduler witness lastPresentedFrameGen+handle), blank after destroy/hide, or older frame dropped for newer. PRESENTED requires up to 3 presentSurfaceNow attempts witnessed.

Frame refused paths: surface mismatch -> REFUSED; no binding or invisible binding -> HIDDEN with REFUSED diagnostic NO_BINDING/HIDDEN; paint/onFrame false/throw -> HIDDEN with PAINT_FAILED. refusedCount increments; host is still acked.

Notice refused when origin != app://metaviewer or ports.length !=1: refusedCount increments and every transferred port is closed. Invalid delivery/state payloads increment refusedCount and emit REFUSED INVALID_DELIVERY diagnostic.

Shape/identity/floor failure on bound path settles REFUSED when ack can be built, else silent drop. Registered-stream gap deliveries refuse rather than hold; unbound valid shapes hold instead of refusing.

Newest-only: enqueue marks in-flight superseded and settles all queued as SUPERSEDED; pump keeps only head. Older-than-current/queued/expiring arrivals refuse pre-hash so older frames never paint after newer ones.

Submit maps refusal: FOLDED_DISPLAY_DISABLED->FOLD_DRAIN, HIDDEN_SURFACE->HIDDEN, CONTEXT_LOST, SURFACE_DESTROYED, else REFUSED. Port-closing outcomes (fold/hide/lost/destroyed) retire the stream after ack.
Digest mismatch settles REFUSED without advancing floor, so retransmit of same generation can succeed. Retired/displaced in-flight records settle SUPERSEDED or SURFACE_DESTROYED and never paint.

Entry is window message carrying one MessagePort with {type:'metaviewer:display-port',schema:'display_port/v1',surface_id}. installDisplayPortRouter listens on target, validates closed-shape notice, then attachStream adopts the port.

Entry is window message with exactly one MessagePort and closed-shape {type,schema,surface_id,surface_generation}. Same-origin only; dormant until first valid notice so it never double-paints with the interim preload painter.

Port message -> unwrap ev.data -> isValidDisplayDelivery or isValidDisplayState. Frames freeze {surfaceId,width,height,seq,captureMonoNs,generation,bytes}, deliver via getCanvas/onFrame, then postAck PRESENTED/HIDDEN/REFUSED with display_ack/v1.

Port message -> unwrapMessage -> hold or admit+enqueue -> serial validateAndPaint (digest, register, submit, present) -> settle with PRESENTED/SUPERSEDED/HIDDEN/FOLD_DRAIN/CONTEXT_LOST/SURFACE_DESTROYED/REFUSED echoed with delivery identity.

Notice contract: exact keys schema,surface_id,type; type and schema must equal DISPLAY_PORT_NOTICE_TYPE/SCHEMA; surface_id matches /^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:-]{0,127}$/. Extra keys or schemaless preload notices are ignored.

Delivery contract: exact DELIVERY_KEYS, schema display_frame/v1 or display_delivery/v1, kind display_frame, format rgb24, 1-4096 width/height, byteLength equals w*h*3, bytes view matches, generation/mono numeric strings.
Seq contract: numeric or numeric-string of 1-20 digits, BigInt >=2 and even. Odd or 0 seq fails. Mismatched payload.surfaceId vs stream surfaceId is REFUSED as SURFACE_MISMATCH, never painted.

State contract: exact STATE_KEYS, schema display_state/v1, kind display_state, state one of active/stale/absent, generation numeric string. Valid state updates stream.state/generation and forwards to binding onState.

Notice contract: exact keys schema,surface_generation,surface_id,type; pinned type/schema; non-empty surface_id; positive safe-int surface_generation. Extra keys, wrong origin, or port count !=1 closes ports and ignores.

Delivery contract: exact DELIVERY_KEYS with or without utilityVerified, schema frame_delivery/v0.2, kind frame, rgb24, positive width/height, byteLength equals bytes.byteLength equals w*h*3, sha256 64 hex not null digest, pixelSpec object.

Identity contract: correlation/principal/leaseId non-empty strings, epoch/surfaceGeneration/frameGeneration safe ints, positive frameGeneration above admittedFloor. Ack identity required for REFUSED ack; else arrival drops silently.

Utility-verified marker skips re-hash only when raw.utilityVerified===true AND port event isTrusted===true. Forged values (1,'true',{}) or synthetic events still hash. Malformed markers hash as before.

Isolation invariant: never enters VERIFIED scheduler, frame_ref handling, or receipts. paintDisplayCanvas only does RGB24->RGBA putImageData on a 2d canvas, reusing a WeakMap scratch ImageData sized w*h*4.

Display-port router is the main-world consumer for unverified 20-30 fps DISPLAY ports. It validates display_frame/state envelopes, paints the newest frame onto the bound tile canvas, tracks 2s stale liveness, and acks every delivery so the host reader never blocks.

Frame-port router is the main-world consumer for brokered verified surface ports. It admits frame_delivery/v0.2, sha256-verifies bytes, paints via the bound tile scheduler, and acks every delivery exactly once with frame_ack/v0.2.

Per-stream states active/stale/absent plus parked flag. Valid frame sets active and arms stale watchdog; watchdog fires after staleTimeoutMs to stale and calls onState stale. Non-active state or absent clears timer and drops lastFrame.

Per-surface one live stream keyed by surfaceId with monotonic streamId high-water persisted across retire. Newer generation retires old as SUPERSEDED; same/older notice closes spare port; retired ids never re-admitted.

Unbound hold: never-registered stream with no binding holds newest-only un-acked delivery. Expiry sha-verifies: mismatch settles REFUSED and drops, valid settles HIDDEN but KEPT as retained latest frame for late bind with no second ack.

Bind drains hold: pending present drains via bound admit path; else retained paints via settled-from-birth replay through validate+paint. Older kept frame drops silently if newer queued/validating work exists.

Missing-handoff retry: requestDisplay posts display-request at most every 500ms while bound and visible, re-armed by 500ms timer. bindSurface and setSurfaceVisible(true) restart it; unbind/hide calls stopPull.
Bindings stack per surface; last bound entry is active. deliverBindingFrame checks binding.visible then isVisible(), paints via getCanvas, then onFrame. False return or throw counts as not painted.

Hide/unbind parks stream: posts display_visibility hidden:true, sets parked, clears lastFrame and watchdog. attachStream replaces any prior stream for that surface; bindSurface unparks with hidden:false.

Serial per-stream validation: validating flag plus current record; pump chains next via promise then. Newer arrival during digest fences expired work via admittedFloor/boundFloor and expiring/retained/queued generation checks.

Bindings stack per surface; most recent bind active. Token unbind removes only its entry; removing active restores previous and re-fires onRegistered. Last-entry removal retires unless keepStream arms 500ms grace for remount.

Unbound hold window defaults 2000ms, far above mount gaps and below host 10s ack timeout. Expiry settles HIDDEN to free host inFlight. Bind during verification paints kept frame immediately with no second ack.

Canvas scratch cached per element in WeakMap and recreated on size change; RGB bytes copied 3->4 bytes with alpha 255 each frame. toUint8Array normalizes Uint8Array/ArrayBuffer/views without copying Uint8Array.

Diagnostics are once-per-stage per surface (FIRST_FRAME, FIRST_PAINT, REFUSED, ROUTER_ATTACHED, VISIBILITY) via diagnosticStages map capped at 256 surfaces; prevents high-rate IPC from a broken stream.

At most one grace timer per kept stream and one hold timer per stream; all funnel through retireStream/dispose which detaches listeners and closes ports. In-flight records settle on completion; queued/pending settle destroyed.

Zero product imports; only target window-like with addEventListener/postMessage. getSharedDisplayPortRouter is the window singleton; tiles import router lazily, and install posts display-ready so preload releases retained ports.

Depends on tile scheduler registerSurface/submitFrame/presentSurfaceNow/getInstrumentation and on host frames.reportDiag facade for diagnostics. No product imports; data-URL importable. Registration seeds panelOpen/selected, unfolded, frame-sized box.
Digest unavailability (no SubtleCrypto) fails closed as REFUSED. Counters never decrease; decreases are ignored. Observers (registered/rehash) never break the stream; throws are swallowed.

ui/src/handoff owns operator handoff interrupt UI for metaviewer.handoff/v1. HandoffNotice.vue renders rows from host.handoff with Take control and Acknowledge, subscribing on mount and surfacing load and subscribe errors. handoffModel.js owns wording and pending state via describeHandoff, receive, load and acknowledge, keyed by surface id plus step index through unseen, pending and acknowledged. IdentitiesDialog.vue manages saved browser sessions via host identity list, create, login and guarded delete. Flows: subscribe pushes into model.receive then sync copies to rows for render; ack sends surface id, step index and gesture; identity actions re-list and refresh rows and role modes. Offers handoff rows, headlines, details and steps, ack and take-control and activity emits, and identity CRUD emits. Needs host handoff subscribe, list and ack, operatorHost default, identity API, capsule-ui-kit, ConfirmDialog, validators, role API and identityProtection. Presentation is additive until successful ack; ack never resumes the run.

User sees a persistent CAPTCHA or bot-check notice with Take control and Acknowledge, or Handoff notifications unavailable, or Acknowledgement could not be saved. The notice stays visible. Cause is failed list, failed subscribe, or refused ack.

User sees No identities yet, Operator login view is open with agent input refused, or error text such as identity bound, protected, missing profile, or refused payload. Cause is host refusal, open capsule, or invalid form blocking confirm.

receive drops state when ok is false or rows is not an array; load throws HANDOFF_UNAVAILABLE when list is not ok or rows missing. Held rows stay. Caller surfaces Handoff notifications unavailable and keeps prior rows.

acknowledge calls host.ack with surface id, step index and operator gesture; when result is not ok it throws HANDOFF_UNAVAILABLE. The Vue handler catches, sets Acknowledgement could not be saved, and leaves the row visible.

invoke returns early while busy, maps foreign id to IDENTITY_PROTECTED, throws on absent host or non-ok result code, then re-lists. Any failure sets error via identityErrorText and clears login flag; success clears form fields on create.

askDelete blocks protected identities and open capsules before arming pendingDelete. deleteIdentity rechecks both guards, then invokes delete. Blocked deletes set error text and clear pendingDelete without calling host.

Entry is host prop defaulting to operatorHost plus activity and take-control emits. Host supplies handoff subscribe, list and ack. Take control emits surface id; activity emits CAPTCHA_HANDOFF with the row.

host.handoff subscribe pushes state into model.receive, sync copies model.rows into rows ref for render. describeHandoff derives headline, detail and steps per row. Acknowledge sends surface id and step index to host.ack.

Dialog opens by invoking list, then create, login or delete on host identity API, refreshing rows and role modes. Open as human or agent emits open-identity and close; program browser rows never emit. Name input flows through normalize and retain helpers.

Closed reason maps to login wall versus CAPTCHA wording; unknown reasons fall back to stop for the operator. Detail shows surface, step and reason label. Steps order is take control, multislot WRITE, solve or sign in, release, re-run.

Presentation is additive until explicit successful acknowledgement. Empty snapshots, missing files and transport failure never dismiss a row. There is no resume ABI; re-run needs operator action after solving or signing in.

HandoffNotice.vue renders operator handoff rows from host.handoff and offers Take control and Acknowledge per row. It subscribes on mount, re-renders via model.rows, and shows error text when load or subscribe fails.

handoffModel.js owns wording and pending state for metaviewer.handoff/v1. describeHandoff maps closed reason to headline and detail; createHandoffModel holds pending, seen and acknowledged sets with receive, load and acknowledge.

IdentitiesDialog.vue manages saved browser sessions: list, create, login, open as human or agent, and guarded delete. It validates the add form locally, then calls host identity API and refreshes rows and role modes.

Row identity is surface id plus step index. States are unseen, pending, and acknowledged. receive adds unseen rows to pending and fires activity once; acknowledge moves the key to acknowledged and deletes from pending. No other transition removes rows.

Notice guards callbacks with active flag and unsubscribes on unmount. Dialog guards concurrent host calls with busy flag and disables actions while busy. Name reconcile uses nextTick after normalization.
Dialog sets body data-mv-modal only when absent and tracks ownsModal, releasing only markers it installed on close or unmount. This avoids clearing a marker owned by another open modal.

Depends on operatorHost default host, capsule-ui-kit buttons and inputs, ConfirmDialog, identityForm validators and wording, role API on globalThis, and electron identityProtection for protected and foreign checks.

Agent never solves, signs in or evades; wall tiles accept typing only under human control plus WRITE set in multislot. Acknowledge hides notice only and never resumes the run. Foreign or program identities cannot be opened or deleted here.

ui/src/identities holds pure identity-dialog rules with shared frame-coordinate math. identityForm.js normalizes and validates id, label and domains, builds a host request or null, maps typed host codes to operator text, and retains typed-name casing. frameMap.js computes object-fit contain scale and centered offsets and maps client points to frame pixels. Interaction is validation-gated: invalid form never reaches host, and out-of-image clicks map to null and are never sent. Offers request, normalize, validate, error-text and contain-fit helpers. Needs only electron identityProtection for reserved names; frame mapper has no dependencies or DOM access.

User sees inline name or label errors, Add stays disabled, or identity request refused before reaching the tool. Cause is id outside 2-40 lowercase pattern, reserved name, bad label, or domains over 16 entries or 253 chars.
User clicks or drags on a capsule tile and nothing happens at the edges or on letterbox bars. By design those points map to null and are never sent, so no input leaves the renderer.

identityFormRequest returns null when name, label or domains fail validation, so the dialog never calls host. Label defaults to name when blank. Operator sees disabled confirm or OPERATOR_PAYLOAD hint to check id, label and domains.

identityErrorText maps PROTECTED, BOUND, PROFILE_NOT_PROVISIONED, PROFILE_MISSING, REFUSED, PAYLOAD and UNAVAILABLE to fixed sentences; unknown or empty codes fall back to generic text with AUSENTE marker. Invalid id argument renders as <id>.

mapClientToFrame returns null for non-object input, non-finite client coords, non safe-integer frame size at or below 0, bad rect, or failed containFit. Points in offset bands or beyond displayed size also return null.

Entry is raw text from Name, Display name and Allowed sites fields. normalizeDomains splits on commas, trims, lowercases, dedupes and sorts; normalizeIdentityName lowercases, turns whitespace to dashes and strips other chars.

Typed name keeps original spelling of unchanged chars while input shows normalized id via prefix and suffix match and boundary mapping. Middle edits reconcile, so deleting or inserting one char preserves surrounding typed casing.

Box size and frame size enter containFit, yielding scale plus displayed width, height and offsets. Client point minus rect origin and offsets, divided by scale and floored, yields frame x and y clamped to frame minus 1.

Profile errors name exact host fix: private 0700 directory owned by uid 10001 under profiles id, with install command and INSTALL doc pointer. UNAVAILABLE names required env roots and tools/mv_identity.py path.

Domains hold at most 16 unique entries matching lowercase host pattern; label is non-empty, at most 128 code points, trimmed, without control or shell metachars; name matches leading alnum plus 1-39 tail and is not protected.

identityForm.js holds pure form rules mirroring closed host validation: normalize and validate id, label and domains, build request or null, and map typed host codes to operator text that keeps the raw code.

frameMap.js maps client pointer points to frame pixels under object-fit contain. containFit computes uniform scale and centered offsets; mapClientToFrame removes letterbox bars and returns null outside the frame image.

No retained state. Each call validates 4 sizes are finite positive numbers, computes min ratio scale, and returns placement or null. Same inputs always give same fit; paint and input share this transform.
Depends only on electron identityProtection for protected names. frameMap has no dependencies and no DOM access, so renderer paint and tests share it without a host.

Label filter blocks semicolon, backtick, dollar, pipe, ampersand, angle brackets and backslash to avoid injection through display text. Frame mapper never extrapolates bars into frame coords, avoiding misdirected clicks.

ui/src/input is the renderer human-input lane for the capsule surface protocol surface_input/v1. It turns DOM mouse, wheel and keyboard activity into validated wire batches sent through the host facade, and gives tests a faithful fake of that facade. Parts: keyMap.js maps a keydown view to key or type or null; inputPort.js owns per-surface sequencing, gating, coalescing, rate limiting, release handling and refusal reporting; inputDouble.js is a test-only in-memory facade that enforces the same closed schema, ordering and size checks while recording batches and emitting results. Interaction: keyMap output feeds inputPort validation and queue or send paths; inputPort packs and sequences batches and sends via window.metaviewer input, handling sync replies and async results with dedup; inputDouble stands in for the host in renderer tests with configurable surfaces, streams and refusals. It offers never-throw send and queue with closed refusal codes through onRefusal, type and scroll coalescing, gate close with release guarantees, and frozen result events. It needs a facade exposing send with optional onResult, frame mapping for coordinate containment, and scheduler hooks for flush and coalesce.

Renderer tests see SCHEMA, SURFACE_UNKNOWN, STALE_STREAM, LIMIT or injected refusal codes instead of ok. Cause is unknown surface, stale stream, non-increasing seq, bad event count, oversize payload, or configured refuse map.

User types, clicks or scrolls and nothing moves, with refusal surfaced via onRefusal as NOT_IN_CONTROL, INPUT_MODE_READ, SURFACE_UNKNOWN, STALE_STREAM, LIMIT, NESTED_DISPLAY_ONLY, SCHEMA or CORE_UNAVAILABLE. Cause is gate closure, rate cap, oversize batch or host refusal.
User presses Escape, dead key, IME composing text, control-only combo or emoji with modifier and nothing reaches the capsule. By design the mapper returns null for those inputs.

decide returns SCHEMA for non-object batch, wrong schema id, bad surface, stream, seq or 1-32 events, or invalid event; LIMIT over 16 KiB; SURFACE_UNKNOWN for unlisted surface; STALE_STREAM on stream mismatch; then configured refusal.

Dynamic refuse function throwing resolves to CORE_UNAVAILABLE; returning unknown code resolves to SCHEMA; nullish accepts. String and map forms validate codes at creation and throw on unknown code before any send.

send returns SCHEMA for bad surface, stream or event shape or count outside 1-32, LIMIT over 16 KiB or over 60 batches per 1000 ms, CORE_UNAVAILABLE when facade missing or reply malformed, never rejecting.

queue emits SCHEMA for invalid surface, stream or event including hostile getters, CORE_UNAVAILABLE without facade, LIMIT beyond 1024 pending. flushRun drops single events exceeding budget with LIMIT and skips batches failing epoch fence or byte check.

normalizeReply maps malformed or unknown replies to CORE_UNAVAILABLE; ok true needs safe accepted count. handleResult ignores disposed, malformed, ok true, or non-result codes; refused results join per seq dedup so at most one emission.
Null input, composing flag, keyCode 229, empty or Unidentified or Dead key, control chars below 0x20 or DEL, unknown long names, and chords exceeding 8 keys or 32 joined chars all return null.

Entry is options surfaces, streams, refuse and results flag. send accepts any batch, records it, decides outcome, emits result when enabled, and resolves. reset clears batches and per-surface seq floors.

Entry is send for single fire-and-await batch and queue for next-frame buffered event with onRefusal reporting. closeGate advances gate epoch and drops queued items; droppedCount and dispose complete the surface API.

Entry is a minimal structural view with key plus ctrl, alt, shift, meta, isComposing and keyCode. Output is type with one code point or key with chord array. No DOM access; real events and test fakes share the shape.
send deep-copies batch via JSON round-trip for assertions, calls decide, emits frozen result with surface id, seq, ok and code, then returns outcome. Batches array preserves arrival order.

queue tags items with gate epoch and schedules raf or coalesce timer. flush fences to current epoch, holds type runs for 40 ms, then flushSurface splits by stream and flushRun packs, seqs and sends via facade, handling replies async.

Wheel input with deltaMode 0-2 converts to pixels, folds into per-surface carry, and emits whole 50 px steps as wire scroll with step counts. deltaMode never reaches wire. Sub-step input only grows carry.

Single chars split by code points; bare printables become type. With modifiers, ASCII punctuation maps through PUNCT_KEYS, digits and letters lowercase, others drop. Named keys map through NAMED_KEYS plus F 1-12, then prepend held modifiers.

Wire schema is surface_input/v1 with seq strictly increasing per surface from 1, 1-32 events, payload at most 16 KiB. Results expose only valid surface id and safe seq at or above 1, frozen, one per settled send.
Schema id is surface_input/v1. Closed refusal set has 8 codes including INPUT_MODE_READ; result set excludes it with 7 codes. Payload is UTF-8 JSON length; unserializable measures infinite.

Clamped release mapping keeps press-armed outside release at frame edge instead of dropping as letterbox; presses stay strict. Tile blocks contextmenu and auxclick only while WRITE armed, leaving READ events alone.
Host owns key name spelling; renames land only in the two tables. X spelling examples are Return, BackSpace, Page_Up, space, exclam, bracketleft. Digits and letters keep own spelling lowercased.

Facade never rejects and never returns off-contract replies. onResult takes exactly 1 function argument or throws ContractError ARGS; unsubscribe is idempotent. Result listeners never break sender on throw.
Wire events carry exactly closed keys: click x y button, key 1-8 keys, type 1-1024 chars, scroll dx dy x y, release_all kind only. Local wheel shape adds deltaMode and never ships.

Coalesce merges consecutive type texts and same-class scrolls, keeping latest position; unsafe integer sums stay split. Type splits avoid surrogate pairs at 1024 boundary. Non-zero deltaMode multiplies by 19 px.
Every emitted chord holds 1-8 keys joined by plus at most 32 chars, matching host adapter grammar. Modifier order is fixed ctrl, alt, shift, super.

Per-surface last seq starts empty and only advances on admitted batches; replayed or equal seq returns SCHEMA. reset clears all floors. Streams map is static expectation; mismatch refuses without updating seq.

Per-surface gate epoch starts at 0; closeGate increments, purges queue, discards wheel carry, and unless release false or nested in send dispatches one release_all under new epoch when live input exists. Release-only batches bypass rate window.

Reply and async result share per surface id and seq dedup bounded to 256 keys. First copy emits, second is silent in either order; ok results are silent. Release-only benign refusals stay silent but still mark seen.
Stateless pure function. Same input always yields same event or null. Spacebar alias normalizes to space before classification; Escape aliases Esc and never forwards.

Result fan-out copies listener set before emit, so subscribe or unsubscribe during emit does not skip or duplicate. Listener throws are swallowed per listener. Sends without usable identity stay silent.

sendDepth tracks re-entrant closure inside facade send as host-driven and skips release. Dispatch-time epoch fence drops runs queued before closure. Async reply handlers never throw; listener and hook throws are swallowed.

dispose clears timers, pending, carries, live streams, dedup maps and listeners, unsubscribes single onResult, and cancels scheduled raf exactly once. droppedCount reports per-surface or total non-release events dropped by closeGate.
Seen-result and release-seq maps evict oldest past 256 entries, bounding memory. Pending per surface caps at 1024 events; stamps prune to window on each take.
Options are now clock, releaseAll default true, typeCoalesceMs default 40, refusalBurstMs default 1000, onRefusalNotice hook, and injectable raf and timer schedulers for tests.
Depends only on inputPort.js for INPUT_LIMITS, INPUT_SCHEMA, byte length, refusal codes and isValidInputEvent. Mirrors host preload ContractError shape with name, code and code-prefixed message.

Single sibling import frameMap for contain mapping. Facade is window.metaviewer input with send plus optional onResult; method-style facades keep receiver. Missing send means unavailable port with same closed outcomes.
Unknown refuse codes fail fast at creation rather than at send, catching typoed test configs. Dynamic refusal returning unknown degrades to SCHEMA, preserving closed refusal set on the wire.

Stale input before READ switch, blur, unmount, stream change or control loss is never sent nor replayed; wheel remainder resets on stream change. send and queue clone events so caller mutation across await cannot reach facade.

ui/src/multislot hosts one capsule live surface with its attached shell terminal on the kit multishell. MultislotHost.vue owns MetaViewer bindings: provider menu, READ/WRITE lease, copy capsule id, facade-to-registry pump, placement, height, launch and typed refusals. multislotAttach.js binds one terminal facade to one kit registry with no DOM, enforcing attach order, byte and sequence validation, credit, lease-off and dispose. multislotCopy.js performs copy-capsule-id writes via injected, transport and ambient clipboard with grammar and identity gating, never throwing. multislotInputGate.js gates keystrokes at lease and writer, builds closed fold, hide, show, float, move and tab intents, and validates placement index, height, activity and state chip. multislotProviders.js adapts host entries and reference listings to kit menus, validates launch requests, parses custom launches, gates session counts, resolves defaults and maps errors. Interaction: host drives facade, pump and registry lifecycle; input gate enforces READ/WRITE; providers gate launch; attach pumps frames to registry; copy projects availability. Offers controlled props and events, attach, close, lease and dispose ops, copy availability, and menu and validation helpers. Needs kit multishell, stream registry, terminal facade and broker, capsule-id validator, copytext grammar, authority intent builder, and clipboard and transport ends.

What the operator sees is disabled buttons with reasons, typed refusal or outcome rows with dismiss controls, a starting-session pending row, state chip labels, and placement reason text; raw broker text never appears.
What the tester sees after a corrupt stream or exit is a dead session view with a failed or exited notice downstream, rather than frozen output or a crash.
What the operator sees is a disabled copy control with an unavailability reason or a copied confirmation; clipboard failures never surface raw errors or host text.
What the operator sees in READ mode is silent keystroke drops with no terminal effect; bad placement or height choices surface as typed refusal rows rather than misplaced slots.
Operator sees Maximum 8 AI slot sessions reached across capsules. Close a session to open another when the global cap is hit, instead of a raw broker error row.

Session limit, unavailable command, rejected arguments, missing broker, and attach failures project typed refusal rows with dismiss and emit launch-refused; cleanup closes the opened broker session best-effort.

A sequence gap or malformed frame marks the session non-live, releases the view, best-effort closes the broker session, and notifies failed; no raw throw escapes and no bytes are invented. Exit events for live tracked sessions mark non-live, release the view, and notify exited; unknown or already dead sessions are ignored.
Lost surface, invalid identity, off-grammar text, missing clipboard path, and write refusal each return unavailable with distinct reasons; host invalid-text refusals preserve their typed code.
Gated writes read live mode per call, so a mode switch applies to the next keystroke; dropped writes return the typed refusal without touching the facade.

Placement index parsing admits only bounded digit strings or integers in range and throws a typed placement error otherwise; unsupported height presets return null so callers project the typed height refusal, with non-finite inputs falling back to clamped height.

Unknown or empty entryId yields ERR_LAUNCH_ENTRY_UNKNOWN with Unknown launch entry; unknown or empty command yields ERR_LAUNCH_COMMAND_UNAVAILABLE; bad args yield ERR_LAUNCH_ARGV_REJECTED with Launch arguments rejected.

Lost or capsule_gone surface gives SURFACE_LOST; hidden slot gives LAYOUT_ILLEGAL_TRANSITION; in-flight launch gives LAUNCH_BUSY; invalid counts or count at ceiling gives SESSION_LIMIT. When no provider or shell command is advertised the default resolves to COMMAND_UNAVAILABLE with Launch unavailable, disabling the header action.

Receives controlled presentation props for mode, fold, float, visibility, placement, height, broker, binding, providers, and clipboard; emits intent, mode and height updates plus session, attach, stop, replay, target, and paste events.
Exposes attach, close, lease sync, id listing, and dispose operations; attach rejects duplicates and invalid shape, close on unknown ids is a false no-op.
Synchronous availability probe checks lost surface first, then injected clipboard shape, then transport copy function, then ambient clipboard, so the host can disable before any attempt.

Input is unknown hostEntries, undefined means empty, or reference-only listing rows plus capability objects; output is a frozen menu array starting with the system shell entry followed by normalized provider entries with empty frozen argv, excluding available-false rows.

Validates one kit launch-request payload against advertised broker commands and rendered menu ids, returning ok with frozen launch or ok false with a typed refusal without spawning; custom executable plus free-form argument text uses whitespace-split grammar with no quoting or shell evaluation.

Gate checks capsule slot launch from session counts, launching flag, hidden flag and surface state using Math.max of local and global counts when a cross-capsule total is supplied; maps broker or transport open errors onto typed refusals with SESSION_LIMIT becoming the designed limit refusal; resolves the + AI slot default to the first admitted provider whose command is advertised else the advertised system shell, revalidated through validateLaunchRequest.

Binding prop drives facade creation, capability fetch, attach, pump creation, and session registration; rebind or unmount disposes pumps and facades, clears writers and lists, and resets attachment and activity. Broker opens without a binding build a transport-backed pump sharing the registry and visible list; replacing the transport disposes the lazy stack and sheds only sessions the old transport owned.

Launch validates the request against advertised commands and menu ids, routes shell versus provider entries, refuses custom arguments as typed rows, and requires an opener plus a pump before opening with fixed console size. Direct host provider data wins; without it the slot lists through the fixed transport API, and malformed data or listing failures fall back to a shell-only menu with a typed provider refusal.

Preset select, stepper, and splitter resize clamp height within bounds; hidden or lost surface refuses with a show-first message, and accepted changes update local state and emit height updates. Fold and placement intents emit host-bound bodies, half-view toggles stay local, close intents are dropped, WRITE requests under agent control are ignored, and session select plus close route to the owning pump before emitting.
Valid frames flow to the registry as output chunks spanning prior to current sequence with byte-array data, then local sequence and byte totals advance and a cumulative credit returns to the facade.
Copy resolves live surface state, validates target text, prefers injected clipboard over transport copy text over ambient clipboard, then writes and projects copied or typed unavailable outcomes.

Slot identity prefixes the capsule id with the kit slot prefix pinned against the kit root ids; fold intents carry that identity through the shared authority builder. Measured float geometry rounds to integer pixels; unmeasurable boxes yield null so callers refuse instead of fabricating geometry.

Listing validation is strict: non-array inputs, malformed ids, labels, hints, reserved ids, duplicates, excess rows and malformed capability objects throw TypeError or RangeError instead of rendering a partial menu.

Builds closed hide, show, float, move, and tab intents with slot identity, group, index, and measured geometry; blank fields keep current placement and invalid input projects a typed placement refusal. Placement builders emit closed bodies that never touch the wire; presentation stays authoritative until echoed acknowledgement.

Copy writes the capsule or slot identity through injected clipboard, transport copy text, or ambient clipboard; lost surface, missing path, invalid or off-grammar identity disable the control with a reason and never throw. Both capsule and slot targets require a valid capsule id and host copytext grammar match, with slot text prefixing the validated id, and grammar admits only strings matching the shared host copytext expression.

Requires a facade with data and exit subscriptions, a registry with session creation and chunk writing, a valid capsule id, and a mode getter; otherwise throws a typed constructor error. Every terminal outcome turns the control lease off and best-effort disposes and forgets the registry view; lease teardown never masks the authoritative failed or exited state.
Only WRITE yields a control lease; every other value normalizes to READ, and the lease helper feeds the kit lease prop directly.

Height helpers clamp expanded height within floor and ceiling, admit only canonical presets, step by the fixed increment, and project the folded rail height when folded. Activity states normalize to the closed kit set with unknown fallback; the state chip derives only from surface, activity, attachment, and session count, with lost surface forcing capsule-gone error tone.

Launch commit allows at most 32 args, each at most 4096 UTF-8 bytes measured by TextEncoder; over-long, non-string or NUL-containing args are refused, mirroring the kit launch guard. Global ceiling is 8 concurrent AI slot sessions across capsules; overflow renders the designed SESSION_LIMIT_MESSAGE naming closing a session as the remedy.

READ mode never delivers operator keystrokes through both the kit lease and the gated writer, with unknown modes failing closed; the veil press guard only prevents default on the veil and leaves terminal and controls untouched.
Replay payloads must be byte arrays within the replay bound and frames within the frame bound; sequence, length coherence, and byte shape are checked before the registry accepts output.

Projected states stay within the closed set aligned with the kit identity plate, with unknown states failing closed to unavailable. Dock target and placement index bounds are shared constants; out-of-range group or index values reject client-side before anything is sent.
Renderer never invents provider identities, labels or argv and never resolves executables; listing rows carry empty argv and the id custom is reserved for the kit custom-executable dialog commit.
At depth 1 the operator sees a display-only wall without their own capsule row; at unknown depth they see the full top-level wall with no error message.
Operator sees Network configuration unavailable or the typed NET_OPEN_PREREQ and NET_PROXIED_UNSUPPORTED alerts inside the dialog; a saved change reports Saved. Applies on the next start.
Condition unreadable or invalid depth; result is silent top-level mode with known false; no error text reaches the wall on any path.

Missing identity reports no admitted profile identity; missing egress method reports no operator network channel; invalid allowlist reports the local problem; host refusal sets typed text via refusalText and NET_OPEN_PREREQ opens the confirm path.
Transport throw during get or set shows Network configuration request failed before the adapter answered and saves nothing; busy clears only for the latest generation.
Null, undefined and empty string parse to top depth 0; safe integers outside 0-1 give NESTED_DEPTH, other types and malformed strings give NESTED_DEPTH_MALFORMED.
Returns true only for depth exactly 1; every other value including 0 and unknown is top-level behavior.
Reads depth and self capsule id through the injected host; throwing host, null depth or unparsable depth resolves to depth 0 with known false and never throws or surfaces host text.
In-memory host double exposes getNestedDepth and getSelfCapsuleId from initial depth and selfCapsuleId for tests and fixtures.

Get resets mode, domains, net mode, reason and stored state then calls egress.get with identity; set builds a versioned egress record and optionally confirms open, guarded by a generation counter against stale responses.
Removes rows whose id or surfaceId equals the self capsule id; non-array input yields empty list and missing self id returns a copy unchanged, preserving non-object rows.
Mode buttons only act when loaded and idle; any edit of mode or domains clears the confirm-open flag and saved state until the next successful set.
Only depths 0 and 1 are accepted as number or bare digit string; leading zeros, depth 2 and above, and non-digit strings are refused, never clamped.
Pure renderer helpers adapt the wall to nested display-only mode at depth 1: filter the self capsule from rows and suppress error text; the main-side retail gate remains the enforcement point.
Per-capsule network dialog loads and saves the egress record for the next start through the operator host egress channel, with open versus allowlisted modes and typed refusal copy.
Display-only true filters the self capsule and reports displayOnly true; any other mode returns rows untouched with displayOnly false.
Loaded tracks a completed get; saved marks a successful set; confirmOpen marks NET_OPEN_PREREQ needing explicit confirm for a future start, with save disabled until loaded.

Depends on injected host egress get and set, operatorHost default, and networkCopy helpers for allowlist parsing, problem text, channel check and refusal copy; per-capsule identity selects the record.
Confirming open when prerequisites are missing records the choice for a future start only; nothing changes until the capsule restarts with the required image and pin.

ui/src/qa provides QA anchor snapshotting for visible interactive UI via anchorCollector.js. collectQaAnchors queries data-semantic-anchor descendants plus root, validates anchor grammar, derives interactive roles, filters private subtrees, value controls, hidden and off-viewport elements, computes accessible names and rounded rects, and emits a closed bounded qa_anchors/v1 snapshot. installQaAnchorReporter adds opt-in debounced reporting on mutations, resize, scroll, transitions and animation end. Offers sorted rows with anchor, role, name and rect for test automation; needs DOM with data-semantic-anchor attributes, window/document facade, scheduler/clock and QA transport.
Missing facade returns a no-op before touching window, document or scheduler; QA transport rejections are swallowed and host-closing throws are caught so the renderer is undisturbed.
Walks ancestors checking hidden, inert, aria-hidden and computed display, visibility, content-visibility and opacity; any match hides the element.
Reads label text from text nodes and element children only, skipping private subtrees, value controls and, unless referenced, invisible elements; never reads form values.
Derives the interactive role from explicit role or local name and input type; hidden inputs and non-href anchors yield no role and are skipped.
Normalizes whitespace, replaces lone surrogates with the replacement character, and truncates at code-point boundaries within the 128 UTF-16 length wire limit.
Prefers aria-labelledby references outside private subtrees, then aria-label, option label, associated labels, static button values and alt text, falling back to visible label text.
Rect carries rounded x, y, w and h; elements with non-finite geometry, zero size or fully outside the viewport are excluded from the snapshot.
Snapshot shape is schema qa_anchors/v1 with monotonic seq and rows; empty wire overhead plus per-row bytes drive the size trim.
Queries data-semantic-anchor descendants plus the root itself, filters by anchor grammar, role, privacy, value ancestry, visibility and finite on-viewport rect, then sorts by y, x and anchor.
Anchor grammar v2: 1-6 slash-joined segments, each alnum-led up to 64 chars, 200 chars total, no empty, dot, dotdot, leading or trailing slash.
Admitted roles are a fixed set of 17 widget roles; explicit role attributes select the first admitted token, native button, link, input, select, option, textarea and summary map to their roles.

Never descends into canvas, iframe, object, embed, script, style, terminal, surface, creative frames or editable payloads; value controls and their ancestors exclude text, labels and values from names.
Collects a closed bounded snapshot of visible interactive elements carrying data-semantic-anchor, with role, accessible name and rounded rect, without observers or DOM changes.
Rows cap at 512 entries and total payload at 64 KiB by dropping trailing rows; rects are integer-rounded and rows with non-positive size are dropped.
Opt-in reporter settles on mutations, resize, scroll, transition and animation end; first-pending time pins a 1000 ms maximum-wait ceiling while minimum spacing enforces 500 ms between reports.
Debounce uses an injected or performance clock with generation-free timer rescheduling; a clock jump before minimum spacing defers without dropping the burst, and dispose clears timers and observers.
Private payload text and live control values must never enter names; aria-labelledby targets inside private subtrees are filtered before reading.

ui/src/recording is the RAM record-for-AI capture UI. MvRecordingPanel.vue is the panel with record toggle, screenshot button, fps ceiling, manifest rows and sealed screenshots section, bound to the host capture store or legacy props and intents. recordingModel.js is the RAM-first adapter building record, screenshot and export gates, typed refusals, labels, DOM ids and anchors; host owns toggle, screenshot, export and refresh sinks. recordingClock.js plus useRecordingElapsed.js interpolate sparse host elapsedMs into a ticking mm:ss readout with testable clocks, freezing outside recording. RecordingBadge.vue plus recordingBadge.js render the tile badge Idle, Starting, Stopping, Sealed or Recording mm:ss with refusal reason. Offers gated record, screenshot, export and select actions with stable ids and anchors; needs host captureState.bySurface, advertised destination, kit intent builders, wall tileCapture helpers and Vue reactivity.
Operator sees a refused click as explicit status text instead of a dead button, and a sealing start as a sealed confirmation line; empty manifests show No recordings yet.
Disabled controls expose Recording is unavailable, Recording is starting or stopping, or the fps range message through title and unavailable-reason attributes.
Operator sees Idle, Starting, Stopping, Sealed, or ticking Recording mm:ss, with refusal or failure reason appended after a dash when a capture action was refused or failed.

User sees Recording failed on rows whose phase is error; host diagnostics never render. Capture refusal RECORDING_FAILED_CODE maps to The recording failed on the host and stopped. Start a new one. Empty code renders nothing.

Record, stop and screenshot refusals show fixed lines for SURFACE_UNKNOWN, ALREADY_RECORDING, NOT_RECORDING, CAPTURE_UNAVAILABLE, NESTED_DISPLAY_ONLY, LIMIT, BUDGET_EXCEEDED, POLICY. Unknown non-empty codes show Capture failed.
Empty manifest shows No recordings yet. Unreadable elapsed renders --:--, never a fabricated zero; unreadable counts render Unknown; spent TTL renders Expired. Store chip shows RAM or Unknown.

User sees a live MM:SS style elapsed that advances smoothly during recording and freezes or clears when stopping, sealing, or erroring. A stuck or runaway tick would point to start or stop timer logic here.
Invalid fps disables the record start with Frame rate must be a whole number; the fps field locks while disabled, held, recording or busy.
Export is skipped when already exporting or exported, when the row gate or destination disallows it, or when no store export action exists; unbound exports emit an export intent.

Refusal copy is fixed literals: No export destination advertised by the host, Only sealed recordings can be exported, destination unavailable, already exported, limit reached, recording gone. Raw codes ride a data attribute only, never user-facing.
When host elapsed is unreadable the computed resolves to null and the UI shows its placeholder rather than a fabricated zero. A missing scope simply skips disposal registration without throwing.
Bound store supplies phase, elapsed, screenshot state and manifest rows; unbound mounts fall back to legacy phase, elapsedSeconds, screenshotState and recordings props.
Live readout interpolates from the last host elapsedMs with an injected testable clock while recording; unbound mounts show elapsedSeconds directly.
Bound store last refusal code per capsule renders as typed status text with data-error-code; sealed confirmation shows only when no refusal is present.
Bound toggle calls store toggleRecord with maxFps only on a valid-fps start, showing sealed text on ok; unbound toggle emits a record AI intent; disabled guards block both.
Bound screenshots call store screenshot; unbound clicks emit a screenshot intent; pending state disables the button with Screenshot capture is pending.
Row select emits a recording-select intent only when enabled and the row id is valid, resolving the capsule from the row or the active capsule.
Bound export sets exporting synchronously to close the double-invoke race, calls store exportCapture, and renders exported only for ok receipts with a 64 hex digest, else typed refusal copy.
Accepts only finite non-negative numbers as host elapsed; all other values are treated as unknown.

Returns base plus non-negative local delta, or null without an anchor; rejects non-finite now values. Builds a frozen anchor from a host sample; jitter-range lag keeps the shown value, larger jumps adopt the host value, unusable host or time input yields null. While recording returns the interpolated anchor value; otherwise returns the last host elapsedMs or null when unknown.
Formats milliseconds floored to whole seconds as mm:ss, or --:-- when the input is not valid host elapsed.
Maps recording to Recording mm:ss, starting, stopping, sealed and other phases to fixed words, appending the typed refusal reason when present.
Reads the surface entry for the capsule id and derives its phase through the wall tileCapture helpers.

Panel, refusal, toggle, screenshot, phase, store, fps, capture-status, row, select, export, gate and status controls each expose a stable DOM id builder and a semantic anchor builder derived from the encoded capsule or recording id.

Entry is useRecordingElapsed(source, getClock): source returns phase and host elapsedMs; getClock is read once and supplies now, setInterval, clearInterval, tickMs. Returns a computed elapsed in ms, null when unknown.
Manifest rows and shots read from the bound store per capsule; mount, capsule switch and store swap relist only when listable and no active-capsule row exists, coalesced by the store.

Recording rows disambiguate duplicate or malformed ids to unknown-N placeholders, compute per-row export gates, and key export status by display row id cleared on store or capsule change. Sealed screenshots list in their own section for visibility and export only; ids stay unique against recording rows and invalid rows key status by disambiguated display id.
Live elapsed interpolates from entry elapsedMs with an injected testable clock; last code string resolves to refusal text; copy drives text, title and conditional error code.

captureEntryFor reads only captureState.bySurface for a surface id, accepting a plain object or Map. Hostile keys __proto__, constructor, prototype return null. Unknown or hostile shapes return null without throwing; panels fail closed to idle.

captureRowsFor keeps kind recording rows for one surface with duration_ms mapped to elapsedSeconds; captureShotsFor keeps kind shot rows only when sealed true and phase sealed, tagged kind shot. Bad shapes yield frozen empty lists.

Anchor helpers anchorElapsed and displayElapsedMs come from recordingClock.js. Anchor plus tick drive the computed display value; host elapsedMs re-anchors on each recording sample while tick advances locally between events.
Optional frame-rate ceiling is a whole number within the documented range; empty uses host default and invalid blocks only start, never stop.
Display tick is 1000 ms; host samples lagging the interpolated value by at most 1000 ms hold instead of rewinding; unknown elapsed shows --:-- never zero.

A destination is usable only as a non-empty string equal to its trim, with no surrounding whitespace. Renderer never invents one. Empty, padded, or non-string values count as absent and force refusal paths.

Panel gate recordToDiskGate checks destination first, then sealed phase. Returns frozen allowed/code/reason. Missing destination yields ERR_EXPORT_WITHOUT_DESTINATION; unsealed phase yields ERR_EXPORT_UNSEALED_RECORDING; only sealed with destination allows. Panel refusal panelDiskRefusalFor returns null when no refusal applies. An explicit non-empty unavailableReason wins over the destination check with ERR_RECORDING_UNAVAILABLE. Otherwise missing destination yields the without-destination refusal.

Per-row gate precedence is unavailable reason, then unsealed phase, then missing destination, then ready. Returns frozen disabled/reason/gate/gateLabel with gates unavailable, sealed-required, destination-required, ready. Export refusal codes are closed: DESTINATION_UNSET, CAPTURE_UNKNOWN, NOT_SEALED, DESTINATION_UNAVAILABLE, DESTINATION_EXISTS, LIMIT, NESTED_DISPLAY_ONLY, CAPTURE_UNAVAILABLE. Unknown codes normalize to CAPTURE_UNAVAILABLE with generic Recording is unavailable copy.
Export receipt never shows a path: receipt is id, bytes and digest. Valid 64-hex sha256 yields Exported plus first 8 hex chars; anything else yields bare Exported. Invalid digest shows no prefix.

Frame-rate field: empty means use host default; plain 1-3 digit integer within 1..60 is ok; anything else is invalid and never reaches host. Hint states frames record up to source rate and a higher choice adds no frames.

resolveClock completes a partial clock: now defaults to performance.now, timers to platform setInterval and clearInterval, tickMs to MV_ELAPSED_TICK_MS when not a positive number. Null or non-object clock input yields full defaults.

DOM segments preserve canonical lowercase-dash ids; anything else encodes every UTF-16 unit as encoded-XXXX-end, and the encoded- prefix itself is encoded to avoid collision. Labels drop strings with newlines, tabs, or ERR_ and enforce a strict alphanumeric pattern.

ui/src/settings owns the mv settings stack: scheme mv-light/mv-dark, density compact/comfortable, live wall fps 3/30/60 with measured actual readout, recording fps 1..60, plus hidden live-session limit. MvSettingsPanel.vue renders the panel, gates input on ready/verified/saving/store, debounces persistence leading-edge with trailing last-wins merge, live-applies scheme, meters actual fps from framesPort notices, and shows typed refusals. settingsModel.js is the pure zero-import core: closed four-key decode/encode with strict unknown-key and float-lexeme refusal, per-value stored fallback, host store, debounced runner, wall meter, refusal literals, normalizers, and stable DOM ids/anchors. settingsHost.js adapts the injected preload host to HostSettingsPort with per-method fallback to kit Storage and in-memory fixture. Offers validated load/save, live scheme apply, fps readout, and refusal mapping. Needs injected settingsHost, Storage, framesPort.subscribeFrames, frameClock/frameTimer, capsule-ui-kit scheme/storage helpers, and parent density/wall application.

User sees radios disabled until ready and verified, a density readout, a wall fps line like 30 requested with actual or placeholder, and a typed refusal row with fixed copy on save or apply failure. Malformed stored text silently uses defaults.

Hidden live sessions field accepts non-negative whole numbers; blank or invalid input shows Enter a non-negative whole number. The previous limit is still active. Valid input updates the injected hiddenSessionSettings.
User with no preload sees scheme and density restored from local preferences and wall/recording at defaults. A failed local write surfaces as Settings could not be saved on the host downstream.

User sees Stored settings are unreadable; defaults are in use when stored text is bad, Settings host is unavailable when wiring fails, and save or apply lines on write failure. Bad stored values silently keep valid fields.
Readout formats as N requested, X.X actual with one decimal, or placeholder -- when the window is empty. Unknown requested values normalize to the default preset, never an error.

Load failure falls back to defaults and live-applies them. Decode failures stay silent with defaults; transport or host failures render a typed refusal via settingsRefusalFor. Apply failure yields ERR_SETTINGS_APPLY_FAILED refusal.

Failed live restoration clears the verified selection and gates changes until reload. Save failure sets a typed refusal and keeps UI state. Rollback save failure never replaces the authoritative apply refusal.

Invalid save payload throws the decoded coded error; null storage or failed write throws ERR_SETTINGS_SAVE_FAILED. Fixture host records text in memory with load/save call logging and always resolves true on save.

Stored-text failures malformed, unknown key, scheme, density, wall or recording fps fall back silently to defaults. Transport and host failures stay loud as typed refusals. Host text never reaches the screen.

Refusals map to fixed literals: host unavailable, stored settings unreadable with defaults in use, scheme could not be applied, could not be saved. Unknown codes collapse to save-failed. Raw error text is never shown.

Inputs are settingsHost, optional framesPort.subscribeFrames, frameClock.now, frameTimer setTimeout/clearTimeout, plus density v-model. Emits scheme-change when the applied scheme changes. Parent applies density; panel only persists and mirrors it.

Entry is createSettingsHostImpl(host, storage, fixtureScheme): partial host plus Storage plus optional fixture scheme. Returns loadSettings/saveSettings pair. Static decodeStoredSettings rides on the factory for the boot parser.

createHostSettingsStore validates the host eagerly, requiring both loadSettings and saveSettings. Load of null resolves defaults; non-string storage throws malformed; unknown-key or float-lexeme storage throws so callers use full defaults.
Stable DOM ids and semantic anchors cover the panel, scheme, density, wall fps, recording fps, actual readout, and refusal rows plus per-option radios, for agent_lane/v1 selection and testing.

loadHost builds a host store, awaits load, then live-applies the scheme before adopting values. Generation counter drops obsolete completions after host replacement or unmount so a stale load cannot change the theme.
Actual wall fps comes from a sliding-window meter over frame_ref.ts_ns notices on framesPort. Each notice pushes the timestamp, updates the readout, and re-arms a single decay timer one window out.

Fallback load normalizes legacy light/dark to mv-light/mv-dark, validates density, and encodes a full four-key object. Fallback save decodes the JSON, then writes only the scheme key, failing when storage is null or the write fails.

parseSettingsText captures raw fps number lexemes via the JSON.parse reviver context source, counting only top-level holder entries. Nested objects cannot poison the reading and string values cannot fool it. Missing source refuses strictly.

Wall fps meter admits only non-negative safe-integer frame_ref.ts_ns values, records arrival clocks, prunes outside MV_WALL_FPS_WINDOW_MS 2000, and reads arrivals per second or null when empty. msUntilEmpty schedules decay past the inclusive edge.

persistSettings runs only when ready, liveVerified, not saving, and store present. It skips non-objects and values equal to current settings. Successful save live-applies the scheme first; apply failure rolls back via a second save and clears verification.

selectSettings merges each patch onto the queued trailing value so cross-field bursts keep every last value. Only a request equal to both applied and pending values is a no-op. Saves during saving, unverified, or replaced host are dropped.

Recording fps field strictly parses trimmed integer strings, clamps to 1..60, and schedules persistence. Empty or non-integer input silently reverts the field to the current value with no save and no visible error.

Fallback is per-method: absent loadSettings reads kit scheme and density preferences and synthesizes wall and recording defaults; absent saveSettings validates then writes scheme only. A host rejection never triggers fallback.

decodeMvSettings accepts an object or JSON text in canonical keys only. Missing keys take defaults. Unknown keys, unknown scheme, density or fps, malformed text, and float or exponent fps lexemes like 30.0 or 3e1 refuse with coded errors.

decodeStoredSettings refuses the whole payload on unknown keys and float fps lexemes so store and boot fall back to full defaults. Invalid values of known keys fall back per value, so a valid scheme survives an invalid density and vice versa.

encodeMvSettings strict-encodes only valid settings to canonical JSON and throws the coded decode error otherwise. Host store save then requires an exact true acknowledgement or raises ERR_SETTINGS_SAVE_FAILED.

Normalizers return the value when known else a fallback, defaulting to primary scheme, compact density, wall 30, recording 3. Recording fallback itself validates so an invalid fallback cannot leak through.

Settings objects must carry string scheme/density and numeric wallFps/recordingFps. Equality compares all four fields; non-objects are never equal. Guards prevent persisting partial or unchanged payloads.

Both directions run through the closed four-key definition, so saves validate every field and loads fall back per field. Fallback persists exactly one storage key per the host feature-detection contract.

Closed sets are schemes mv-light/mv-dark, densities compact/comfortable, wall presets 3/30/60, recording integers 1..60. Defaults are mv-light, compact, wall 30, recording 3. Encoded saves carry exactly four keys in canonical order.

Persistence is leading-edge debounced over MV_SETTINGS_SAVE_WINDOW_MS: first change saves immediately, bursts collapse to one trailing last-wins write. Trailing continuations re-check guards so replaced hosts and in-flight saves drop safely.

createDebouncedRunner runs the first call synchronously, collapses within-window calls to one trailing last-value call, and exposes cancel, pending and pendingValue. Cancel drops the trailing call on unmount or host replacement.

At most one fps decay timeout is ever pending. The decay callback re-reads the meter and re-arms for the remaining window when a sample is still inside, so a stale rate never lingers. Teardown never throws.
Frames subscription holds a single stop function; resubscribe and unmount call it defensively. Missing or throwing subscribeFrames leaves the panel running with a placeholder actual readout.
Save burst window is 150 ms: first change writes immediately plus at most one trailing write. Fps window is 2000 ms. Both bound host writes and memory; encoded payloads are fixed-shape and tiny.

Live theme goes through capsule-ui-kit setKitScheme inside applyLive, which returns false instead of throwing. Density application and wall cadence belong to parent and host; panel only saves the request.
Depends on capsule-ui-kit SettingsModel readStoredSetting, writeStoredSetting, SETTINGS_STORAGE_KEYS and on local settingsModel decode, encode, density helpers. No direct localStorage access.

Fallback saves only the scheme key, so density, wall and recording choices made while the host is absent are lost on reload. Mixed host with only one method splits persistence across host and Storage.

A fps number that parses as an integer but was written with a fraction or exponent refuses the whole load. Editors that serialize 30 as 30.0 therefore reset all settings to defaults rather than keeping the scheme.

ui/src/surfaces renders wall tiles for live capsules. RoleSurface.vue owns one native role view via metaviewerRoles, syncing tile geometry, scroll and wall clips, floating occluders and modal state into mount/resize/visibility/raise, retaining hidden sessions instead of revoking on transient occlusion. SurfaceCanvas.vue hosts one canvas tile via tileScheduler plus frame, display and input port routers, keeping pixel bytes out of reactivity, retaining last witness across generation gaps, mapping input through frame coordinates, and showing frozen, lost, connecting and FPS/capture states with click echo. tileScheduler.js is the fair newest-only RGB scheduler with mailbox, coordinated tick, present-handle-only draw, leases, frozen budgets, eligibility and tombstoned destroys. frameTile.js bridges a brokered port to the scheduler with ack on release. fpsMeter.js meters painted rate and capture duration over a sliding window. hiddenSessions.js caps retained hidden native sessions. overlayCoordinator.js counts overlay owners to mirror modal state while excluding modeless floats and nav menus. pointerEcho.js shows a transient click dot. presentationServices.js installs pool, coordinator and persisted limit. Offers tiled live paint, gated input, visibility accounting; needs scheduler, routers, metaviewer host and preferences.

User sees Connecting... before mount or when connecting, Reconnecting... when reconnecting after a prior connect, Human capsule or Read-only watch when live, Recording paused (size limit) badge, or error text with a Reopen button that clears error and retries sync().

User sees Connecting to surface when live is claimed without a handle, Waiting for surface for empty, Lost plus No frames were presented without a frame, or Lost plus Showing the last frame with frozen bitmap when a witness exists.

Footer shows FPS: count and CAP: ms, or em dash placeholder when the window is empty or capture is absent; a stall timer re-flushes to placeholder once the newest paint ages past the window. Text updates never cost frames.
Consumer sees fpsText/captureText as numbers or em dash; after a stall longer than the window both read placeholder, and capture alone arriving cannot revive FPS text without a paint.

Operator sees a dot at the click for up to one second; it vanishes early when the repainted frame answers the click, or immediately on blur/control loss/READ/surface change via clear(gate). Letterbox clicks never draw.

User-visible words come from accessible names such as Live surface, Surface connecting, Surface lost, No surface, Capsule input, and Capsule lost: showing the last frame, plus the witness strip READ-ONLY ISOLATED EXECUTION and shortened digest head-ellipsis-tail. A failed tile shows black or frozen last frame with the Lost badge.

When hidden, folded, context-lost, over budget, or mailbox-empty, immediate present and tick return HIDDEN_SURFACE, FOLDED_DISPLAY_DISABLED, CONTEXT_LOST, BUDGET_EXHAUSTED, or EMPTY_MAILBOX with disqualifiers. The wall then shows no new pixels; instrumentation exposes eligible, box, pending and presented generations, and counters.

If status.ok===false throw XPRA_REFUSED; if view.state error throw view.code; if visibility/resize/mount reply !ok throw reply.code. Catch sets error.message or XPRA_REFUSED and awaits revoke(), which closes host view and resets mounted/signature/viewState.

lifecycle() blocks while busy, sets progress Switching to... or Stopping capsule..., awaits revoke(), emits lifecycle with completion promise for the persistent parent, then awaits it; !ok throws code into error. Reveal emits before stopped because pane close can unmount this component and suppress later emits.

subtractRoleOccluders() returns hidden with zero width when occluders exceed 64, when split pieces exceed 256 or vanish, or when surviving area differs from bounding box (native views paint one rectangle only, so L/T/R/B splits must exactly tile).
registerSurface failure throws Error(reason). Port onRevoke destroys the scheduler surface. close() revokes with SHUTDOWN, destroys scheduler, and resolves all pending leases as SURFACE_DESTROYED.

Over-limit eviction deletes oldest hidden entry then calls its release callback, which the caller wires to revoke and resource-release UI. Visible entries never evict; remove() drops without releasing.

Submit refusal always releases the candidate lease once as REFUSED, HIDDEN, CONTEXT_LOST, or SUPERSEDED for displaced mailboxes. Stale generation, binding mismatch, folded display, expired or missing lease, RGB shape mismatch, over-budget bytes, and hidden state each return their closed reason; folded advances the admissible floor.

Tick drops ineligible mailboxes with HIDDEN drain, and stale or expired candidates with REFUSED drain plus rejectedStaleFrames count. Over-budget candidates defer with budgetDeferrals and preserve priority via retry cursor. A present with no successful draw witness retires its handle, releases REFUSED, and retains canvas-less frames as pendingPaint.

Present outside a coordinated turn refuses INVALID_BINDING. Unknown handles refuse unknown-handle, foreign handles refuse SURFACE_MISMATCH, retired or non-current handles refuse STALE_FRAME_GENERATION. Missing canvas or failed 2d context refuses without advancing lastPresentedFrameGen.

Operator entries are the tile menu (Switch mode, Mark as logged in, Watch read-only, Move desktop, Stop, Take control), the Reopen button after error, and the reconnect button after resource release; all funnel into lifecycle(), confirmLogin(), sync() or revoke().

Geometry entries are mount status fetch, 100 ms sync timer, window pointermove/resize listeners, capture-phase scroll listeners on window/document/ancestors/shell-wall, and a MutationObserver on body data-mv-modal; each calls sync().

Human input enters only when inputEnabled plus available inputPort plus canvas focus plus not lost. Key/click/scroll map through frameMap and queue on the port with streamId; Escape blurs and emits canvas-escape and is never forwarded.

submitFrame(frame) is the only frame ingress. It validates binding, generation floors, lease liveness, packed RGB shape, aggregate byte cap and eligibility, then replaces the single mailbox slot newest-wins. It never draws and emits SUPERSEDED for the displaced slot.

runTick([targetSurfaceId]) executes one coordinated fair tick over a snapshot of surfaceOrder. It checks eligibility, lease expiry, staleness and frozen aggregate draws plus bytes plus present-ms, presents at most budget, and freezes the result record.

presentHandle({surfaceId,handle}) is the only draw path. It is valid only while insideTurn is true, only for the owning live surface, only for the current presented handle, and only with a canvas attached. Unknown, foreign, retired or mismatched handles refuse closed.

sync() reads root.getBoundingClientRect(), collects scroll ancestors and wall viewport, computes baseClip via clipRoleBounds(), subtracts floating occluders, then calls api.mount/resize/visibility/raise with the surviving rectangle.

floatingPresentation() enumerates .dv-resize-container floats with nonzero rect and visible style, walks up to 64 ancestors for max zIndex, maps a dv-render-overlay-float portal to its container at portalZ-1, and returns front flag plus occluder rects above own tile.

Router onRegistered pins delivery identity (surfaceGeneration/epoch) into registeredIdentity; later attaches use that verbatim, never projection generation/epoch props. A new delivery identity drops retained witness and FPS state; re-attach reclaims the scheduler canvas binding.

Client-to-frame mapping uses paint-owned canvas.width/height with letterbox removal, never projection frameWidth/Height props; mapper failure fails closed with null. Canvas intrinsic size is owned by scheduler paint; no reactive width/height binding may clear a painted frame.

onFrame rejects duplicate leaseId with REFUSED, submits to scheduler, records capture witness for admitted or FOLDED_DISPLAY_DISABLED folds, and resolves pending on onReleaseLease outcome; unadmitted non-fold deletes pending and returns REFUSED immediately.

Frame bytes flow as owned tightly packed top-left RGB24 by reference from submitFrame mailbox to presented slot to canvas. convertRgb24ToRgba expands to opaque RGBA; little-endian aligned outputs use one Uint32 store per pixel, otherwise the reference byte loop, bit-identical.

Host contract is globalThis.metaviewerRoles: status(surfaceId) returns role/view.state/view.code/view.recording, plus mount/resize/visibility/raise/close/confirmLogin/switchMode/stop and onFocus. Missing api leaves role agent with no mount and header teleported only when api and role exist.

clipRoleBounds() intersects tile rect with window viewport (innerWidth/Height or override) and every scroll/wall clip, then ceil/floor quantizes; visible requires width>=1 and height>=1, else bounds zeroed. Non-finite inputs yield null rect and skipped clips.

Scheduler contract: attachCanvas({surfaceId,surfaceGeneration,epoch,canvas}) returns ok/token, detachCanvas, getInstrumentation, evictSurface, subscribePresentation. bindToken symbol scopes unbind so wall and multislot tiles sharing surfaceId do not remove each other.
Default limit 4; constructor and setLimit reject non-safe-integer or negative with HIDDEN_SESSION_LIMIT_INVALID. API: update(id,shown,release,isShown?), remove(id), size, limit, setLimit.

API: set(owner,open) adds/removes owner object identity and syncs attribute; count; dispose() clears and syncs. Native popover/details toggles track per-element owners and prune disconnected nodes; SELECT open sets selectOwner until change/focusout/pointer-away/Escape/Enter/Tab.

Budget must be a frozen object with exactly maxDrawsPerTick, maxUploadBytesPerTick, maxPresentMsPerTick, maxWarmResourcesPerSurface, maxDrainSteps. Unknown, missing, or out-of-range limits refuse INVALID_BUDGET; constructor throws on invalid budget.

Limit reads preferences mv.hiddenLiveSessionLimit; absent uses default 4. Malformed stored value throws HIDDEN_SESSION_LIMIT_INVALID. Settings set() validates safe-integer >=0, persists string, and calls pool.setLimit.

Temporary clipping, docking and window visibility must not revoke the authenticated session: when not visible but mounted, sync() calls api.visibility(id,false) and retains the connection instead of revoke(); only wanted()==false or errors revoke.

Painted requires nonempty getClientRects and computed style not hidden/collapse/none, so Dockview inactive tabs with nonempty rects stay session-retained but native-hidden. Modal active is body data-mv-modal attribute/dataset/props; visible requires geometricallyShown and clipped.visible and no modal.

Dockview floats (dialog plus dv-resize-container without aria-modal true) and sidebar nav menus (menu inside aside/nav/navigation) are excluded so modeless floats never hide their own native view and idle nav never occludes everything. Closed popovers are ignored.
